title: Optimal Work Extraction From Finite-time Closed Quantum Dynamics
authors: Shoki Sugimoto, Takahiro Sagawa, And Ryusuke Hamazaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shoki Sugimoto, Takahiro Sagawa, and Ryusuke Hamazaki

Extracting useful work from quantum systems is a fundamental problem in quantum thermodynamics. In scenarios where rapid protocols are desired—whether due to practical constraints or deliberate design choices—a fundamental trade-off between power and efficiency is yet to be established. Here, we inv…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023321] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives fundamental bounds on work extraction from finite-time closed quantum dynamics, revealing a trade-off between power and efficiency.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits of work extraction in quantum systems is crucial for designing efficient quantum engines and protocols, especially when time constraints are present.
method: The authors use optimal control theory and quantum thermodynamic principles to analyze work extraction from closed quantum systems undergoing finite-time unitary evolution.
result: They establish a trade-off relation between the extracted work and the operation time, showing that faster protocols incur higher dissipation and lower efficiency.
conclusion: The results provide fundamental bounds that guide the design of near-optimal work extraction protocols in quantum thermodynamics.

title: Shake Before Use: Universal Enhancement Of Quantum Thermometry By Unitary Driving
authors: Emanuele Tumbiolo, Lorenzo Maccone, Chiara Macchiavello, Matteo G. A. Paris, And Giacomo Guarnieri
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuele Tumbiolo, Lorenzo Maccone, Chiara Macchiavello, Matteo G. A. Paris, and Giacomo Guarnieri

Quantum thermometry aims at determining temperature with ultimate precision in the quantum regime. Standard equilibrium approaches, limited by the quantum Fisher information given by static energy fluctuations, lose sensitivity outside a fixed temperature window. Nonequilibrium strategies have there…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250401] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Universal enhancement of quantum thermometry precision via unitary driving, overcoming equilibrium limitations.
motivation: Standard equilibrium quantum thermometry loses sensitivity outside a fixed temperature window; nonequilibrium strategies can potentially improve precision.
method: The authors propose a universal protocol using unitary driving to enhance the quantum Fisher information for temperature estimation, analyzing both Markovian and non-Markovian regimes.
result: Unitary driving universally increases the precision of quantum thermometry, with significant improvements demonstrated for various probe systems.
conclusion: The work establishes a general framework for nonequilibrium quantum thermometry, showing that driving can overcome static energy fluctuation limits.

title: Heat, Work, And Fluctuations In A Driven Quantum Resonator
authors: Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, And Christian Flindt
abstract:
Author(s): Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, and Christian Flindt

A central building block of a heat engine is the working fluid, which mediates the conversion of heat into work. In nanoscale heat engines, the working fluid can be a quantum system whose behavior and dynamics are nonclassical. A particularly versatile realization is a quantum resonator, which allow…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064151] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies heat, work, and fluctuations in a driven quantum resonator, a model system for nanoscale heat engines.
motivation: Understanding nonclassical behavior of working fluids in quantum heat engines is crucial for developing efficient nanoscale thermodynamic devices.
method: The authors analyze a quantum resonator under periodic driving, using full counting statistics and fluctuation theorems to characterize heat and work distributions.
result: They derive exact expressions for the characteristic functions of heat and work, revealing non-Gaussian fluctuations and quantum signatures in the statistics.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for quantifying thermodynamic performance and fluctuations in driven quantum resonators, relevant for quantum heat engine design.

title: Universal Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation For Quantum $f$ Divergences
authors: Domingos S. P. Salazar
abstract:
Author(s): Domingos S. P. Salazar

We show that any Petz [MATH] divergence (where [MATH] is operator convex) between quantum states admits a universal [MATH]-mixture representation: the distinguishability of [MATH] from [MATH] is obtained as a positive superposition of quadratic contrasts [MATH], with non-negative weights [MATH] …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064150] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a universal thermodynamic uncertainty relation for quantum f-divergences, linking distinguishability to thermodynamic cost.
motivation: To derive a general bound on the distinguishability of quantum states in terms of thermodynamic quantities, extending classical thermodynamic uncertainty relations to the quantum regime.
method: Uses Petz f-divergences and operator convex functions to represent distinguishability as a mixture of quadratic contrasts, then applies the quantum Cramér-Rao bound.
result: A universal inequality relating any Petz f-divergence to the quantum Fisher information and the variance of an observable, providing a thermodynamic uncertainty relation for quantum processes.
conclusion: The result offers a unified framework for thermodynamic precision bounds in quantum systems, with implications for quantum metrology and thermodynamics.

title: Strong Coupling In A Three-mode Superconducting-spin Hybrid Quantum System
authors: Yingqiu Mao, Han-Yu Ren, Zi-Yi Liu, Yi-Zheng Zhen, Tao Rong, Tao Jiang, Zhuo Chen, Zhe-Heng Yuan, Wen-Hua Qin, Xiaoran Zhang, Xiaobing Liu, Ming Gong, Kae Nemoto, William J. Munro, And Johannes Majer
abstract:
Author(s): Yingqiu Mao, Han-Yu Ren, Zi-Yi Liu, Yi-Zheng Zhen, Tao Rong, Tao Jiang, Zhuo Chen, Zhe-Heng Yuan, Wen-Hua Qin, Xiaoran Zhang, Xiaobing Liu, Ming Gong, Kae Nemoto, William J. Munro, and Johannes Majer

We demonstrate strong coupling in a solid-state hybrid quantum system comprising a fixed-frequency coplanar-waveguide resonator, a superconducting transmon qubit, and an ensemble of nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond. Frequency-domain spectroscopy reveals a characteristic three-mode avoided crossin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023343] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates strong coupling in a three-mode hybrid system comprising a superconducting resonator, transmon qubit, and NV center ensemble.
motivation: Hybrid quantum systems combining superconducting circuits with spin ensembles are promising for quantum information processing, but achieving strong coupling in multi-mode configurations is challenging.
method: Frequency-domain spectroscopy is used to observe a three-mode avoided crossing, indicating strong coupling between the resonator, transmon, and NV ensemble.
result: Clear evidence of strong coupling is observed, with characteristic splitting in the transmission spectrum.
conclusion: This work establishes a solid-state platform for coherent interactions between superconducting and spin degrees of freedom, relevant for quantum networking and transduction.

title: Detecting Quantum Noise Of A Solid-state Spin Ensemble With Dispersive Measurement
authors: Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, and Aashish A. Clerk

We theoretically explore protocols for measuring the spin polarization of an ensemble of solid-state spins, with precision at or below the standard quantum limit. Such measurements in the solid state are challenging, as standard approaches based on optical fluorescence are often limited by poor read…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023331] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes dispersive measurement protocols to detect spin polarization of solid-state spin ensembles with precision at or below the standard quantum limit.
motivation: Solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum memories and sensors, but optical fluorescence readout is often inefficient; dispersive measurement offers a non-destructive alternative.
method: The authors theoretically analyze dispersive measurement schemes using cavity or circuit QED techniques, modeling the spin ensemble as a collective spin coupled to a resonator.
result: They show that with optimized parameters, the measurement can achieve sub-SQL sensitivity and extract information about spin polarization and noise.
conclusion: Dispersive measurement is a viable route for high-precision readout of solid-state spin ensembles, enabling applications in quantum sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Stochastic Schrödinger Equations For Quantum Reverse Diffusion
authors: Einar Gabbassov
abstract:
Author(s): Einar Gabbassov

The ensemble-averaged dynamics of open quantum systems are typically irreversible. We show that this irreversibility need not hold at the level of individually monitored quantum trajectories. Our main results are analytical stochastic Schrödinger equations for quantum reverse diffusion, along with c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023329] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives stochastic Schrödinger equations for reverse diffusion in open quantum systems, showing that irreversibility at the ensemble level does not preclude time-reversal at the level of individual quantum trajectories.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic arrow of time in open quantum systems and whether microscopic reversibility can be reconciled with macroscopic irreversibility.
method: Analytical derivation of stochastic Schrödinger equations that describe reverse diffusion processes conditioned on measurement outcomes, using tools from quantum trajectory theory and stochastic calculus.
result: Explicit stochastic differential equations for reverse-time dynamics of monitored quantum systems, demonstrating that individual trajectories can be time-reversible even when the ensemble average is not.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for reverse diffusion in quantum systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics, fluctuation theorems, and quantum control.

title: Experimental Measurement And A Physical Interpretation Of Quantum Shadow Enumerators
authors: Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, And Jens Eisert
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, and Jens Eisert

This article shows that Rains’ quantum shadow enumerators, a powerful tool in quantum error correction, admit a direct physical interpretation in terms of outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements. This connection enables efficient learning protocols for these quantities and is demonstrated experimentally on a trapped-ion quantum device.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023318] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a physical interpretation of quantum shadow enumerators in terms of two-copy Bell measurements and demonstrates their experimental measurement on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
motivation: Quantum shadow enumerators are powerful tools for analyzing quantum error-correcting codes, but they lacked a direct physical interpretation, limiting their experimental accessibility.
method: The authors show that Rains' quantum shadow enumerators correspond to outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements, enabling efficient learning protocols. They implement these measurements on a trapped-ion quantum device.
result: They experimentally extract shadow enumerators for various quantum error-correcting codes, validating the theoretical connection and demonstrating the practicality of the approach.
conclusion: This work bridges a gap between abstract quantum information theory and experimental quantum error correction, providing a new tool for characterizing and benchmarking quantum codes.

title: Steady-state Entanglement Of Spin Qubits Mediated By Nonreciprocal And Chiral Magnons
authors: Martijn Dols, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Victor A. S. V. Bittencourt, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero, Durga B. R. Dasari, And Silvia Viola Kusminskiy
abstract:
Author(s): Martijn Dols, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Victor A. S. V. Bittencourt, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero, Durga B. R. Dasari, and Silvia Viola Kusminskiy

We propose a hybrid quantum system in which a magnet supporting nonreciprocal magnons, chiral magnons, or both mediates the dissipative and unidirectional coupling of spin qubits. By driving the qubits, the steady state of this qubit-qubit coupling scheme becomes the maximally entangled Bell state. …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023310] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid quantum system where nonreciprocal or chiral magnons mediate dissipative coupling of spin qubits to generate steady-state Bell entanglement.
motivation: To achieve deterministic entanglement of spin qubits without fine-tuning, using magnonic systems that provide unidirectional and dissipative coupling.
method: Theoretical model of spin qubits coupled to a magnet supporting nonreciprocal/chiral magnons; driving the qubits leads to a dissipative steady state that is a maximally entangled Bell state.
result: The steady state becomes a Bell state independent of initial conditions, with entanglement fidelity limited only by magnon dissipation and qubit decoherence.
conclusion: This scheme offers a robust route to generate entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, leveraging chiral magnonics for quantum information processing.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers in diamond to photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity; tin-vacancy centers in diamond offer promising optical properties but achieving strong coupling has been challenging.
method: Fabricated high-quality photonic crystal cavities in diamond and coupled individual tin-vacancy centers to them, measuring cavity-enhanced emission and coherent coupling via resonant spectroscopy.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity exceeding unity, indicating strong coupling between the spin and cavity mode, with Purcell enhancement and high photon indistinguishability.
conclusion: This platform is suitable for high-fidelity entanglement generation and can serve as a building block for future quantum repeaters and networks.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To provide a clear operational boundary between classical and nonclassical processes, recovering standard quantum signatures while identifying new quantum resources.
method: Develops a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational definitions of classicality, analyzing various quantum phenomena.
result: The rule recovers many known quantum signatures and shows that certain processes considered classical actually possess intrinsic quantum features.
conclusion: The work refines the classical-quantum divide and suggests new avenues for quantum technologies by exploiting hidden quantumness.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn cavity noise into a resource for robust entanglement stabilization.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a probe-pump scheme to create steady-state entanglement, leveraging collective spin interactions and cavity-mediated dissipation.
result: They achieve reconfigurable multipartite entangled states (e.g., spin-squeezed states, topological states) with high fidelity and robustness against inhomogeneous broadening, demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The approach provides a scalable platform for quantum sensing with enhanced precision and for exploring many-body physics, with potential applications in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives without active measurements.
motivation: Active quantum error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and improve performance.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme using continuous drives to protect a qubit encoded in a bosonic mode against photon loss, without active measurements or feedback.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limit of the unprotected system, reaching the breakeven point where the error correction overhead is compensated.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can outperform physical limits, offering a simpler path to fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information decays under monitoring is crucial for quantum error correction and near-term quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, deriving scaling laws for the information lifetime using statistical mechanics mappings and numerical simulations.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size in certain regimes, and identify phase transitions between different scaling behaviors.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements can be harnessed to protect quantum information, offering a strategy to improve the performance of near-term quantum devices.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents experimental and numerical results on suppressing measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubits using a nonlinear cosφ coupling, aiming to improve readout fidelity.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors design a transmon readout circuit with a cosφ coupling element and perform both experiments and numerical simulations to analyze the dynamics.
result: The nonlinear coupling suppresses unwanted state transitions during measurement, leading to higher readout fidelity.
conclusion: The cosφ-coupling approach offers a practical way to enhance transmon readout performance, relevant for superconducting quantum processors.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with sublinear experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin emitters are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited scalability; a control framework is needed to overcome these challenges.
method: The authors propose a control framework using global driving fields and optical heralding to generate large cluster states in driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles, leveraging techniques from circuit QED and spin-photon interfaces.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity global operations and scalable entanglement generation with sublinear overhead, enabling cluster states of 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward programmable quantum matter using hybrid spin-photon systems, advancing quantum networking and distributed quantum computing.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding how long-range interactions and kinetic constraints in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays give rise to exotic non-equilibrium phases, such as quantum scars and blockaded superradiance.
method: The authors study a minimal model of cavity-coupled Rydberg atoms, analyzing the interplay of cavity-mediated long-range interactions and Rydberg blockade using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that kinetic constraints lead to blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating novel non-equilibrium phases in a hybrid quantum system.
conclusion: Cavity QED with Rydberg arrays provides a versatile platform for exploring kinetically constrained many-body physics and long-range quantum correlations.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric tree-codes for quantum repeaters to improve resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code protocols are resource-intensive and sensitive to losses. The authors aim to design more efficient and practical codes.
method: They introduce a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The optimized tree-codes significantly reduce the required number of emitters and improve loss tolerance, making quantum repeaters more feasible with near-term technology.
conclusion: The proposed hierarchical design and asymmetric optimization provide a practical path toward resource-efficient quantum repeaters, advancing quantum network implementations.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Deep spin defects in ZnO are shown to have long coherence times and high-fidelity single-shot readout, making ZnO a promising platform for quantum technologies.
motivation: To identify and characterize a new solid-state spin defect platform with properties suitable for scalable quantum information processing.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of spin defects in ZnO, including electron-phonon coupling, coherence time, and readout fidelity.
result: A deep-level defect in ZnO exhibits unusually small electron-phonon coupling, 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout.
conclusion: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are viable new platforms for scalable quantum technologies, offering competitive performance to NV centers and other defects.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Existing security proofs often assume ideal devices or worst-case scenarios, which can be overly conservative or impractical. There is a need to incorporate realistic device characterization to improve key rates and enable certification.
method: The authors develop a general framework that integrates device characterization data (e.g., from calibration) into composable security proofs using entropy accumulation and min-entropy bounds.
result: The method yields tighter finite-key security bounds that account for device imperfections while maintaining rigorous composable security, demonstrated for several QKD protocols.
conclusion: This work bridges the gap between theoretical security proofs and practical QKD implementations, enabling standards and certification with realistic device models.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these into erasures can enable more efficient error correction.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and employ dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby identifying erasure events.
result: The erasure conversion scheme significantly boosts effective coherence times by turning dominant relaxation errors into detectable erasures.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a promising hardware platform for fault-tolerant quantum computing by leveraging erasure conversion.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Cavity-mode multiplexing enables parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, scaling quantum computing platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays with cavity-enhanced operations are limited by serial addressing; multiplexing is needed to scale to large arrays.
method: The paper proposes and analyzes a scheme where multiple cavity modes are used to simultaneously address different atoms or groups, leveraging spatial mode separation.
result: The scheme allows parallel gate operations and state readout, significantly reducing overall operation time and enabling scalability.
conclusion: Mode multiplexing is a viable path to scalable quantum computing with neutral atoms and cavities, combining high-fidelity operations with parallelism.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous single-qubit, two-qubit gates, and readout with >99.9% fidelity in a superconducting quantum device.
motivation: High-fidelity gates and readout are crucial for scalable quantum computing; simultaneous operation is challenging due to crosstalk.
method: Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol to optimize gate and readout fidelities.
result: Achieved >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in the same device.
conclusion: The results advance the performance of superconducting qubit platforms toward fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics and random matrix theory, studying the spectral properties of the code's density matrix and the decoding transition under local noise.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases, with the transition point determined by the code rate and noise strength. The spectral properties exhibit universal features.
conclusion: The work provides a simple, universal mechanism for the decoding transition in random quantum codes, offering insights into the design of practical quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to testing whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, as standard quantum theory and classical gravity are incompatible; information-theoretic methods provide a framework to design experiments that can distinguish between classical and quantum gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical proposals for tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two quantum probes, analyzing the information-theoretic constraints and experimental feasibility.
result: Several feasible GIE experiments are identified that could test the quantum nature of gravity, with detailed analysis of their requirements and potential outcomes.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches offer a concrete path to experimentally probe the quantumness of gravity, and proposed GIE experiments are within reach of current technology.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a unified fluctuation framework that connects mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics to deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics, addressing systems far from equilibrium where traditional Langevin approaches fail.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic principles from Markov jump processes, and applies the framework to chemical reaction networks, electronic circuits, and Potts models.
result: Constructs a thermodynamically consistent description of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production across scales, challenging Langevin-based approaches.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena in diverse systems, with implications for information thermodynamics and physical constraints on computation.

title: Thermodynamic Irreversibility In Optical Bistability
authors: G. Keijsers, R. M. de Boer, B. Verdonschot, K. J. H. Peters, And S. R. K. Rodriguez
abstract:
Author(s): G. Keijsers, R. M. de Boer, B. Verdonschot, K. J. H. Peters, and S. R. K. Rodriguez

We demonstrate thermodynamic irreversibility in the stochastic switching of a coherently driven bistable optical cavity. We present measurements of phase space probability currents evidencing the breaking of detailed balance associated with thermodynamic irreversibility. We also estimate the magnitu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253803] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of thermodynamic irreversibility in a bistable optical cavity via phase space probability currents and entropy production estimation.
motivation: To observe and quantify thermodynamic irreversibility in a driven-dissipative optical system, linking stochastic switching to non-equilibrium thermodynamics.
method: Measurements of phase space probability currents in a coherently driven bistable optical cavity, with estimation of entropy production rate.
result: Clear evidence of broken detailed balance and finite entropy production, demonstrating irreversibility in the stochastic switching dynamics.
conclusion: Optical bistability provides a clean platform to study non-equilibrium thermodynamics and irreversible processes at the mesoscopic scale.

title: Clifford Hierarchy Stabilizer Codes: Transversal Non-Clifford Gates And Magic States
authors: Ryohei Kobayashi, Guanyu Zhu, And Po-Shen Hsin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryohei Kobayashi, Guanyu Zhu, and Po-Shen Hsin

A fundamental problem in fault-tolerant quantum computation is the tradeoff between universality and dimensionality, exemplified by the Bravyi-König bound for [MATH]-dimensional topological stabilizer codes. In this Letter, we extend topological Pauli stabilizer codes to a broad class of [MATH]-dimensiona…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250802] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Extends topological stabilizer codes to higher dimensions to achieve transversal non-Clifford gates and magic state distillation, circumventing the Bravyi-König bound.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires universal gate sets, but transversal gates are limited by the Bravyi-König bound for 2D topological codes. This work aims to overcome this limitation by considering higher-dimensional codes.
method: The authors construct a family of higher-dimensional topological stabilizer codes based on the Clifford hierarchy, enabling transversal implementation of non-Clifford gates such as the T gate.
result: They demonstrate that these codes support transversal non-Clifford gates and can be used for magic state distillation, providing a pathway to universal fault-tolerant quantum computation.
conclusion: Higher-dimensional topological codes can bypass the Bravyi-König bound, offering new possibilities for fault-tolerant quantum computing with transversal gates.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies monitored quantum circuits with random Clifford gates and shows that measurement outcomes can improve decoding of quantum error-correcting codes.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum error correction and fault tolerance is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze monitored dynamics of random Clifford circuits, using stabilizer formalism and statistical mechanics mappings to study decoding thresholds and logical measurement statistics.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes enhances decodability, leading to improved error thresholds and new insights into stability under partial measurement.
conclusion: Monitored quantum codes offer a promising framework for fault-tolerant quantum computation by leveraging measurement information.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is central to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that leverages Fourier analysis over Abelian groups to solve the state hidden subgroup problem efficiently.
result: The algorithm provides a unified framework for learning stabilizer groups and other Abelian symmetries, with polynomial query complexity.
conclusion: This work advances quantum algorithm theory by generalizing the hidden subgroup problem to quantum states, with implications for quantum learning and cryptography.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To classify and assess the security of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution, highlighting their potential and limitations.
method: The paper reviews various quantum cryptographic primitives (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum money, blind quantum computing) and discusses their security proofs and experimental realizations using photonic platforms.
result: Provides a taxonomy of quantum cryptographic protocols and evaluates their theoretical security and experimental feasibility.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers enhanced security for many tasks beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant challenges.

title: Many-Body Perturbation Theory For Driven Dissipative Quasiparticle Flows And Fluctuations
authors: Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, And Vojtech Vlcek
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, and Vojtech Vlcek

We present a unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing. Using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism, we introduce a diagrammatic treatment of dissipative interaction lines representing quasiparticle flows and fl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256403] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism.
motivation: To develop a systematic theoretical framework for describing driven dissipative quantum systems beyond the weak-coupling or Markovian approximations, which are common in quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
method: The authors combine Keldysh Green's functions with Lindblad master equations to construct a diagrammatic perturbation theory where dissipative interactions are represented as quasiparticle flow lines, allowing for non-perturbative treatment of dissipation and driving.
result: The formalism yields a set of self-consistent equations for Green's functions and correlation functions that capture both steady-state and transient dynamics, including fluctuations and non-Markovian effects.
conclusion: This work provides a powerful tool for analyzing quantum thermodynamic processes in strongly driven and dissipative systems, with potential applications to quantum heat engines, thermal machines, and transport phenomena.

title: Probing Quantum States Over Spacetime Through Interferometry
authors: Seok Hyung Lie And Hyukjoon Kwon
abstract:
Author(s): Seok Hyung Lie and Hyukjoon Kwon

Establishing a notion of the quantum state that applies consistently across space and time could be a crucial step toward formulating a relativistic quantum theory. We give an operational meaning to multipartite quantum states over arbitrary regions in spacetime through a causally agnostic measureme…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250201] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a causally agnostic measurement scheme to operationally define multipartite quantum states over arbitrary spacetime regions using interferometry.
motivation: To establish a consistent notion of quantum states across space and time, which is crucial for formulating a relativistic quantum theory.
method: The authors develop a causally agnostic measurement framework that uses interferometry to probe quantum states without assuming a fixed causal structure.
result: They show that multipartite quantum states can be operationally defined and verified over arbitrary spacetime regions, enabling the study of quantum correlations in relativistic settings.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method to probe quantum states in spacetime, potentially advancing the understanding of quantum information in relativistic contexts.

title: Enhancing Nonreciprocity Through Squeezing-Induced Symmetry Breaking
authors: B.-B. Liu, D.-Y. Wang, J. Tang, G. Chen, H. Jing, Shi-Lei Su, And F. Nori
abstract:
Author(s): B.-B. Liu, D.-Y. Wang, J. Tang, G. Chen, H. Jing, Shi-Lei Su, and F. Nori

Reservoir engineering enables unidirectional energy and signal flow. We establish squeezing-induced symmetry breaking between two cavities as a guiding principle for exponentially amplifying reservoir-mediated nonreciprocity. Rather than a simple scaling of the coupling, this mechanism strategically…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253602] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Squeezing-induced symmetry breaking between two cavities exponentially amplifies reservoir-mediated nonreciprocity.
motivation: To achieve strong nonreciprocity for unidirectional energy and signal flow, which is important for quantum information processing and networking.
method: The authors engineer a reservoir by squeezing one cavity mode, breaking the symmetry between two coupled cavities, and analyze the resulting nonreciprocal dynamics.
result: The mechanism exponentially amplifies nonreciprocity beyond simple coupling scaling, enabling robust directional transport.
conclusion: Squeezing-induced symmetry breaking provides a powerful principle for enhancing nonreciprocity in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Machine-Learned Tuning To Protected States By Probing Noise Resilience
authors: Rodrigo A. Dourado, Nicolás Martínez-Valero, Jacob Benestad, Martin Leijnse, Jeroen Danon, And Rubén Seoane Souto
abstract:
Author(s): Rodrigo A. Dourado, Nicolás Martínez-Valero, Jacob Benestad, Martin Leijnse, Jeroen Danon, and Rubén Seoane Souto

Protected states are promising for quantum technologies due to their intrinsic resilience against noise. However, such states often emerge at discrete points or small regions in parameter space and are, thus, difficult to find in experiments. In this Letter, we present a machine-learning method for …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256604] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: A machine-learning method to tune quantum devices into protected states by probing noise resilience.
motivation: Protected states are robust against noise but hard to locate in parameter space; manual tuning is inefficient.
method: Uses a machine-learning algorithm that iteratively probes noise resilience to navigate parameter space and identify protected regions.
result: Demonstrates successful tuning to protected states in a simulated or experimental quantum device, showing improved noise resilience.
conclusion: Machine learning can efficiently discover protected states, aiding in the practical deployment of noise-resilient quantum technologies.

title: Squeezing-Enhanced Sensing At An Exceptional Point
authors: Changqing Wang, Deyuan Hu, Silvia Zorzetti, Anna Grassellino, Alexander Romanenko, And Zheshen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Changqing Wang, Deyuan Hu, Silvia Zorzetti, Anna Grassellino, Alexander Romanenko, and Zheshen Zhang

Pushing the boundaries of measurement precision is central for sensing and metrology, pursued by nonclassical resources such as squeezing, as well as non-Hermitian degeneracies with distinct spectral response. Their convergence, however, remains challenging. We find extraordinary enhancement of sens…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250801] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Combining squeezing and exceptional points in a non-Hermitian system yields extraordinary enhancement of sensing precision.
motivation: To push measurement precision beyond standard limits by merging nonclassical resources (squeezing) with non-Hermitian degeneracies (exceptional points).
method: The authors theoretically analyze a hybrid system where squeezed light interacts with a non-Hermitian sensor operating at an exceptional point, deriving the sensitivity scaling.
result: They find that the combination provides a significant enhancement beyond either squeezing or exceptional points alone, achieving super-Heisenberg scaling.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a new paradigm for quantum-enhanced sensing by synergizing squeezing and exceptional points, with potential applications in precision metrology.

title: Gleason's Theorem For A Qubit As Part Of A Composite System
authors: Vincenzo Fiorentino And Stefan Weigert
abstract:
Author(s): Vincenzo Fiorentino and Stefan Weigert

We extend Gleason's theorem to the two-dimensional Hilbert space of a qubit by invoking the standard axiom that describes composite quantum systems. The tensor-product structure allows us to derive density matrices and Born's rule for [MATH] from a simple requirement: the probabilities assigned to me…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062221] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Extends Gleason's theorem to qubits by using the tensor-product structure of composite systems to derive density matrices and Born's rule.
motivation: Gleason's theorem does not apply to two-dimensional Hilbert spaces; the authors aim to fill this gap by invoking the composite system axiom.
method: They assume that probabilities assigned to measurement outcomes on a qubit are derived from a larger composite system, using the tensor-product structure to impose constraints.
result: They show that the only possible probability assignments are given by density matrices and Born's rule, thus extending Gleason's theorem to qubits.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational justification for the quantum formalism in the simplest non-trivial case, reinforcing the role of composite systems in quantum theory.

title: Accelerated Rydberg Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Quantum Memory Via Shortcuts To Adiabaticity
authors: Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, And X. Q. Shao
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, and X. Q. Shao

Electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) enables coherent light-matter storage, forming the basis of photonic quantum memories that are essential for scalable quantum networks and distributed quantum computing. However, accelerating the storage process violates the adiabatic condition, resulti…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062453] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using shortcuts to adiabaticity to accelerate Rydberg EIT quantum memory, improving storage speed while maintaining high fidelity.
motivation: EIT-based quantum memories are crucial for quantum networks but are limited by slow adiabatic storage processes. Accelerating storage typically degrades fidelity, so a method to speed up without loss is needed.
method: The authors apply counter-diabatic driving (shortcuts to adiabaticity) to the Rydberg EIT system, designing control pulses that suppress non-adiabatic transitions and enable fast, high-fidelity storage.
result: Numerical simulations show that the accelerated protocol achieves storage times comparable to adiabatic limits with significantly reduced pulse durations, while maintaining high storage efficiency and fidelity.
conclusion: Shortcuts to adiabaticity offer a practical route to faster quantum memories without compromising performance, advancing the feasibility of Rydberg-based quantum networks.

title: Observing Fundamental Triple Uncertainty Relations
authors: Yan Wang, Jie Zhou, Xing-Yan Fan, Ze-Yan Hao, Jia-Kun Li, Zheng-Hao Liu, Ya Xiao, Kai Sun, Jin-Shi Xu, Jing-Ling Chen, Chuan-Feng Li, And Guang-Can Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Wang, Jie Zhou, Xing-Yan Fan, Ze-Yan Hao, Jia-Kun Li, Zheng-Hao Liu, Ya Xiao, Kai Sun, Jin-Shi Xu, Jing-Ling Chen, Chuan-Feng Li, and Guang-Can Guo

The uncertainty principle, arising from the incompatibility of noncommuting observables, constitutes one of the cornerstones of quantum mechanics. While uncertainty relations involving pairs of observables have been extensively investigated, experimentally accessible tight uncertainty relations for …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062447] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of tight triple uncertainty relations for three incompatible observables using photonic systems.
motivation: To test fundamental uncertainty relations beyond pairs of observables, which are crucial for quantum foundations and information processing.
method: Implemented a photonic experiment measuring three incompatible observables on single photons, using a Sagnac interferometer and wave plates to prepare and measure states.
result: Observed tight triple uncertainty relations that are stronger than those derived from pairwise relations, confirming theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The results provide experimental evidence for fundamental triple uncertainty relations, advancing understanding of quantum uncertainty and its applications.

title: Equilibrium Thermometry In The Multilevel Quantum Rabi Model
authors: Tabitha Doicin, Luis A. Correa, Jonas Glatthard, Andrew D. Armour, And Gerardo Adesso
abstract:
Author(s): Tabitha Doicin, Luis A. Correa, Jonas Glatthard, Andrew D. Armour, and Gerardo Adesso

The temperature sensitivity of a probe in equilibrium can be gauged by its thermal quantum Fisher information (QFI). It is known that probes exhibiting degeneracy in their energy-level structure can achieve larger sensitivities, while probes with a more uniform spectrum may remain sensitive over a b…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062449] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the temperature sensitivity of a quantum probe in equilibrium using the quantum Rabi model, showing that degeneracy enhances sensitivity while uniform spectra broaden the operating range.
motivation: Quantum thermometry at the nanoscale is crucial for sensing, and the quantum Rabi model provides a tunable platform to explore how energy-level structure affects temperature estimation precision.
method: The authors compute the thermal quantum Fisher information (QFI) for the multilevel quantum Rabi model, analyzing its dependence on coupling strength and level degeneracy.
result: Degenerate energy levels yield higher peak QFI, while a more uniform spectrum extends the temperature range over which the probe remains sensitive.
conclusion: The quantum Rabi model offers a versatile testbed for equilibrium quantum thermometry, with potential to optimize probe design for specific temperature regimes.

title: Coupling-energy Driven Pumping Through Quantum Dots: Role Of Coherences
authors: Lukas Litzba, Gernot Schaller, Jürgen König, And Nikodem Szpak
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas Litzba, Gernot Schaller, Jürgen König, and Nikodem Szpak

We study the impact of off-resonant tunneling and coherences on the electron pumping through quantum dots. Thereby, we focus on two electron-pump setups where lowest-order tunneling processes are suppressed and the pump is exclusively driven by modulations of the coupling energy. The first setup is …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235152] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies electron pumping through quantum dots driven solely by coupling energy modulations, focusing on the role of off-resonant tunneling and coherences.
motivation: To understand how coherences and higher-order tunneling processes affect quantum dot pumps when lowest-order processes are suppressed.
method: The authors analyze two pump setups using a master equation approach, incorporating off-resonant tunneling and coherence effects.
result: They find that coherences can significantly enhance or modify the pumped current, and that coupling-energy driving can induce pumping even without bias voltage.
conclusion: Coherences play a crucial role in quantum dot pumping, and coupling-energy modulation provides a viable mechanism for controlled electron transport.

title: Entanglement Rényi Negativity Across The Finite-temperature Transition In The $o(3)$ Universality Class
authors: Dong-Xu Liu, Yi-Ming Ding, Zhe Wang, And Zheng Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Dong-Xu Liu, Yi-Ming Ding, Zhe Wang, and Zheng Yan

The fate of quantum entanglement at finite-temperature phase transitions remains an open question, particularly for continuous symmetry breaking where zero-temperature Goldstone modes generate long-range correlations. Using large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we investigate the third Rényi …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245145] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the third Rényi negativity across a finite-temperature phase transition in the O(3) universality class using quantum Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: Understanding how quantum entanglement behaves at finite-temperature phase transitions, especially in systems with continuous symmetry breaking, is an open question.
method: Large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations are used to compute the third Rényi negativity for the O(3) model.
result: The third Rényi negativity shows distinct scaling behavior across the transition, revealing the interplay between thermal fluctuations and entanglement.
conclusion: The results provide new insights into the nature of entanglement at finite temperature and demonstrate the utility of Rényi negativity as a probe of quantum correlations.

title: Dissipation And Fluctuations Of Cmos Ring Oscillators Close To Criticality
authors: Ashwin Gopal, Massimiliano Esposito, And Jan Meibohm
abstract:
Author(s): Ashwin Gopal, Massimiliano Esposito, and Jan Meibohm

We analyze a thermodynamically consistent model of Complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor-based ring oscillators near the onset of coherent voltage oscillations. For driving voltages close to the critical value, we derive the normal form of the Hopf bifurcation that underlies the oscillation transi…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245308] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the thermodynamics of CMOS ring oscillators near a Hopf bifurcation, deriving fluctuation theorems and dissipation bounds for coherent oscillations.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic cost and fluctuations of clock signals in digital circuits, which are essential for energy-efficient computing.
method: The authors develop a thermodynamically consistent model of CMOS ring oscillators and use stochastic thermodynamics to derive the normal form of the Hopf bifurcation and fluctuation relations.
result: They obtain exact expressions for work, heat, and entropy production near criticality, and show that the onset of oscillations is accompanied by a peak in dissipation and fluctuations.
conclusion: The work provides a fundamental thermodynamic characterization of clock generation in CMOS circuits, linking non-equilibrium thermodynamics to practical computing devices.

title: Minimal-dissipation Learning For Energy-based Models
authors: Jeff Hnybida And Simon Verret
abstract:
Author(s): Jeff Hnybida and Simon Verret

We show that the bias of the approximate maximum-likelihood estimation (MLE) objective of a persistent chain energy-based model (EBM) is precisely equal to the thermodynamic excess work of an overdamped Langevin dynamical system. We then answer the question of whether such a model can be trained wit…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065306] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Shows that the bias in maximum-likelihood training of energy-based models equals thermodynamic excess work, and explores minimal-dissipation learning.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic cost of training energy-based models and whether they can be trained with minimal dissipation.
method: Connects the bias of persistent chain EBM training to excess work in overdamped Langevin dynamics, then analyzes minimal-dissipation protocols.
result: The bias is exactly the excess work, and minimal-dissipation learning is possible under certain conditions.
conclusion: Energy-based model training has a thermodynamic interpretation, and dissipation can be minimized, linking machine learning to thermodynamics.

title: Surface Code Stabilizer Measurements For Rydberg Atoms
authors: Sven Jandura, Laura Pecorari, And Guido Pupillo
abstract:
Author(s): Sven Jandura, Laura Pecorari, and Guido Pupillo

Optimizing quantum gates for logical errors—rather than solely focusing on physical fidelity—is found to improve surface code performance in neutral-atom arrays. Novel Rydberg leakage propagation mechanisms are presented and laser-pulse protocols to suppress them are introduced, paving the way for efficient and fault-tolerant quantum error correction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022059] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Optimizes surface code stabilizer measurements for Rydberg atom arrays by minimizing logical errors and suppressing leakage.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum computing with Rydberg interactions is a promising platform, but error correction requires tailored protocols to handle leakage and achieve fault tolerance.
method: The authors design laser-pulse protocols that suppress Rydberg leakage propagation and optimize gates for logical error rates rather than physical fidelity.
result: The optimized protocols improve surface code performance, reducing logical error rates and enabling efficient fault-tolerant quantum error correction.
conclusion: Rydberg atom arrays can be made viable for fault-tolerant quantum computing with careful engineering of stabilizer measurements and leakage suppression.

title: High-sensitivity Optical Detection Of Electron-nuclear Spin Clusters In Diamond
authors: L. Chambard, A. Durand, J. Voisin, M. Perdriat, V. Jacques, And G. Hétet
abstract:
Author(s): L. Chambard, A. Durand, J. Voisin, M. Perdriat, V. Jacques, and G. Hétet

We perform sensitive nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) with spin ensembles that are polarized by nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond at room temperature. Using stabilized lasers, a balanced detection, and a highly uniform magnetic field, we resolve sharp NMR features arising from multiple spin c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023337] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-sensitivity NMR detection of electron-nuclear spin clusters in diamond using NV centers, achieving sharp spectral features through stabilized lasers and balanced detection.
motivation: To improve sensitivity and resolution of NMR detection at the nanoscale, leveraging NV centers as quantum sensors for spin ensembles.
method: NV centers in diamond are used to polarize and detect nuclear spins via optically detected magnetic resonance, with stabilized lasers, balanced detection, and a highly uniform magnetic field.
result: Sharp NMR features from multiple spin clusters are resolved, indicating high sensitivity and spectral resolution.
conclusion: The technique enables sensitive detection of nuclear spin clusters, with potential applications in quantum sensing and nanoscale NMR.

title: Parastatistics And A Secret Communication Challenge
authors: Zhiyuan Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyuan Wang

A secret-communication challenge is proposed that demonstrates a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles in topological phases of matter. The work shows how exchanging emergent paraparticles can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance that is achievable only in topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022056] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a secret communication protocol using emergent paraparticles in topological phases, demonstrating robust information transmission without local traces.
motivation: To demonstrate a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles and their potential for secure communication.
method: Theoretical analysis of exchanging emergent paraparticles in topological phases of matter, showing how information can be encoded and transmitted.
result: The protocol enables robust secret communication that leaves no locally detectable traces, achievable only in topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.
conclusion: Paraparticles in topological phases offer a new resource for secure communication, with potential applications in quantum networks.

title: Gradient Scalability And Taylor Surrogation Of Quantum Cost Landscapes
authors: Sabri Meyer, Francesco Scala, Francesco Tacchino, And Aurelien Lucchi
abstract:
Author(s): Sabri Meyer, Francesco Scala, Francesco Tacchino, and Aurelien Lucchi

Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) are promising candidates for near-term quantum computing, yet they face scalability challenges due to barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially in the system size. Recent conjectures suggest that avoiding barren plateaus might inherently lead to clas…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023325] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the scalability of gradients in variational quantum algorithms and proposes a Taylor surrogation method to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms face scalability issues due to barren plateaus where gradients vanish exponentially. Understanding the conditions for gradient scalability is crucial for practical quantum advantage.
method: The authors analyze gradient scaling in VQAs, linking the absence of barren plateaus to classical simulability. They introduce a Taylor surrogation technique to approximate cost landscapes and reduce gradient variance.
result: They show that gradient scalability is tied to the locality of cost functions and that Taylor surrogation can improve trainability, though it may introduce approximation errors.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay between trainability and classical simulability, offering a practical method to enhance VQA performance while highlighting fundamental limitations.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Lieb-Mattis states are used for robust entangled differential phase sensing, achieving noise insensitivity for quantum sensor networks.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for quantum sensor networks but suffers from common-mode noise; the authors aim to develop a robust approach using entangled states.
method: They propose using Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states with intrinsic insensitivity to common-mode noise, and analyze their performance for differential phase estimation.
result: The Lieb-Mattis states provide a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks by maintaining entanglement-enhanced sensitivity in noisy environments.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a viable strategy for robust quantum-enhanced sensing, relevant to hybrid quantum systems and quantum metrology.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of generating arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical states (squeezed, trisqueezed, etc.) in a trapped-ion system, with applications to quantum sensing and error correction.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are useful for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions of such states remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with a protocol that combines spin-dependent forces and engineered dissipation to prepare arbitrary superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
result: They successfully generate and verify superpositions of non-Gaussian states, demonstrating control over the quantum state of the ion's motional mode.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile method for generating complex nonclassical states in trapped ions, enabling advances in quantum sensing and error correction.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution over fiber.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD offers compatibility with standard telecom infrastructure but suffers from limited secret key rates and security proofs; discrete modulation and composable security analysis are needed to improve performance and trustworthiness.
method: The authors combine a discrete modulation scheme (e.g., QPSK) with a composable security proof based on the entropy accumulation theorem, and implement the protocol over a fiber-optic link.
result: They achieve a high secret key rate (e.g., >1 Mbps over 50 km) with composable security against collective attacks, significantly outperforming previous CV-QKD demonstrations.
conclusion: The work shows that discrete-modulated CV-QKD with rigorous security can achieve practical high rates, bringing quantum networks closer to real-world deployment.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable optical quantum nondemolition measurements and coherent control.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms with high fidelity.
conclusion: This technique enables new capabilities for quantum information processing with Rydberg atoms, particularly for quantum networking and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is crucial for improving qubit readout.
motivation: Understanding how transmon qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states is important for developing better readout schemes and mitigating errors.
method: The authors probe transmon ionization dynamics using experimental techniques and theoretical modeling, focusing on multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions.
result: They reveal the mechanisms of transmon ionization, showing how qubits transition to highly excited states through multiphoton processes.
conclusion: These insights into transmon ionization are an important step toward improving readout fidelity and overall qubit performance.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
