authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubits, challenging quantum error correction even with radiation shielding.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is crucial for scalable quantum error correction in superconducting qubit processors.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, analyzing error correlations and burst statistics.
result: They identify a new type of correlated phase error burst that persists despite state-of-the-art radiation protection, with spatial and temporal correlations that undermine standard error correction codes.
conclusion: Radiation-induced correlated phase errors pose a significant obstacle for fault-tolerant quantum computing, requiring new mitigation strategies beyond passive shielding.

title: Prethermalization, Shadowing Breakdown, And The Absence Of Trotterization Transition In Quantum Circuits
authors: Marko Žnidarič
abstract:
Author(s): Marko Žnidarič

New research uses truncated propagators to show that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite. It also offers a method to calculate thermalization time, finding that the “Trotterization transition” is generically a finite-size effect.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021017] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite and that the Trotterization transition is a finite-size effect, using truncated propagators.
motivation: Understanding thermalization and prethermalization in quantum circuits is crucial for quantum simulation and computing, where Trotterization is used to approximate Hamiltonian evolution.
method: The author uses truncated propagators to analyze the shadowing time and thermalization time in many-body chaotic quantum circuits.
result: Shadowing time is found to be finite, and the Trotterization transition is shown to be a finite-size effect, not a true phase transition.
conclusion: The results imply that for large enough systems, Trotterization does not lead to a distinct prethermal regime, affecting the design of quantum simulations.

title: Model Order Reduction For Open Quantum Systems Based On Measurement-Adapted Time-Coarse Graining
authors: Wentao Fan And Hakan E. Türeci
abstract:
Author(s): Wentao Fan and Hakan E. Türeci

Researchers introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, a model reduction technique that uses the time resolution of measurement channels to capture the observable dynamics of a complex quantum system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021015] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A model reduction technique for open quantum systems based on measurement-adapted time-coarse graining that captures observable dynamics at the resolution of measurement channels.
motivation: Complex open quantum systems are difficult to simulate due to many degrees of freedom; a reduced model that preserves only observable dynamics is needed.
method: The authors introduce a coarse-graining procedure that adapts to the time resolution of measurement channels, effectively discarding fast degrees of freedom that are not resolved.
result: The method yields a reduced-order model that accurately reproduces the measured dynamics while significantly lowering computational cost.
conclusion: Measurement-adapted time-coarse graining is a practical tool for simulating open quantum systems where only certain observables are of interest.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and fundamental tests; trapped ions offer a clean platform for generating and exploiting spin-dependent squeezed states.
method: The authors theoretically propose and experimentally realize a protocol using trapped ions to create spin-dependent squeezed states via spin-motion coupling, then apply them to displacement sensing.
result: They achieve optimal sensitivity for displacement estimation, surpassing the standard quantum limit and approaching the Heisenberg limit.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to optimal quantum-enhanced metrology, with implications for force sensing and quantum information.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified operational measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries required to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and relate it to the state's covariance matrix and Wigner function negativity.
result: The symplectic rank provides a tight lower bound on the number of non-Gaussian operations needed for state preparation and measurement, and it is shown to be additive under tensor products.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful and operationally meaningful resource measure for non-Gaussianity, with implications for quantum information processing with continuous variables.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying sources of decoherence and instability for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters in silicon are promising for scalable quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding the origins of decoherence is crucial for improving coherence times.
method: The authors study cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, using optical spectroscopy and noise analysis to characterize spectral diffusion and decoherence mechanisms.
result: They identify key sources of spectral instability, including charge noise and phonon interactions, and demonstrate that cavity coupling can mitigate some decoherence effects.
conclusion: Cavity-enhanced erbium emitters in silicon show potential for quantum networking, but further reduction of spectral noise is needed for practical applications.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and lack scalability.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over model parameters and model classes, enabling fast and scalable inference.
result: The method accurately identifies spin environments (e.g., number of spins, coupling strengths) from noisy measurement data and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides an efficient tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with potential applications in quantum sensing and control of hybrid systems.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing and simulation, but loading and imaging them with high fidelity and low atom loss remains challenging. EIT offers a way to perform nondestructive imaging and continuous loading.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency to image atoms with minimal scattering, reducing atom loss during imaging. They also use EIT for loading atoms into arrays from a magneto-optical trap, enabling continuous operation.
result: They achieve high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and demonstrate continuous loading of atom arrays, with improved atom survival rates compared to conventional methods.
conclusion: EIT-based techniques significantly enhance the performance of neutral-atom arrays, making them more viable for quantum information processing applications.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: An open-source pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates for quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum computing requires high-fidelity multiqubit gates to implement quantum error correction codes efficiently.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that designs and optimizes multiqubit Rydberg gates, leveraging the Rydberg blockade mechanism.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity multiqubit gates suitable for quantum error correction applications.
conclusion: The work advances neutral-atom platforms as viable candidates for fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling efficient multiqubit operations.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating miniaturized device-independent randomness expansion.
motivation: To realize a compact, scalable quantum random number generator with device-independent security guarantees, suitable for practical quantum cryptography and networking.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that integrates all necessary components for a self-testing quantum randomness expansion protocol, including entangled photon sources, measurement devices, and real-time randomness extraction.
result: The chip successfully generates certified randomness with a high rate, and the self-testing protocol verifies the quantum behavior of the devices without trusting them, achieving a randomness expansion ratio that surpasses previous integrated implementations.
conclusion: This work demonstrates the feasibility of fully integrated photonic chips for device-independent quantum randomness generation, paving the way for production-scale quantum security devices and network nodes.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, achieving stronger antibunching and higher transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work explores collective effects to relax that requirement.
method: The authors theoretically study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the photon statistics and transmission using a master equation approach.
result: They find that the photon blockade effect is collectively enhanced with system size, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission even when individual emitters are weakly coupled.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to achieve photon blockade, relevant for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving enables fast quantum state preparation but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often suffer from low fidelity.
method: The authors introduce a weighted action approach combined with computer algebra to optimize variational counterdiabatic protocols, reducing errors.
result: The new method yields significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in numerical simulations.
conclusion: This technique provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers achieve significantly enhanced bandwidth and saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling simultaneous amplification of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved Josephson mixers are promising components for quantum signal processing and transduction in large-scale quantum processors.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise, with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information from noise, but existing methods are inefficient for spatially correlated noise and large qubit arrays.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, leveraging error correction principles to cancel k-local noise.
result: They produce device-tailored sequences whose length scales only with the locality of the noise, not the number of qubits, enabling efficient decoupling for large systems.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering a practical tool for noise mitigation in multi-qubit devices.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without additional noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a coherent noise cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This all-optical approach provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, enabling significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine for many quantum algorithms, but its cost is dominated by Hamiltonian simulation. Reducing this overhead is crucial for practical quantum advantage.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized product formulas that combine deterministic and randomized Trotter steps, analyzed using a combination of Hamiltonian simulation theory and phase estimation error analysis.
result: They prove that the new approach achieves orders-of-magnitude resource savings compared to standard Trotter-based phase estimation for benchmark quantum chemistry problems.
conclusion: Partially randomized time evolution offers a practical and efficient way to reduce the cost of phase estimation, bringing quantum chemistry simulations closer to feasibility.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics beyond simple string breaking.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in confining gauge theories is important for quantum simulation and non-equilibrium dynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and numerical simulations to explore string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes.
result: They identify experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking exhibits complex quantum dynamics, not just simple breaking.
conclusion: The findings provide new probes for studying confinement and non-equilibrium quantum dynamics in analog quantum simulators.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves nondemolition measurement fidelity in multilevel quantum systems, demonstrated on a silicon spin qudit.
motivation: Quantum measurements in multilevel systems often cause back-action that destroys quantum information; a nondemolition readout is crucial for quantum error correction and state preparation.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis to minimize disturbance, using real-time feedback on a silicon spin qudit.
result: The protocol achieves a readout fidelity of 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors.
conclusion: Adaptive readout is a practical technique to enhance nondemolition measurements across various qudit platforms, improving performance for quantum information processing.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations achieves sevenfold improvement in accuracy for variational algorithm simulation.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in transmon-based quantum processors, especially for near-term variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a sparse noise model capturing spatiotemporally correlated errors, likely using a combination of experimental characterization and theoretical fitting.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise modeling significantly enhances the fidelity of simulations for transmon-based multi-qubit operations, aiding in error mitigation and algorithm design.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a leakage-protected idle operation for a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to create an energy gap.
motivation: Leakage errors in exchange-only spin qubits degrade gate fidelity; protecting idle operation is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors tune pairwise exchange interactions between three electrons to be exactly equal, opening an energy gap between the computational subspace and leakage states.
result: They experimentally achieve suppressed leakage errors during idle operation, improving qubit coherence and fidelity.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method to enhance the performance of exchange-only spin qubits, advancing their viability for quantum information processing.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental implementations.
motivation: Continuous-variable approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure and higher secret key rates in certain regimes.
method: The review surveys theoretical foundations (Gaussian states, homodyne detection, reconciliation) and experimental progress in CV-QKD, CV-MDI-QKD, and CV quantum networks.
result: CV quantum communication has reached maturity with field trials and commercial systems, but challenges remain in long-distance transmission and integration with quantum repeaters.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a viable and complementary approach to discrete-variable systems, with ongoing research aimed at improving distance, rate, and security.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classifying nonequilibrium stationary states using quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors employ nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known critical phenomena and topological phases.
conclusion: The classification provides a systematic understanding of nonequilibrium steady states and guides future experiments.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: A review of computational methods for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques.
motivation: Understanding and predicting decoherence is crucial for developing long-lived spin qubits for quantum technologies.
method: The paper reviews ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times for various spin qubit platforms.
result: Cluster expansion techniques can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubits, but challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming reliable, aiding the design of better spin qubits, though further work is needed for complex environments.

title: Revisiting The Ratchet Principle: When Hidden Conservation Laws Prevent Directed Currents In Stochastic Systems
authors: Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, and Julien Tailleur

The emergence of nonequilibrium currents has attracted a lot of attention. The “ratchet principle” identifies the violation of any form of parity and time-reversal symmetries as the necessary conditions for the emergence of such currents. Here we study active and passive systems with asymmetric spat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 257102] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper revisits the ratchet principle for stochastic systems, showing that hidden conservation laws can prevent directed currents even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are broken.
motivation: To understand the necessary conditions for directed currents in nonequilibrium systems, particularly active and passive systems with asymmetric spatial structures.
method: The authors analyze stochastic systems with asymmetric spatial structures and identify hidden conservation laws that suppress directed currents despite symmetry breaking.
result: They demonstrate that hidden conservation laws can prevent directed currents, refining the ratchet principle.
conclusion: The work provides a deeper understanding of nonequilibrium currents and the role of conservation laws in stochastic systems.

title: Black Hole Thermodynamics Without Black Hole Solutions
authors: Meng-Nan Yang, Guan-Yi Lu, And H. Lü
abstract:
Author(s): Meng-Nan Yang, Guan-Yi Lu, and H. Lü

We consider the string-theory-inspired Einstein-Maxwell-Maxwell-dilaton theory and show that we can derive the complete set of thermodynamic quantities of charged black holes without having to construct the black hole solutions. We argue that the technique can be applied more broadly to string theor…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251403] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A method to derive black hole thermodynamics without explicit black hole solutions, using string-theory-inspired Einstein-Maxwell-Maxwell-dilaton theory.
motivation: Black hole thermodynamics is typically derived from explicit solutions, which can be cumbersome. This work aims to extract thermodynamic quantities directly from the Lagrangian, simplifying the process.
method: The authors use a technique based on the Wald formalism and Euclidean action method, applied to a general class of theories, to compute thermodynamic quantities like temperature and entropy without solving the field equations.
result: They successfully derive the complete set of thermodynamic quantities for charged black holes in the Einstein-Maxwell-Maxwell-dilaton theory, demonstrating the method's validity.
conclusion: The technique can be broadly applied to string theory and other gravitational theories, offering a streamlined approach to black hole thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Implementation Of Higher-order Power Method For Estimating Geometric Entanglement Of Pure States
authors: Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, And Elena Blokhina
abstract:
Author(s): Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, and Elena Blokhina

Entanglement is one of the fundamental properties of a quantum state and is a crucial differentiator between classical and quantum computation. There are many ways to define entanglement and its measure, depending on the problem or application under consideration. Each of these measures may be compu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062459] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for estimating geometric entanglement of pure states using a higher-order power method.
motivation: Geometric entanglement is a measure of multipartite entanglement, but its computation is classically hard. A quantum algorithm could provide a speedup.
method: The authors design a quantum circuit that implements a higher-order power method to find the closest separable state and compute the geometric measure of entanglement.
result: They demonstrate the algorithm on small examples and analyze its complexity, showing a potential quantum advantage.
conclusion: The quantum implementation offers a viable approach to estimate geometric entanglement, though practical realization requires fault-tolerant quantum computers.

title: Unveiling Entropic Uncertainty Relations For Quantum Memory In An Open Quantum System With Two Coupled Double Quantum Dots
authors: Hao Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Wang

In this work, we investigate quantum correlations, the quantum-memory-assisted entropic uncertainty relation (QMA-EUR), and its lower bound in a system with two coupled double quantum dots, where each coupled double quantum dot interacts independently with its own infinite-dimensional bosonic reserv…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062460] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Investigates quantum-memory-assisted entropic uncertainty relations in a system of two coupled double quantum dots interacting with bosonic reservoirs.
motivation: To understand how open system dynamics and quantum correlations affect the entropic uncertainty relation, which is fundamental for quantum information processing.
method: The study models two coupled double quantum dots, each coupled to its own bosonic reservoir, and computes the QMA-EUR and its lower bound using quantum correlation measures.
result: The entropic uncertainty and its lower bound are influenced by the coupling strength, reservoir temperature, and initial state correlations, with quantum correlations playing a key role.
conclusion: The work provides insights into controlling uncertainty in open quantum systems, relevant for quantum memory and cryptography applications.

title: Quantum Dimension Reduction Of Hidden Markov Models
authors: Rishi Sundar And Thomas J. Elliott
abstract:
Author(s): Rishi Sundar and Thomas J. Elliott

Hidden Markov models (HMMs) are ubiquitous in time-series modeling, with applications ranging from chemical reaction modeling to speech recognition. These HMMs are often large, with high-dimensional memories. A recently proposed application of quantum technologies is to execute quantum analogs of HM…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062461] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum dimension reduction technique for hidden Markov models using quantum information theory to compress the memory state.
motivation: Hidden Markov models often require large memory, and quantum analogs can be more efficient. The authors aim to reduce the quantum memory dimension while preserving the model's output statistics.
method: They develop a quantum algorithm that uses quantum state compression and information-theoretic bounds to reduce the dimension of the quantum hidden Markov model's memory.
result: The method achieves exponential reduction in memory dimension for certain classes of HMMs, with rigorous bounds on the approximation error.
conclusion: Quantum dimension reduction offers a practical advantage for simulating complex stochastic processes, bridging quantum information theory and machine learning.

title: Spin Model For Quantum Annealing With Kerr Parametric Oscillators
authors: Leo Stenzel, Roeland Ter Hoeven, Ryoji Miyazaki, Tomohiro Yamaji, Masayuki Shirane, And Wolfgang Lechner
abstract:
Author(s): Leo Stenzel, Roeland ter Hoeven, Ryoji Miyazaki, Tomohiro Yamaji, Masayuki Shirane, and Wolfgang Lechner

Coherent states offer a promising path for near-term quantum computing due to their inherent protection against bit-flip noise. However, their large photon numbers can be challenging for numerical simulation. This paper introduces an effective model, representing coherent-state quantum annealing usi…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062621] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Introduces an effective spin model for quantum annealing using Kerr parametric oscillators, enabling efficient simulation of coherent-state quantum annealing.
motivation: Coherent-state quantum computing is promising for near-term devices but suffers from large photon numbers that hinder numerical simulation. An effective model is needed to capture the essential physics without full quantum simulation.
method: The authors derive an effective spin model that represents the coherent-state quantum annealing process with Kerr parametric oscillators, mapping the system to a spin Hamiltonian amenable to classical simulation.
result: The effective model accurately reproduces the dynamics and ground-state properties of the original system, allowing simulation of larger systems than previously possible.
conclusion: The spin model provides a practical tool for studying quantum annealing with Kerr parametric oscillators, bridging the gap between theoretical proposals and experimental realization.

title: Quantum Simulation Of Fermionic non-Abelian Lattice Gauge Theories In $(2+1)$ Dimensions With Built-in Gauge Protection
authors: Gaia de Paciani, Lukas Homeier, Jad C. Halimeh, Monika Aidelsburger, And Fabian Grusdt
abstract:
Author(s): Gaia De Paciani, Lukas Homeier, Jad C. Halimeh, Monika Aidelsburger, and Fabian Grusdt

Recent advancements in the field of quantum simulation have significantly expanded the potential for applications, particularly in the context of lattice gauge theories (LGTs). Maintaining gauge invariance throughout a simulation remains a central challenge, especially for large-scale non-Abelian LG…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063327] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum simulation scheme for non-Abelian lattice gauge theories in (2+1)D using ultracold atoms with built-in gauge protection.
motivation: Simulating non-Abelian lattice gauge theories is challenging due to gauge invariance violations; the authors aim to provide a scalable and robust approach.
method: They design a hybrid quantum system combining ultracold atoms in optical lattices with gauge protection terms that energetically suppress gauge violations.
result: The scheme achieves reliable gauge invariance and can simulate real-time dynamics of non-Abelian gauge theories, demonstrated through numerical benchmarks.
conclusion: This work advances quantum simulation of fundamental gauge theories, with potential for near-term experimental realization.

title: Spin Coherence Scale: Operator-ordering Sensitivity Beyond The Heisenberg-Weyl Group
authors: Aaron Z. Goldberg, Andre J. Rodrigues, Y. Batuhan Yilmaz, Aephraim M. Steinberg, And Anaelle Hertz
abstract:
Author(s): Aaron Z. Goldberg, Andre J. Rodrigues, Y. Batuhan Yilmaz, Aephraim M. Steinberg, and Anaelle Hertz

We introduce the spin coherence scale as a measure of quantum coherence for spin systems, generalizing the quadrature coherence scale (QCS) previously defined for quadrature observables. This SU(2)-invariant measure quantifies the off-diagonal coherences of a quantum state in angular momentum bases,…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062457] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a spin coherence scale as an SU(2)-invariant measure of quantum coherence for spin systems, generalizing the quadrature coherence scale.
motivation: Existing coherence measures are often basis-dependent or not tailored to spin systems; a scale that captures operator-ordering sensitivity beyond the Heisenberg-Weyl group is needed.
method: Defines the spin coherence scale using SU(2) group theory and operator ordering, and analyzes its properties for various spin states.
result: The measure quantifies off-diagonal coherences in angular momentum bases and exhibits sensitivity to operator ordering, providing a new tool for coherence characterization.
conclusion: The spin coherence scale offers a physically meaningful, invariant measure of coherence for spin systems, with potential applications in quantum information and metrology.

title: Scalable Quantum Resources With Short-range Interacting Spin-1/2 Chains
authors: Marcin Płodzień And Jan Chwedeńczuk
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień and Jan Chwedeńczuk

The dynamical generation of quantum resources, such as many-body entanglement, Bell correlations, or spin squeezing, can be achieved via one-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics, which require all-to-all couplings. However, current digital and analog quantum simulation platforms natively provide short-range…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062220] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that short-range interacting spin-1/2 chains can generate scalable many-body entanglement and Bell correlations via one-axis twisting dynamics, overcoming the need for all-to-all couplings.
motivation: One-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics generate useful quantum resources but require all-to-all couplings, which are not native to most quantum simulation platforms. The authors aim to achieve similar resource generation using only short-range interactions.
method: The authors analyze spin-1/2 chains with nearest-neighbor interactions and show that by appropriately engineering the initial state and evolution, the dynamics effectively mimic OAT, leading to scalable entanglement and spin squeezing.
result: They demonstrate that short-range interacting chains can produce many-body entanglement, Bell correlations, and spin squeezing that scale with system size, comparable to OAT with all-to-all couplings.
conclusion: Short-range interacting spin chains are a viable platform for generating scalable quantum resources, making them promising for quantum metrology and quantum information processing.

title: Microwave-enabled Continuous-variable Measurement-device-independent Quantum Key Distribution In Free Space
authors: Zhuokuan Jia, Tianai Zhou, Yongxin Feng, And Ying Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Zhuokuan Jia, Tianai Zhou, Yongxin Feng, and Ying Guo

Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) over free-space channels offers more flexibility for secure key exchange between authenticated parties than fiber-based CV-QKD in practical scenarios. However, traditional CV-QKD systems use 1550-nm optical signals as the quantum source, which ar…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062450] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a microwave-enabled continuous-variable measurement-device-independent QKD protocol for free-space channels to overcome atmospheric turbulence and background noise.
motivation: Free-space CV-QKD at 1550 nm suffers from atmospheric turbulence and background noise; using microwave signals can mitigate these issues and enable more robust key distribution.
method: The protocol uses microwave signals as the quantum source, employs continuous-variable encoding, and implements measurement-device-independent detection to eliminate detector side-channel attacks.
result: Simulations show that the microwave-based protocol achieves higher secret key rates and longer transmission distances compared to conventional optical CV-QKD under realistic atmospheric conditions.
conclusion: Microwave-enabled CV-MDI-QKD is a promising approach for practical free-space quantum communication, offering improved resilience to environmental disturbances.

title: Quantum States Supported By Matroids
authors: Xiaowei Huang, Fei Shi, Lijun Zhang, And Lvzhou Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaowei Huang, Fei Shi, Lijun Zhang, and Lvzhou Li

In this work, we establish a structural correspondence between quantum states and matroid theory. This connection demonstrates that key properties of quantum states, including entanglement and measurement, can be characterized in purely combinatorial terms via matroids, despite the apparent conceptu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062452] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a structural correspondence between quantum states and matroid theory, characterizing entanglement and measurement combinatorially.
motivation: To bridge quantum information and matroid theory, providing a combinatorial framework for understanding quantum state properties.
method: Develops a mapping from quantum states to matroids and proves that key properties like entanglement and measurement outcomes correspond to matroid invariants.
result: Demonstrates that entanglement and measurement can be fully characterized by matroid structures, offering new combinatorial tools.
conclusion: Matroid theory provides a powerful language for quantum state analysis, potentially simplifying complex quantum information problems.

title: Control Framework For Broadband Population Transfer In Multilevel Quantum Ensembles With Time-dependent Dispersions
authors: Vishesh Kaushik And Navin Khaneja
abstract:
Author(s): Vishesh Kaushik and Navin Khaneja

We develop a control framework for broadband population transfer in ensembles of [MATH]-level quantum systems with time-dependent energy levels and time-varying dispersion across ensemble members. Ensemble inhomogeneity is modeled through time-varying dispersion functions that capture Hamiltonian varia…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062620] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for broadband population transfer in multilevel quantum ensembles with time-dependent dispersions is developed.
motivation: Ensemble inhomogeneities and time-dependent energy levels hinder efficient population transfer in quantum systems, which is crucial for quantum information processing and sensing.
method: The authors model ensemble inhomogeneity via time-varying dispersion functions and design control pulses using optimal control theory to achieve robust broadband population transfer.
result: The framework demonstrates high-fidelity population transfer across a range of dispersions and time-dependent variations, outperforming standard methods.
conclusion: This work provides a practical control strategy for quantum ensembles with realistic inhomogeneities, applicable to hybrid quantum systems such as spin ensembles coupled to superconducting circuits.

title: Intercavity Phonons And Dynamics In Coupled Polariton Cavities
authors: Iliana Carmona-Moreno, Grover Andrade-Sánchez, Hugo A. Lara-García, Giuseppe Pirruccio, And Arturo Camacho-Guardian
abstract:
Author(s): Iliana Carmona-Moreno, Grover Andrade-Sánchez, Hugo A. Lara-García, Giuseppe Pirruccio, and Arturo Camacho-Guardian

Intercavity polaritons, hybrid quasiparticles with spatially separated photonic and excitonic components, provide a platform to engineer structured light-matter states. We show that resonant driving of the middle polariton branch leads to a qualitatively distinct dynamical regime in which coherent R…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062814] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies intercavity phonons and dynamics in coupled polariton cavities, revealing a regime of coherent Rabi-like oscillations between photonic and phononic modes.
motivation: To understand the role of phonons in coupled polariton cavities and explore new dynamical regimes for engineering structured light-matter states.
method: The authors use a theoretical model of coupled cavities with exciton-phonon interactions, solving the dynamics under resonant driving of the middle polariton branch.
result: They find that resonant driving leads to coherent Rabi-like oscillations between photonic and phononic modes, mediated by the excitonic component.
conclusion: Intercavity phonons can be coherently controlled, offering a new platform for hybrid quantum systems and phonon-mediated interactions.

title: Magnetometry With Broadband Microwave Fields In Nitrogen-vacancy Centers In Diamond
authors: Arezoo Afshar, Andrew Proppe, Noah Lupu-Gladstein, Lilian Childress, Aaron Z. Goldberg, And Khabat Heshami
abstract:
Author(s): Arezoo Afshar, Andrew Proppe, Noah Lupu-Gladstein, Lilian Childress, Aaron Z. Goldberg, and Khabat Heshami

Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are optically addressable and versatile light-matter interfaces with practical application in magnetic-field sensing, offering the ability to operate at room temperature and reach sensitivities below pT/[MATH]. We propose an approach to simultan…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063113] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a magnetometry scheme using broadband microwave fields in NV centers to improve sensitivity and dynamic range.
motivation: NV centers are promising for magnetic field sensing but conventional narrowband microwave excitation limits sensitivity and dynamic range.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a protocol using broadband microwave fields to simultaneously address multiple NV spin transitions, enhancing signal-to-noise ratio.
result: The broadband approach can achieve sub-pT sensitivity and extend the dynamic range compared to standard continuous-wave or pulsed methods.
conclusion: Broadband microwave excitation offers a practical route to improve NV magnetometry performance without complex hardware modifications.

title: Phonon Scattering From Spatial Relaxation Of One-dimensional Bose Gases
authors: Bilal Alilou, Clément Duval, Frederick Del Pozo, And Nicolas Cherroret
abstract:
Author(s): Bilal Alilou, Clément Duval, Frederick Del Pozo, and Nicolas Cherroret

We theoretically investigate the nonequilibrium relaxation of a spatial density modulation in a one-dimensional nonintegrable Bose gas and its connection to the equilibrium scattering rate [MATH] of the system's phononic excitations. We show that the density relaxation is generically go…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063321] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies nonequilibrium relaxation of density modulations in 1D Bose gases and connects it to phonon scattering rates.
motivation: Understanding relaxation dynamics in low-dimensional quantum systems is important for quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium physics.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the relaxation of a spatial density modulation in a nonintegrable 1D Bose gas using a hydrodynamic approach and relate it to the equilibrium phonon scattering rate.
result: They show that the density relaxation is generically governed by the phonon scattering rate, providing a direct link between non-equilibrium dynamics and equilibrium properties.
conclusion: The work establishes a connection between spatial relaxation and phonon scattering, offering insights into thermalization and transport in one-dimensional quantum gases.

title: Temperature-driven False-vacuum Decay In Coherently Coupled Bose Superfluids
authors: Paniyanchatha Moolayil Sivasankar, Franco Dalfovo, Alessio Recati, And Arko Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Paniyanchatha Moolayil Sivasankar, Franco Dalfovo, Alessio Recati, and Arko Roy

The relaxation of a quantum field from a metastable state (false vacuum) to a stable one (true vacuum), also known as false-vacuum decay, is a fundamental problem in quantum field theory and cosmology. We study this phenomenon using a two-dimensional interacting and coherently coupled Bose-Bose mixt…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063323] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies false-vacuum decay in a two-dimensional coherently coupled Bose-Bose mixture, focusing on the role of temperature and thermal fluctuations.
motivation: False-vacuum decay is a fundamental process in quantum field theory and cosmology, but its dynamics in the presence of thermal effects are not well understood.
method: The authors use numerical simulations of the stochastic Gross-Pitaevskii equation to model the finite-temperature dynamics of a two-dimensional Bose-Bose mixture with coherent coupling.
result: They find that temperature enhances the decay rate and modifies the nucleation mechanism, with a crossover from quantum to thermal regime.
conclusion: The work provides insights into non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and the interplay between thermal and quantum fluctuations in metastable systems.

title: Generalized Stochastic Spin-wave Theory For Open Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Zejian Li, Anna Delmonte, And Rosario Fazio
abstract:
Author(s): Zejian Li, Anna Delmonte, and Rosario Fazio

We propose a semiclassical framework for solving open quantum dynamics in driven-dissipative spin systems. Our method consists of generalized spin-wave approximations tailored to describing quantum trajectories unraveled from the master equation, and it generically applies to regimes beyond the reac…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214324] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: A semiclassical framework for open quantum spin systems using generalized spin-wave theory and quantum trajectories.
motivation: To efficiently simulate driven-dissipative spin systems beyond the reaction coordinate method.
method: Generalized spin-wave approximations applied to quantum trajectories from the master equation.
result: The method accurately captures dissipative dynamics in regimes where standard approaches fail.
conclusion: Provides a scalable semiclassical tool for open quantum spin systems, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium physics.

title: Dynamics Of Majorana Fermions On A Quantum Computer
authors: Yuxiao Hang, Rosa Di Felice, Aiichiro Nakano, And Stephan Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Yuxiao Hang, Rosa Di Felice, Aiichiro Nakano, and Stephan Haas

The study of quasiparticle dynamics is central to understanding nonequilibrium phenomena in quantum many-body systems. Direct simulation of such dynamics on quantum hardware has been limited by circuit depth and noise constraints. In this work, we use a recently developed constant-depth circuit algo…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235145] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Simulates Majorana fermion dynamics on a quantum computer using a constant-depth circuit algorithm.
motivation: Understanding quasiparticle dynamics in quantum many-body systems is central to nonequilibrium phenomena, but direct simulation on quantum hardware is limited by circuit depth and noise.
method: Uses a recently developed constant-depth circuit algorithm to simulate the dynamics of Majorana fermions on a quantum computer.
result: Demonstrates that the constant-depth approach enables simulation of Majorana dynamics within current quantum hardware constraints.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method for studying quasiparticle dynamics on near-term quantum devices, advancing hybrid quantum-classical simulation.

title: Revisiting The Ratchet Principle: Lessons From Active And Passive Stochastic Dynamics
authors: Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, and Julien Tailleur

The “ratchet principle” identifies the violation of parity and time-reversal symmetries as necessary for the emergence of steady-state directed currents. When all such symmetries are violated, one generically expects the emergence of currents. We study stochastic systems in the presence of asymmetri…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064152] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper revisits the ratchet principle in stochastic systems, showing that directed currents can emerge even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are preserved, through active or passive asymmetric potentials.
motivation: To clarify the necessary conditions for directed transport in stochastic systems, challenging the traditional ratchet principle that requires violation of both parity and time-reversal symmetries.
method: The authors study stochastic dynamics with asymmetric potentials, both active (self-propelled particles) and passive (Brownian particles), using analytical and numerical methods to compute steady-state currents.
result: They demonstrate that directed currents can arise even when all symmetries are preserved, provided the system is out of equilibrium due to activity or non-conservative forces, thus refining the ratchet principle.
conclusion: The ratchet principle must be extended to account for non-equilibrium driving beyond symmetry breaking; active matter and asymmetric potentials provide new routes to directed transport.

title: Accuracy Comes At A Cost: Optimal Localization Against A Flow
authors: Till Welker And Patrick Pietzonka
abstract:
Author(s): Till Welker and Patrick Pietzonka

How can a small swimmer stay close to a target, while struggling against a flow and also being hit by the water molecules around it? The authors investigate this question in a simple setup, and find that the optimal navigation strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming with a trade-off between cost and accuracy.


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064142] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Optimal navigation of a small swimmer in a flow with thermal noise involves a trade-off between accuracy and thermodynamic cost.
motivation: Understanding how microscopic swimmers can localize near a target despite environmental noise and flow is relevant to active matter and biological systems.
method: The authors model a swimmer with active control in a stochastic environment and derive optimal strategies using stochastic optimal control theory.
result: The optimal strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming, with accuracy limited by the thermodynamic cost of control.
conclusion: There is a fundamental trade-off between localization accuracy and energy dissipation, linking information thermodynamics to active matter.

title: Dynamical Typicality In Classical Lattice Systems
authors: Nicolas Nessi And Peter Reimann
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Nessi and Peter Reimann

Considering deterministic classical lattice systems with continuous dynamical variables, we show that, if the initial conditions are sampled according to a probability distribution in which the dynamical variables are statistically independent, the temporal evolution of any macroscopic observable is…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064138] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves dynamical typicality for classical lattice systems with continuous variables, showing that macroscopic observables evolve typically under independent initial conditions.
motivation: Understanding the emergence of thermodynamic behavior from microscopic dynamics is a fundamental question in statistical mechanics, and dynamical typicality provides a rigorous framework for this.
method: The authors consider deterministic classical lattice systems with continuous dynamical variables and sample initial conditions from a product distribution. They then analyze the temporal evolution of macroscopic observables using mathematical techniques from dynamical systems and probability theory.
result: They show that for any macroscopic observable, its time evolution is typical (i.e., close to the ensemble average) for most initial conditions, with deviations that vanish in the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: This work extends dynamical typicality results to classical lattice systems, reinforcing the idea that typicality is a general mechanism for the emergence of thermodynamic behavior, and has implications for the foundations of statistical mechanics.

title: Diffusion In Quantum State Preparation: From Passive Cooling To System-bath Engineering
authors: Tim Pokart, Lukas König, Sebastian Diehl, And Jan Carl Budich
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Pokart, Lukas König, Sebastian Diehl, and Jan Carl Budich

We investigate and compare two particle number-conserving protocols for the preparation of a topologically nontrivial state. The first is derived from thermally coupling the system to a cold bath, while the second is based on engineered dissipation. We numerically study the time required to reach th…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023336] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Compares passive thermal cooling and engineered dissipation for preparing a topologically nontrivial state, focusing on preparation time and fidelity.
motivation: Efficient preparation of topological states is crucial for quantum technologies; understanding the thermodynamic cost and speed limits of state preparation is of interest.
method: Numerical simulation of two particle number-conserving protocols: one coupling the system to a cold bath, the other using engineered dissipation.
result: Engineered dissipation can achieve faster preparation times compared to passive cooling, with trade-offs in fidelity.
conclusion: System-bath engineering offers a practical advantage for preparing topological states, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Casimir-Polder Potential On An Excited Atom Near An Atomic Array
authors: Annyun Das And Kanu Sinha
abstract:
Author(s): Annyun Das and Kanu Sinha

We develop a microscopic description of the fluctuation-mediated Casimir-Polder (CP) shifts on a “test” two-level atom placed near a two-dimensional atomic array of two-level atoms. We derive the resonant and off-resonant CP potentials experienced by the excited test atom using fourth-order perturba…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023339] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a microscopic theory of Casimir-Polder potentials on an excited atom near a 2D atomic array, using fourth-order perturbation theory.
motivation: Understanding fluctuation-mediated interactions between quantum emitters and structured atomic arrays is important for hybrid quantum systems and quantum networks.
method: The authors use fourth-order perturbation theory to derive resonant and off-resonant Casimir-Polder potentials for an excited test atom near a two-dimensional atomic array of two-level atoms.
result: They obtain expressions for the CP potential that depend on the array geometry and atomic properties, showing both resonant and off-resonant contributions.
conclusion: The work provides a microscopic description of CP interactions in atomic arrays, which can be used to engineer atom-surface interactions for quantum technologies.

title: Emergence Of A Luttinger Liquid Phase In An Array Of Chiral Molecules
authors: Muhammad Arsalan Ali Akbar, Bretislav Friedrich, And Sabre Kais
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Arsalan Ali Akbar, Bretislav Friedrich, and Sabre Kais

We propose a robust platform for simulating chiral quantum magnetism using linear arrays of trapped asymmetric-top molecules, specifically 1,2-propanediol ([MATH]). By mapping the Stark-dressed rotational states onto an effective spin-[MATH] subspace, we ri…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023340] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Proposes using trapped chiral molecules to simulate a Luttinger liquid phase, leveraging molecular quantum control.
motivation: To realize a robust platform for simulating chiral quantum magnetism and Luttinger liquid physics using molecular qubits.
method: Maps Stark-dressed rotational states of asymmetric-top molecules (1,2-propanediol) onto an effective spin-1/2 subspace and arranges them in a linear array.
result: Demonstrates that the system can emulate a Luttinger liquid phase with tunable interactions.
conclusion: Trapped chiral molecules offer a promising hybrid quantum platform for studying quantum magnetism and one-dimensional physics.

title: Rotation Sensor Based On An Atom-cavity System
authors: Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, And Ludwig Mathey
abstract:
Author(s): Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, and Ludwig Mathey

A transversely pumped atom-cavity system operating near a critical transition is proposed as a rotation sensor. The cavity-emitted light serves as a probe for changes in rotation frequency, with a sensitivity that scales with the area enclosed by the atomic array.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022057] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an atom-cavity system as a rotation sensor with sensitivity scaling with enclosed area.
motivation: Develop a quantum rotation sensor using a transversely pumped atom-cavity system operating near a critical transition.
method: The cavity-emitted light serves as a probe for changes in rotation frequency; the system exploits critical behavior for enhanced sensitivity.
result: Sensitivity scales with the area enclosed by the atomic array, demonstrating a quantum sensing application.
conclusion: The atom-cavity system provides a viable platform for rotation sensing with potential advantages over classical sensors.

title: Quantum Dynamical Signatures Of Topological Flow Transitions In Limit Cycle Phases
authors: Alejandro S. Gómez And Javier Del Pino
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro S. Gómez and Javier del Pino

Quantum self-oscillatory phases are ubiquitous in driven-dissipative systems. Classically, each phase is defined by its flow pattern and how stationary sets organize phase space (e.g., fixed points and limit cycles), with transitions triggered by local bifurcations or global basin rearrangements. In…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023319] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum signatures of topological flow transitions in limit cycle phases of driven-dissipative systems, linking classical bifurcations to quantum observables.
motivation: Understanding how classical topological transitions in phase space manifest in quantum systems is crucial for characterizing driven-dissipative phases and their stability.
method: The authors analyze a quantum van der Pol oscillator model using semiclassical methods and full quantum simulations, identifying topological changes in the Wigner function and quantum fluctuations.
result: They find that topological flow transitions (e.g., from fixed point to limit cycle) are accompanied by distinct quantum dynamical signatures, such as changes in the Wigner function topology and enhanced quantum fluctuations near the transition.
conclusion: Quantum systems can exhibit clear signatures of classical topological transitions, providing a framework to classify and detect non-equilibrium phases in quantum optics and condensed matter.

title: Memory-enhanced Quantum Extreme Learning Machines For Characterizing non-Markovian Dynamics
authors: Hajar Assil, Abderrahim El Allati, And Gian Luca Giorgi
abstract:
Author(s): Hajar Assil, Abderrahim El Allati, and Gian Luca Giorgi

We use a quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) for characterizing and estimating parameters of quantum dynamics generated by a tunable collision model. The input to the learning protocol consists of quantum states produced by successive system-environment interactions, while the reservoir is imple…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023306] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses a quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) with memory to characterize non-Markovian dynamics in a collision model, demonstrating parameter estimation and detection of non-Markovianity.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are important in quantum systems but challenging to characterize; machine learning offers a data-driven approach to extract parameters and detect memory effects.
method: A QELM is implemented with a reservoir of qubits that interact sequentially with system states, incorporating memory via a feedback loop; the reservoir's output is used to train a linear readout for parameter estimation.
result: The QELM successfully estimates system-environment coupling strengths and discriminates between Markovian and non-Markovian regimes, with high accuracy even for limited training data.
conclusion: Memory-enhanced QELMs are effective tools for characterizing non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with potential applications in quantum metrology and open quantum system control.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A review of the process tensor framework for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics using tensor-network methods.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for understanding open quantum systems, but their simulation is computationally challenging. The process tensor provides a systematic way to capture memory effects.
method: The paper reviews the process tensor formalism and demonstrates how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product operators) enable efficient simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The framework is applied to various physical systems, showing that tensor-network methods can handle long memory times and strong system-bath couplings that are intractable with standard approaches.
conclusion: The process tensor approach, combined with tensor networks, offers a powerful and practical tool for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse fields.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which are central to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise identities and establishing a continuum limit that bridges jump and diffusion processes.
result: Achieves a unification of previously disjoint theories, enabling consistent treatment of observables like work and heat in both jump and diffusion settings.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for studying thermodynamic quantities in stochastic systems, with implications for non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensates, through phase transitions, can process high-dimensional environmental information, linking phase separation to cellular computation.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals, but traditional molecular circuits may be insufficient; phase transitions offer a collective, thermodynamic mechanism for information processing.
method: The authors present a conceptual framework drawing on phase separation, condensation, and information theory, supported by examples from cell biology and physical principles.
result: They argue that phase transitions enable cells to classify and respond to multiple signals simultaneously, effectively performing high-dimensional computations.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation provides a novel, physically-grounded paradigm for cellular information processing, with implications for understanding biological computation and designing synthetic systems.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: Simulating quantum field dynamics is computationally challenging; photonic platforms offer scalability and programmability.
method: Decomposes quantum field dynamics into sequences of standard optical elements (e.g., beam splitters, phase shifters) to build a configurable photonic circuit.
result: Demonstrates efficient simulation of a class of quantum field theories with high configurability and low resource overhead.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical path toward photonic quantum simulation of field theories, relevant for hybrid quantum systems.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
