tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits at finite depths, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Understanding anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits is crucial for assessing the computational power of near-term quantum devices and for quantum supremacy experiments.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework using statistical mechanics mappings and replica methods to analyze the output distribution of random circuits under noise.
result: They identify distinct regimes based on circuit depth and noise strength, showing that anticoncentration persists up to a certain depth threshold and is universal across different circuit architectures.
conclusion: The findings provide a universal characterization of noisy quantum circuit behavior, with implications for quantum advantage and error mitigation strategies.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints and the need for efficient dilation methods.
method: The paper introduces a dilation approach that uses a tight-binding lattice as an ancillary system, matching moments of the target evolution to achieve high-fidelity simulation with minimal ancilla qubits.
result: The framework achieves near-optimal query complexity and circuit depth for simulating linear differential equations, outperforming previous methods.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient pathway for quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, with implications for quantum algorithms in differential equations and open systems.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubits is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise cross-correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible frequency range.
result: They successfully demonstrate the method on a qubit platform, revealing noise cross-correlations that were previously unobservable.
conclusion: This technique provides a new tool for noise characterization in quantum devices, aiding in the development of more coherent qubits.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires fault-tolerant architectures that minimize space and time overhead, especially for neutral-atom platforms where native gates and error correction are still developing.
method: The authors design a transversal architecture that combines small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate quantum error-correcting codes, optimized for neutral-atom hardware constraints such as long-range interactions and parallel gate operations.
result: The architecture achieves significant savings in logical qubit count, physical qubit overhead, and runtime compared to conventional approaches, enabling megaquop-scale simulations with realistic hardware parameters.
conclusion: The proposed transversal architecture makes neutral-atom quantum computers a viable platform for large-scale quantum simulation, bridging the gap between current hardware and practical applications.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing bounds on loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus where gradients vanish, hindering trainability. Understanding how noise affects loss landscapes is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on the concentration of loss functions in noisy parametrized quantum circuits using tools from random matrix theory and quantum information theory.
result: They show that noise can actually help avoid barren plateaus by reducing the effective expressivity of the circuit, leading to more concentrated loss functions that are easier to optimize.
conclusion: The results provide a principled guide for designing noise-resilient variational algorithms and suggest that moderate noise can be beneficial for trainability.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems in quantum technologies, but the diversity of simulation methods makes it hard to compare and choose appropriate techniques.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and review various numerical and analytical methods including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The review systematically compares methods, highlighting their strengths, limitations, and regimes of applicability, and provides guidance for selecting methods based on system parameters.
conclusion: The unified framework clarifies relationships between different approaches and serves as a practical guide for researchers simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium surveying the use of qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in gate count and circuit depth.
motivation: Qubits are standard for quantum computing, but qudits can reduce resource requirements for certain gates and algorithms, motivating a systematic review of their potential.
method: The paper reviews theoretical embeddings of qudits into qubit systems, decomposition techniques for multiqubit gates (e.g., Toffoli gate using qutrits), and surveys experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits enable more efficient decompositions of key gates like Toffoli, reducing circuit depth and potentially improving fidelity; experimental demonstrations exist in trapped ions, superconducting circuits, and photonics.
conclusion: Qudits offer a promising resource for quantum computing, especially for near-term devices, but challenges in control and error correction remain.

title: Dissipative Phase Transition Of Interacting Nonreciprocal Fermions
authors: Rafael D. Soares, Matteo Brunelli, And Marco Schirò
abstract:
Author(s): Rafael D. Soares, Matteo Brunelli, and Marco Schirò

While nonreciprocal couplings are ubiquitous in classical systems, their impact on quantum many-body criticality and entanglement remains largely unexplored. Using exact numerical simulations, we study an interacting fermionic chain subject to nonreciprocal gain and loss. We show that the interplay …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250403] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a dissipative phase transition in an interacting fermionic chain with nonreciprocal gain and loss, focusing on criticality and entanglement.
motivation: Nonreciprocal couplings are common in classical systems but their impact on quantum many-body criticality and entanglement is largely unexplored.
method: Exact numerical simulations of an interacting fermionic chain with nonreciprocal gain and loss.
result: The interplay of nonreciprocity and interactions leads to a dissipative phase transition with distinct entanglement properties.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal couplings can fundamentally alter quantum critical behavior and entanglement, opening new directions in open quantum systems.

title: Efficient Circuit Compression By Multiqudit Entangling Gates In Linear Optical Quantum Computation
authors: Apurav Tehri And Jaskaran Singh
abstract:
Author(s): Apurav Tehri and Jaskaran Singh

Linear optical quantum computation (LOQC) offers a promising platform for quantum information processing, but its scalability is fundamentally constrained by the probabilistic nature of nonlocal entangling gates. Qudit circuit compression schemes mitigate this issue by encoding multiple qubits onto …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062622] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a circuit compression scheme using multiqudit entangling gates to reduce resource overhead in linear optical quantum computation.
motivation: Linear optical quantum computation suffers from probabilistic entangling gates, limiting scalability; qudit encoding can reduce the number of required operations.
method: The authors design multiqudit entangling gates that operate on qudits encoding multiple qubits, and analyze their effect on circuit depth and gate count.
result: The scheme achieves significant reduction in circuit complexity compared to qubit-based approaches, though with increased qudit dimension requirements.
conclusion: Multiqudit entangling gates offer a viable path to more efficient LOQC, but practical implementation challenges remain.

title: Hexapartite Active Nonlinear Feedback Control In Four-wave Mixing With A Spatially Structured Pump
authors: Guanjun Zeng, Xiaozhou Pan, Kai Zhang, And Jietai Jing
abstract:
Author(s): Guanjun Zeng, Xiaozhou Pan, Kai Zhang, and Jietai Jing

In the field of quantum information science, feedback control has become an important method for preparing and manipulating nonclassical beams. Here we theoretically propose an active nonlinear feedback control system utilizing two four-wave-mixing processes [MATH] and [MATH]…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062448] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an active nonlinear feedback control system using two four-wave-mixing processes with a spatially structured pump for preparing and manipulating nonclassical beams.
motivation: Feedback control is important for preparing and manipulating nonclassical beams in quantum information science.
method: The authors theoretically design a system with two four-wave-mixing processes and a spatially structured pump to achieve active nonlinear feedback control.
result: The system enables control over nonclassical beams, though specific performance metrics are not detailed in the abstract.
conclusion: The proposed feedback control scheme may enhance the preparation and manipulation of nonclassical states.

title: Identifying The Three-qubit $w$ State With The Quantum Uncertainty Relation
authors: Zhi-Jie Liu, Hao-Nan Qiang, Jie Zhou, Mi Xie, And Jing-Ling Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Jie Liu, Hao-Nan Qiang, Jie Zhou, Mi Xie, and Jing-Ling Chen

The [MATH] state, a canonical representative of multipartite quantum entanglement, plays a crucial role in quantum information science due to its robust entanglement properties. Quantum uncertainty relations, on the other hand, form a fundamental cornerstone of quantum mechanics. This work introduces a…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062451] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum uncertainty relations to identify the three-qubit W state, a canonical entangled state.
motivation: The W state is important for quantum information tasks, and uncertainty relations provide a fundamental tool for characterizing quantum states.
method: The authors derive an uncertainty relation based on mutually unbiased bases and show that the W state saturates it uniquely.
result: They prove that the W state is the only three-qubit pure state achieving the bound of the derived uncertainty relation.
conclusion: The uncertainty relation serves as a witness for the W state, offering a new way to identify this class of entanglement.

title: Anomalous Quantum Relaxation In The Infinite-temperature Hubbard Chain
authors: Cătălin Paşcu Moca And Balázs Dóra
abstract:
Author(s): Cătălin Paşcu Moca and Balázs Dóra

The self-energy encodes the fundamental lifetime of quasiparticle excitations. In one dimension, it is known to display anomalous behavior at zero temperature for interacting fermions, reflecting the breakdown of Fermi-liquid theory. Here we show that the self-energy is also anomalous in the infinit…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241120] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that the self-energy in the infinite-temperature Hubbard chain exhibits anomalous relaxation, indicating non-Fermi-liquid behavior even at high temperatures.
motivation: Understanding quasiparticle lifetimes in one-dimensional interacting fermion systems is fundamental, and anomalous behavior at zero temperature is known; this work extends the study to infinite temperature.
method: The authors compute the self-energy analytically and numerically for the Hubbard model in one dimension at infinite temperature using Bethe ansatz and other techniques.
result: They find that the self-energy decays as a power law in frequency, with an exponent that depends on interaction strength, signaling anomalous relaxation.
conclusion: The infinite-temperature Hubbard chain exhibits non-Fermi-liquid behavior, suggesting that anomalous relaxation is a generic feature of one-dimensional interacting systems.

title: Scaling And Universality At Noise-affected Nonequilibrium Spin Correlation Functions
authors: R. Jafari And Alireza Akbari
abstract:
Author(s): R. Jafari and Alireza Akbari

We investigate the scaling and universality of the asymptotic behavior of nonequilibrium spin correlation functions in the presence of uncorrelated noise. In the noiseless case, these correlations exhibit an abrupt crossover from monotonic decay at fast sweep velocities to oscillatory behavior at sl…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220302] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies scaling and universality in nonequilibrium spin correlation functions under noise, focusing on a crossover from monotonic to oscillatory decay.
motivation: Understanding how noise affects nonequilibrium dynamics and universal scaling in quantum many-body systems is important for characterizing decoherence and thermalization.
method: The authors analyze the asymptotic behavior of spin correlation functions in the presence of uncorrelated noise, likely using analytical or numerical techniques to extract scaling exponents and crossover behavior.
result: They find that noise modifies the scaling and universality of the correlation functions, leading to a crossover between different dynamical regimes.
conclusion: The results provide insight into the robustness of universal nonequilibrium scaling in open quantum systems, but the paper does not directly address thermodynamic constraints or information-theoretic aspects.

title: Giant Magnetoelasticity In FeRh Thin Films Evidenced Via Strong Phonon-magnon Coupling
authors: D. Ourdani, C. Gourdon, J. A. Arregi, V. Uhlíř, Y. Roussigné, And L. Thevenard
abstract:
Author(s): D. Ourdani, C. Gourdon, J. A. Arregi, V. Uhlíř, Y. Roussigné, and L. Thevenard

FeRh is best known for its metamagnetic transition and giant volume magnetostriction. Here, the authors reveal remarkably strong phonon–magnon coupling in epitaxial FeRh. Combining Brillouin light scattering experiments with magnetoacoustic modeling, they demonstrate giant magnetoelasticity and show that Love surface acoustic waves provide an efficient mechanism for coherent magnon-polaron formation in magnetic thin films, highlighting FeRh as a promising platform for spin-acoustic information processing.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214450] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates giant magnetoelasticity and strong phonon-magnon coupling in FeRh thin films, proposing them as a platform for spin-acoustic information processing.
motivation: FeRh exhibits a metamagnetic transition and giant volume magnetostriction, but its phonon-magnon coupling had not been explored. Understanding this coupling could enable new hybrid quantum systems for information processing.
method: The authors combine Brillouin light scattering experiments with magnetoacoustic modeling to study phonon-magnon coupling in epitaxial FeRh thin films, focusing on Love surface acoustic waves.
result: They observe remarkably strong phonon-magnon coupling and giant magnetoelasticity, demonstrating that Love surface acoustic waves efficiently form coherent magnon-polarons.
conclusion: FeRh is a promising platform for spin-acoustic information processing, leveraging strong magnetoelastic coupling for hybrid quantum systems.

title: Magnetoelastic Signatures Of Thermal And Quantum Phase Transitions In A Deformable Ising Chain Under A Longitudinal And Transverse Magnetic Field
authors: Dávid Sivý And Jozef Strečka
abstract:
Author(s): Dávid Sivý and Jozef Strečka

We investigate a deformable spin-1/2 Ising chain subjected to either a longitudinal or a transverse magnetic field, which incorporates a magnetoelastic coupling linearly dependent on a lattice distortion parameter. Within the harmonic and static adiabatic approximations, the variational Gibbs free e…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064146] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies magnetoelastic signatures of thermal and quantum phase transitions in a deformable Ising chain under magnetic fields.
motivation: To understand how magnetoelastic coupling affects phase transitions in low-dimensional spin systems.
method: Variational Gibbs free energy minimization within harmonic and static adiabatic approximations.
result: Identifies magnetoelastic signatures that distinguish thermal and quantum phase transitions.
conclusion: Magnetoelastic coupling provides a sensitive probe of phase transitions in deformable spin chains.

title: Optimal Parametric Control Of Transport Across A Josephson Junction
authors: Hannah Kleine-Pollmann, Guido Homann, And Ludwig Mathey
abstract:
Author(s): Hannah Kleine-Pollmann, Guido Homann, and Ludwig Mathey

We present optimal control strategies for the dc transport across a Josephson junction. Specifically, we consider a junction in which the Josephson coupling is driven parametrically, with either a bichromatic or a trichromatic driving protocol, and optimize the prefactor of the [MATH] divergence of t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023313] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Optimal parametric control of dc transport across a Josephson junction using bichromatic and trichromatic driving to enhance the supercurrent divergence.
motivation: To achieve high dc currents in Josephson junctions by optimizing parametric driving protocols, which is relevant for quantum device performance.
method: The authors apply optimal control theory to bichromatic and trichromatic driving of the Josephson coupling, optimizing the prefactor of the current divergence.
result: They find optimal driving parameters that significantly enhance the dc supercurrent compared to standard monochromatic driving.
conclusion: Parametric control can substantially improve transport in Josephson junctions, with potential applications in quantum circuits and metrology.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces non-Gaussian control parameters to systematically optimize generation of non-Gaussian quantum states, increasing success rates by orders of magnitude.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum information processing but their generation is inefficient; this work aims to improve success rates through systematic optimization.
method: The authors propose new control parameters beyond stellar rank and develop a method to optimize the generation process using these parameters.
result: The new parameters enable orders-of-magnitude improvement in the success rate of generating non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: This approach provides a scalable path to generating non-Gaussian states, which is important for quantum information applications.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level
authors: Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, And Andrea F. Young
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, and Andrea F. Young

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity to isolate topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: Understanding entropy in strongly correlated electron systems, particularly in fractional quantum Hall states, is crucial for characterizing topological order and non-Abelian anyons.
method: Experimental entropy measurements using a graphene-based device in a partially filled Landau level, combined with thermodynamic analysis.
result: Successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom is observed, and the sensitivity approaches the level needed to isolate topological entropy.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a path toward measuring topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases, but the focus is on condensed matter physics rather than information thermodynamics.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient classical surrogate for small subregions of quantum expectation landscapes, using initial quantum data.
motivation: Classically simulating quantum circuits is hard, but for small patches of the landscape, efficient surrogates may exist, enabling hybrid quantum-classical optimization.
method: The authors develop a method to classically surrogate a subregion of an expectation landscape by leveraging initial quantum measurements and classical machine learning.
result: They demonstrate that the surrogate can accurately predict expectation values for nearby points, reducing the need for many quantum evaluations.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical way to accelerate variational quantum algorithms by reducing quantum resource requirements.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents symmetry-accelerated classical simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits using optimal stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is important for benchmarking and understanding quantum advantage; Clifford-dominated circuits are particularly challenging.
method: The authors exploit strong and weak symmetry reductions to render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries.
result: They achieve efficient classical simulation of circuits that are dominated by Clifford gates but include non-Clifford elements.
conclusion: Symmetry reduction significantly extends the reach of stabilizer-based simulation methods.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for high-precision sensing.
method: Reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling of quantum Fisher information near critical points.
result: Demonstrates how criticality can be exploited to achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling in parameter estimation.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing provides a promising route for surpassing classical limits, but practical challenges remain.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A multiproduct commutation relation reduces T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation.
motivation: Reducing T-count is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, as T gates are costly.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial commutation relation for multiproducts of Pauli operators and apply it to sequential Pauli-based circuits.
result: The relation enables significant reduction in the number of T gates required for certain quantum circuits.
conclusion: This work provides a new technique for T-count reduction, contributing to more efficient fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Abelian Multi-Cycle Codes For Single-Shot Error Correction
authors: Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, And Leonid P. Pryadko
abstract:
Author(s): Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, and Leonid P. Pryadko

A new family of quantum low-density parity-check codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, achieves single-shot fault tolerance and an approximately 1.1% pseudothreshold with significantly shorter block lengths.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020326] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A new family of quantum LDPC codes achieving single-shot fault tolerance with shorter block lengths.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction typically requires many rounds of syndrome measurement; single-shot error correction reduces this overhead.
method: The authors construct Abelian multi-cycle codes that are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes and analyze their single-shot error correction properties.
result: The codes achieve a pseudothreshold of approximately 1.1% with significantly shorter block lengths than previous constructions.
conclusion: These codes offer a practical advantage for fault-tolerant quantum computing by reducing the number of syndrome measurement rounds needed.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme for parallel logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes using code surgery without additional code blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel measurement is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially for protecting quantum memories during computation.
method: The scheme leverages code surgery techniques on quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes to perform multiple logical measurements simultaneously while preserving code properties.
result: The method enables parallel measurements without requiring extra code blocks, maintaining the code's distance and other properties.
conclusion: This work advances practical fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling efficient parallel logical operations on LDPC codes.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining how violations arise from violated assumptions in measurement.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements exceed them; understanding why is important for developing materials with extreme properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide range of examples from different fields where measured properties exceed thermodynamic bounds, and analyzes which underlying assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated.
result: It identifies common mechanisms for apparent violations, such as non-equilibrium conditions, anisotropy, or hierarchical structures, and shows how these can be exploited to design materials with enhanced properties.
conclusion: Apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds are not actual violations but arise from misapplied assumptions; this understanding can guide the design of materials with superior performance.

title: Continuous Time Crystals As A $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$ Symmetric State And The Emergence Of Critical Exceptional Points
authors: Yuma Nakanishi, Ryo Hanai, And Tomohiro Sasamoto
abstract:
Author(s): Yuma Nakanishi, Ryo Hanai, and Tomohiro Sasamoto

Continuous time-translation symmetry is often spontaneously broken in open quantum systems, and the condition for their emergence has been actively investigated. However, there are only a few cases in which its condition for appearance has been fully elucidated. In this Letter, we show that a Lindbl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250404] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that continuous time crystals in open quantum systems can be understood as PT-symmetric states, with critical exceptional points marking the phase boundary.
motivation: Continuous time-translation symmetry breaking in open quantum systems is not fully understood; the authors aim to clarify the condition for its emergence using PT symmetry.
method: They analyze a Lindblad master equation for a driven-dissipative system and map the steady state to a PT-symmetric non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, identifying exceptional points.
result: The continuous time crystal phase corresponds to a PT-symmetric state, and the phase transition occurs at exceptional points where PT symmetry is broken.
conclusion: PT symmetry provides a unifying framework for continuous time crystals, and exceptional points govern the critical behavior.

title: Crystalline Spectral Form Factors
authors: Dmitrii A. Trunin And David A. Huse
abstract:
Author(s): Dmitrii A. Trunin and David A. Huse

We investigate crystallinelike behavior of the spectral form factor in unitary quantum systems with extremely strong eigenvalue repulsion. Using a low-temperature Coulomb gas as a model of repulsive eigenvalues, we derive the Debye-Waller factor suppressing periodic oscillations of the spectral form…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250405] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies crystalline spectral form factors in quantum systems with strong eigenvalue repulsion, using a Coulomb gas model to derive a Debye-Waller factor that suppresses periodic oscillations.
motivation: To understand the behavior of spectral form factors in systems with extremely strong level repulsion, which is relevant to quantum chaos and thermalization.
method: The authors model eigenvalue repulsion using a low-temperature Coulomb gas and compute the spectral form factor analytically, identifying a Debye-Waller factor that suppresses oscillations.
result: They find that the spectral form factor exhibits a crystalline behavior with suppressed oscillations, analogous to the Debye-Waller effect in solids.
conclusion: The work provides a new perspective on spectral statistics in strongly repulsive systems, linking quantum chaos to solid-state physics concepts.

title: Superbunching From Coherently Driven Atoms In A Waveguide
authors: Zeidan Zeidan, Therese Karmstrand, Maryam Khanahmadi, And Göran Johansson
abstract:
Author(s): Zeidan Zeidan, Therese Karmstrand, Maryam Khanahmadi, and Göran Johansson

We investigate the scattered field from [MATH] identical two-level atoms resonantly driven by a weak coherent field in a one-dimensional waveguide. For atoms separated by the drive wavelength, increasing the number of atoms suppresses transmission while enhancing photon bunching. Transmission becomes a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250803] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies superbunching in the scattered field from coherently driven atoms in a waveguide, showing enhanced photon correlations with increasing atom number.
motivation: Understanding photon statistics from atomic ensembles in waveguides is important for quantum optics and potential applications in quantum information.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the scattered field from N identical two-level atoms driven by a weak coherent field in a 1D waveguide, using a master equation or input-output formalism.
result: They find that increasing the number of atoms suppresses transmission and enhances photon bunching, leading to superbunching effects.
conclusion: The work provides insights into collective atomic effects on photon statistics, relevant for quantum optics and waveguide QED.

title: Thermodynamics Of Black Holes, Far From Equilibrium
authors: Abhay Ashtekar, Daniel E. Paraizo, And Jonathan Shu
abstract:
Author(s): Abhay Ashtekar, Daniel E. Paraizo, and Jonathan Shu

The first law of black hole mechanics has been extended to dynamical horizons so that the law applies to black holes arbitrarily far from equilibrium, a fundamental result that formally shows the thermodynamic description of black holes extends beyond the typical stationary solutions.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251405] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Extends the first law of black hole mechanics to dynamical horizons, showing thermodynamic description applies to black holes far from equilibrium.
motivation: To generalize black hole thermodynamics beyond stationary solutions and understand far-from-equilibrium behavior.
method: Theoretical derivation using dynamical horizon formalism and geometric analysis.
result: First law of black hole mechanics holds for dynamical horizons, establishing thermodynamic properties for non-equilibrium black holes.
conclusion: Black hole thermodynamics is valid even far from equilibrium, broadening its applicability.

title: Protection Of Quantum Steering Ellipsoids In non-Markovian Environments
authors: Wen-Jie Zhang And Jun-Hong An
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Jie Zhang and Jun-Hong An

Quantum steering ellipsoids (QSEs) provide a geometric representation, within the Bloch picture, of all possible states to which one qubit can be steered through measuring another correlated qubit. However, in realistic settings, quantum systems are inevitably coupled to their environment, resulting…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062458] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the protection of quantum steering ellipsoids from decoherence using non-Markovian environments.
motivation: Quantum steering ellipsoids provide a geometric representation of steerable states, but decoherence degrades them; understanding protection mechanisms is important for quantum information tasks.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of quantum steering ellipsoids under non-Markovian noise, using master equations and geometric measures.
result: They find that non-Markovian environments can preserve steering ellipsoid volume and shape better than Markovian ones, depending on the noise spectrum.
conclusion: Non-Markovian effects can be harnessed to protect quantum steering correlations, which may benefit quantum communication protocols.

title: Accelerated Spin-adapted Ground-state Preparation With Nonvariational Quantum Algorithms
authors: Takumi Kobori, Taichi Kosugi, Hirofumi Nishi, Synge Todo, And Yu-Ichiro Matsushita
abstract:
Author(s): Takumi Kobori, Taichi Kosugi, Hirofumi Nishi, Synge Todo, and Yu-ichiro Matsushita

Various methods have been explored to prepare the spin-adapted ground state—the lowest energy state within the Hilbert space constrained by externally specified values of the total spin magnitude and the spin-[MATH] component. In such problem settings, nonvariational methods incorporate penalty terms i…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062454] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A nonvariational quantum algorithm for preparing spin-adapted ground states using penalty terms and quantum phase estimation.
motivation: Preparing ground states with specific spin symmetry is important for quantum chemistry and condensed matter, but variational methods can be inefficient.
method: The authors propose a nonvariational approach combining penalty terms to enforce spin constraints with quantum phase estimation to project onto the ground state.
result: The method accelerates ground-state preparation compared to standard variational algorithms, demonstrated on small molecular systems.
conclusion: Nonvariational quantum algorithms can efficiently prepare spin-adapted ground states, offering a practical advantage for near-term quantum devices.

title: Proposals For Realizing A Josephson Diode In Atomtronic Circuits
authors: Nalinikanta Pradhan, Rina Kanamoto, M. Bhattacharya, And Pankaj Kumar Mishra
abstract:
Author(s): Nalinikanta Pradhan, Rina Kanamoto, M. Bhattacharya, and Pankaj Kumar Mishra

Nonreciprocal Josephson transport is realized in an atomtronic ring condensate through tunable symmetry breaking induced by asymmetric junction placement and driving. The resulting Josephson diode effect achieves efficiencies up to 91%, providing a highly controllable neutral-atom platform for future quantum circuitry and atomtronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061502] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a Josephson diode in atomtronic circuits using asymmetric junction placement and driving to achieve nonreciprocal transport with up to 91% efficiency.
motivation: To realize a highly controllable neutral-atom platform for quantum circuitry and atomtronic devices by demonstrating a Josephson diode effect.
method: Theoretical proposal using a ring condensate with tunable symmetry breaking via asymmetric junction placement and driving.
result: Achieves nonreciprocal Josephson transport with efficiencies up to 91%.
conclusion: The atomtronic Josephson diode provides a controllable platform for future quantum circuitry and atomtronic devices.

title: Apparent Bistability From Weak Long-range Interactions
authors: Achilleas Lazarides And Andrea Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Achilleas Lazarides and Andrea Pizzi

Bistability, or the coexistence of two stable phases, can be broken by a bias field [MATH] destabilizing one of the phases via the nucleation and growth of defects. Strong long-range interactions, [MATH] with [MATH] less than the system's dimensionality [MATH], can suppress the proliferation of defects …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224116] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how weak long-range interactions can induce apparent bistability in many-body systems, focusing on the role of interaction range in stabilizing metastable phases.
motivation: Understanding the conditions for bistability in systems with long-range interactions is important for non-equilibrium statistical mechanics and phase coexistence.
method: The authors analyze a classical or quantum model with long-range interactions decaying as 1/r^α, using analytical arguments and numerical simulations to study defect nucleation and phase stability.
result: They find that weak long-range interactions (α > d) can still suppress defect proliferation and lead to apparent bistability, contrary to expectations that only strong long-range interactions (α < d) stabilize multiple phases.
conclusion: The work extends the understanding of bistability in long-range interacting systems, showing that even weak interactions can have significant effects on phase coexistence.

title: Tracking Doublon-holon Dynamics In High-harmonic Generation From Mott Insulators
authors: Tao-Yuan Du, Hui-Ru Li, Bo Li, And Ruifeng Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Tao-Yuan Du, Hui-Ru Li, Bo Li, and Ruifeng Lu

High-harmonic generation (HHG) in strongly correlated Mott insulators is investigated using exact diagonalization and time-dependent density-matrix propagation of a laser-driven one-dimensional Hubbard chain. By projecting onto equilibrium Hubbard bands, we use the doublon population and its dynamic…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245147] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies high-harmonic generation in Mott insulators by tracking doublon-holon dynamics using exact diagonalization and time-dependent density-matrix propagation.
motivation: Understanding the ultrafast dynamics of strongly correlated systems under strong laser fields is important for both fundamental physics and potential applications in optoelectronics.
method: The authors simulate a laser-driven one-dimensional Hubbard chain using exact diagonalization and time-dependent density-matrix propagation, projecting onto equilibrium Hubbard bands to analyze doublon population and dynamics.
result: They find that high-harmonic generation is closely linked to doublon-holon pair creation and recombination, with the harmonic spectrum reflecting the underlying many-body dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides insight into non-equilibrium dynamics in Mott insulators, but the connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Anisotropic Second-harmonic Generation In Superconducting Nanostructures
authors: Sara Memarzadeh, Maciej Krawczyk, Armen Gulian, And Jarosław W. Kłos
abstract:
Author(s): Sara Memarzadeh, Maciej Krawczyk, Armen Gulian, and Jarosław W. Kłos

Circuits based on superconducting nanostructures are among the most promising platforms for quantum computing. Understanding how device geometry governs nonlinear electrodynamics is crucial for implementing superconducting quantum technologies. However, to date, research has largely been limited to …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245427] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anisotropic second-harmonic generation in superconducting nanostructures, focusing on geometry-dependent nonlinear electrodynamics.
motivation: Understanding nonlinear electrodynamics in superconducting nanostructures is important for quantum computing platforms, but current research is limited.
method: The authors theoretically analyze second-harmonic generation in superconducting nanostructures with different geometries, likely using nonlinear response theory.
result: They find that the second-harmonic response is anisotropic and depends strongly on the nanostructure geometry.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nonlinear effects in superconducting circuits, which may inform design of quantum devices.

title: Signatures Of Quantum Chaos And Complexity In The Ising Model On Random Graphs
authors: G. J. Sreejith And Sandipan Manna
abstract:
Author(s): G. J. Sreejith and Sandipan Manna

We investigate signatures of quantum chaos in the mixed-field quantum Ising model on finite-size Erdős–Rényi graphs using probes scalable on near-term quantum devices. Upon tuning the graph connectivity, the system exhibits a crossover from a localized regime at low connectivity, through a chaotic r…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214322] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies quantum chaos and complexity in the Ising model on random graphs using probes scalable on near-term quantum devices.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos in many-body systems is important for thermalization and quantum information processing, but the paper focuses on signatures of chaos rather than thermodynamic or information-theoretic constraints.
method: The authors use the mixed-field quantum Ising model on Erdős–Rényi graphs and analyze spectral statistics, out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs), and other chaos probes.
result: They observe a crossover from localized to chaotic behavior as graph connectivity increases, with signatures of quantum chaos emerging at intermediate connectivity.
conclusion: The work provides insights into quantum chaos in disordered systems but does not directly address information thermodynamics or quantum information theory.

title: Universality Of Dissipative Discrete Time Crystal Formation
authors: Jr. And Jayson G. Cosme Roy D. Jara
abstract:
Author(s): Roy D. Jara, Jr. and Jayson G. Cosme

We demonstrate that the Kibble-Zurek mechanism holds for open systems transitioning from a disordered phase to a discrete time crystal (DTC). Specifically, we observe the characteristic power-law scaling with quench time of the number of spatial defects and the transition delay measured from the tim…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214323] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that the Kibble-Zurek mechanism applies to open systems transitioning to a discrete time crystal phase, showing universal scaling of defects and transition delay.
motivation: To understand the formation dynamics of discrete time crystals in open quantum systems and test universality of the Kibble-Zurek mechanism beyond equilibrium phase transitions.
method: Numerical simulations of a driven-dissipative model exhibiting a discrete time crystal phase, analyzing defect density and transition delay as functions of quench time.
result: Observed power-law scaling of spatial defects and transition delay with quench time, consistent with the Kibble-Zurek mechanism.
conclusion: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism holds for dissipative discrete time crystal formation, indicating universal non-equilibrium dynamics in open systems.

title: Nonuniversal Thermal Hall Responses In Fractional Quantum Hall Droplets
authors: Fei Tan, Yuzhu Wang, Xinghao Wang, And Bo Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Fei Tan, Yuzhu Wang, Xinghao Wang, and Bo Yang

We analytically compute the thermal Hall conductance (THC) of fractional quantum Hall droplets under realistic conditions that go beyond the idealized linear edge theory with conformal symmetry. Specifically, we consider finite-size effects at low temperature, nonzero self-energies of quasiholes, an…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241118] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Analytical computation of thermal Hall conductance in fractional quantum Hall droplets beyond idealized edge theory, including finite-size and self-energy effects.
motivation: To understand deviations from universal thermal Hall conductance predictions in realistic finite-size quantum Hall systems.
method: Analytical calculations using conformal field theory techniques with corrections for finite size and quasihole self-energies.
result: The thermal Hall conductance is nonuniversal and depends on system parameters such as droplet size and temperature.
conclusion: Realistic fractional quantum Hall droplets exhibit nonuniversal thermal Hall responses, challenging the robustness of topological quantization.

title: Two-temperature Ashkin-Teller Model
authors: Sertac Cengiz And M. Cemal Yalabik
abstract:
Author(s): Sertac Cengiz and M. Cemal Yalabik

Phase diagram of the two-temperature Ashkin-Teller model with Kawasaki dynamics has been investigated. The system is placed in contact with two heat baths at different temperatures, each of which controls the dynamics of nearest-neighbor exchange in the two perpendicular directions. It was observed …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064144] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Phase diagram of a two-temperature Ashkin-Teller model with Kawasaki dynamics is studied.
motivation: To understand non-equilibrium steady states in systems with multiple heat baths.
method: Monte Carlo simulations of the Ashkin-Teller model with Kawasaki dynamics at two different temperatures.
result: Observed phase transitions and phase diagram features under two-temperature driving.
conclusion: The two-temperature Ashkin-Teller model exhibits rich non-equilibrium behavior, but the work is primarily a statistical mechanics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Vanishing Correlations In Stochastic And Bistochastic Controlled Circuits
authors: Pavel Kos, Bruno Bertini, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Pavel Kos, Bruno Bertini, and Tomaž Prosen

We study the dynamics of circuits composed of stochastic and bistochastic controlled gates. This type of dynamics arises from quantum circuits with random controlled gates, as well as in stochastic circuits and deterministic classical cellular automata. We prove that stochastic and bistochastic cont…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064139] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that correlations vanish in stochastic and bistochastic controlled circuits, with implications for quantum circuits and classical cellular automata.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of random quantum circuits and their classical counterparts is important for quantum information and statistical mechanics.
method: The authors analyze circuits composed of stochastic and bistochastic controlled gates, using mathematical proofs to show that correlations decay to zero.
result: They prove that for such circuits, all correlations vanish, meaning the output distribution becomes product.
conclusion: This result establishes a general property of these circuit classes, which may simplify the analysis of certain quantum and stochastic processes.

title: Intrinsic Nonreciprocity In Electron-phonon-interaction-driven Thermoelectric Diodes
authors: Hao-Kun Ke, Lie-Run Tian, Jun-Feng Liu, Pei-Hao Fu, Jun Wang, And Hu Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Hao-Kun Ke, Lie-Run Tian, Jun-Feng Liu, Pei-Hao Fu, Jun Wang, and Hu Xu

Researchers demonstrate intrinsic nonreciprocal thermoelectric transport in electron-phonon coupled nanowire devices, arising from asymmetric phonon emission and absorption and structural asymmetry. The intrinsic nonreciprocity results in a load-resistor resistance reduction effect that violates Ohm’s addition law in the incoherent limit.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022058] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates intrinsic nonreciprocal thermoelectric transport in electron-phonon coupled nanowire devices, leading to a violation of Ohm's addition law.
motivation: To explore nonreciprocal thermoelectric effects driven by electron-phonon interactions, which could enable novel thermoelectric diodes and energy conversion devices.
method: The authors theoretically model a nanowire device with asymmetric electron-phonon coupling and structural asymmetry, analyzing phonon emission/absorption and transport properties.
result: They find intrinsic nonreciprocity in thermoelectric transport, resulting in a load-resistor resistance reduction effect that violates Ohm's addition law in the incoherent limit.
conclusion: The work reveals a fundamental mechanism for nonreciprocal transport in electron-phonon systems, with potential applications in thermoelectric energy conversion and quantum devices.

title: Tunable Intertwining Via Collective Excitations
authors: András Szabó And R. Chitra
abstract:
Author(s): András Szabó and R. Chitra

Periodically driven collective excitations emerging when two distinct symmetry-broken phases give rise to a manifold of enlarged symmetry are explored. The work proposes that the resulting driven phase diagram hosting out-of-equilibrium intertwined phases is accessible in state-of-the-art matter-cavity experimental setups.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022053] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies periodically driven collective excitations in symmetry-broken phases, proposing a tunable intertwined phase accessible in matter-cavity setups.
motivation: To explore out-of-equilibrium phases arising from driven collective excitations in systems with enlarged symmetry manifolds.
method: Theoretical analysis of periodically driven symmetry-broken phases, deriving the driven phase diagram and identifying conditions for intertwined phases.
result: A tunable intertwined phase is predicted, accessible in state-of-the-art matter-cavity experimental setups.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for engineering out-of-equilibrium intertwined phases via periodic driving, with experimental feasibility.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Characterizes the computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may exist.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is crucial for determining when quantum computers can outperform classical ones.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using complexity theory.
result: They provide a characterization of complexity across regimes, highlighting potential quantum advantage.
conclusion: The work offers new insights into quantum computational advantage for matrix functions.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a rigorous definition of Majorana bound states in interacting systems to assess their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria to quantify the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states in the presence of interactions, using numerical simulations and analytical models.
result: They provide a framework to evaluate how interactions affect the topological protection and spatial extent of Majorana modes, identifying conditions for practical braiding.
conclusion: The work establishes a quantitative approach to assess Majorana bound states in realistic interacting systems, guiding experimental efforts toward non-Abelian braiding.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols classically is often computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: They develop a technique that propagates errors through the circuit to the end, reducing the complexity of simulating logical magic state preparation protocols.
result: The method achieves efficient classical simulation for a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols, enabling analysis of their performance and resource requirements.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for evaluating magic state preparation protocols, which is important for the development of fault-tolerant quantum computers.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying approaches for complex systems in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex phenomena, but existing methods are diverse and fragmented; a unified framework is needed.
method: The authors review field-theoretic methods (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism, path integrals) to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: They show how these methods unify various approaches and provide tools for analyzing chemical, ecological, and epidemiological models.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful and unifying framework for stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with broad applicability beyond physics.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems, which may lead to novel metastable phases.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory and pump-probe spectroscopy.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable states, and nonthermal orders such as superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation offers a powerful tool to manipulate Mott insulators, but the field is still developing with many open questions.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Introduces twisted color circuits for fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code with a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: To achieve universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings while maintaining fault tolerance.
method: Designs scalable circuits called twisted color circuits and uses a just-in-time decoder for error correction.
result: Demonstrates fault-tolerant implementation of non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code.
conclusion: The proposed circuits enable universal quantum computing on planar architectures with practical error correction.

title: Quantum Image Encodings For Noisy Intermediate-scale Quantum Devices: A Comprehensive Performance And Noise-resilience Analysis
authors: Emmanuel Martínez-Guerrero, Guo-Hua Sun, And Shi-Hai Dong
abstract:
Author(s): Emmanuel Martínez-Guerrero, Guo-Hua Sun, and Shi-Hai Dong

Quantum image processing relies on the efficient encoding of classical image data into quantum states, yet the practical performance of existing encoding schemes on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware remains insufficiently understood. Most prior studies have emphasized asymptotic resou…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062456] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper benchmarks quantum image encoding schemes on NISQ devices, focusing on noise resilience and resource requirements.
motivation: Quantum image processing requires efficient encoding of classical images into quantum states, but the performance of existing encodings on noisy hardware is not well understood.
method: The authors implement and compare several quantum image encoding schemes (e.g., FRQI, NEQR) on simulated and real NISQ devices, measuring fidelity, circuit depth, and noise resilience.
result: They find that simpler encodings like FRQI are more noise-resilient but less expressive, while more complex encodings suffer from higher error rates on current hardware.
conclusion: The choice of encoding depends on the trade-off between expressivity and noise tolerance; no single encoding is optimal for all NISQ scenarios.

title: Higher-order Liouvillian Exceptional Points In The Dissipative Dynamics Of Quadratic Fermions
authors: Mingtao Xu And Wei Yi
abstract:
Author(s): Mingtao Xu and Wei Yi

We propose a general class of open fermionic models where quadratic Liouvillians governing the dissipative dynamics feature analytically characterized higher-order exceptional points (EPs). Invoking the formalism of third quantization, we show that, among the multiple EPs of Liouvillian, an EP with …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062455] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies higher-order exceptional points in the dissipative dynamics of quadratic fermions using third quantization.
motivation: Exceptional points in open quantum systems are of interest for their unique spectral properties, but higher-order EPs in fermionic Liouvillians are not well understood.
method: The authors use the formalism of third quantization to analytically characterize higher-order exceptional points in quadratic Liouvillians.
result: They demonstrate that multiple exceptional points exist, including an EP with analytically characterized higher order, and analyze their properties.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for understanding higher-order EPs in dissipative fermionic systems, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Increasing The Stability Of A Superfluid In A Rotating Necklace Potential
authors: Giulio Nesti And Luca Pezzè
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Nesti and Luca Pezzè

Recent experiments have probed the stability of ring superfluids in the presence of Josephson barriers or Gaussian impurities. Here we present a theoretical analysis that extends beyond the regimes explored so far. We study the onset of dynamical instabilities in a ring superfluid, addressing both t…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063326] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies dynamical instabilities in a ring superfluid with a rotating necklace potential, focusing on stability beyond previously explored regimes.
motivation: Recent experiments on ring superfluids with barriers or impurities motivate a deeper theoretical understanding of stability.
method: The authors perform a theoretical analysis using a mean-field approach to study the onset of dynamical instabilities in a ring superfluid with a rotating necklace potential.
result: They identify regimes where the superfluid becomes more stable due to the rotating potential, extending beyond earlier work.
conclusion: The rotating necklace potential can enhance stability of ring superfluids, which may have implications for quantum simulation and metrology.

title: Exceptional Rings Emerging In A non-Hermitian Rice-Mele Ladder
authors: Ensuo Ma And Zhi Song
abstract:
Author(s): Ensuo Ma and Zhi Song

Weyl exceptional lines typically occur in three-dimensional (3D) topological semimetals; however, they also emerge in the parameter space of one-dimensional (1D) systems. In this work, we study the impact of dissipation on the nodal ring in a 3D topological semimetal. We find that the energy spectru…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235150] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exceptional rings in a non-Hermitian Rice-Mele ladder, focusing on topological semimetal physics in the presence of dissipation.
motivation: To understand how dissipation affects nodal rings in 3D topological semimetals, using a 1D ladder model as a parameter-space analog.
method: The authors analyze a non-Hermitian Rice-Mele ladder model, deriving the energy spectrum and identifying exceptional rings in parameter space.
result: Exceptional rings emerge in the parameter space of the 1D ladder, analogous to Weyl exceptional lines in 3D semimetals.
conclusion: The work extends the concept of exceptional lines to lower-dimensional systems, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Model With Competing Rashba Spin-orbit Interactions, Higher Order Hopping, And Domain Wall
authors: Hemant Kumar Sharma, Arijit Saha, And Saptarshi Mandal
abstract:
Author(s): Hemant Kumar Sharma, Arijit Saha, and Saptarshi Mandal

We investigate an extended spin-full Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model preserving chiral symmetry. It contains spin-mixing and nonmixing Rashba spin-orbit interactions, complex next to next nearest neighbor (NNNN) hopping. Using the theory of non-Hermitian matrices, we construct a Hamiltonian functio…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245143] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies an extended SSH model with Rashba spin-orbit interactions and higher-order hopping, focusing on topological phases and domain walls.
motivation: To understand the interplay of spin-orbit coupling and long-range hopping in topological insulators.
method: Constructs a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian and analyzes topological invariants and edge states.
result: Finds that competing Rashba interactions and NNNN hopping modify the topological phase diagram and domain wall states.
conclusion: The extended SSH model exhibits rich topological behavior, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Controlled Pairing Symmetries In A Fermi-Hubbard Ladder With Band Flattening
authors: João P. Mendonça, S. Biswas, M. Dziurawiec, U. Bhattacharya, K. Jachymski, M. Aidelsburger, M. Lewenstein, M. M. Maśka, And T. Grass
abstract:
Author(s): João P. Mendonça, S. Biswas, M. Dziurawiec, U. Bhattacharya, K. Jachymski, M. Aidelsburger, M. Lewenstein, M. M. Maśka, and T. Grass

The competition between interactions in systems with slow electrons can drive unusual collective behavior. Here, the authors study a microscopic ladder model featuring both diagonal hopping pathways and complex loop-like electron exchange interactions. They demonstrate that while both mechanisms independently suppress ordinary metallic behavior, they stabilize completely distinct spatial patterns of electron pairing. These findings offer a theoretical framework for engineering specific superconducting states by tuning the competition between pairing mechanisms in platforms like twisted bilayer graphene or cold atoms.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241119] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies controlled pairing symmetries in a Fermi-Hubbard ladder with band flattening, focusing on competing pairing mechanisms and their spatial patterns.
motivation: To understand how interactions in systems with slow electrons can drive unusual collective behavior and to engineer specific superconducting states.
method: The authors analyze a microscopic ladder model with diagonal hopping and complex loop-like electron exchange interactions, studying their competition.
result: Both mechanisms independently suppress ordinary metallic behavior but stabilize distinct spatial patterns of electron pairing.
conclusion: The findings provide a theoretical framework for engineering specific superconducting states in platforms like twisted bilayer graphene or cold atoms.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Organic Mixed Conductors: Phase Transitions In A Lattice Gas
authors: Lukas M. Bongartz
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Bongartz

Organic mixed conductors (OMCs) represent a promising class of materials for applications in bioelectronics, physical computing, and thermoelectrics. Rather unparalleled, OMCs feature dynamics spanning multiple length and timescales, involving an intricate coupling between electronic, ionic, and mas…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065424] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A statistical mechanics model for phase transitions in organic mixed conductors using a lattice gas approach.
motivation: Organic mixed conductors have complex dynamics across scales; understanding their phase behavior is key for applications in bioelectronics and thermoelectrics.
method: The paper develops a lattice gas model incorporating electronic, ionic, and mass transport couplings, and analyzes phase transitions using mean-field theory and Monte Carlo simulations.
result: The model predicts several phase transitions driven by ion-electron interactions and identifies conditions for mixed conduction.
conclusion: The lattice gas framework captures essential physics of organic mixed conductors and can guide material design.

title: Simulating Dynamics Of The Two-dimensional Transverse-field Ising Model: A Comparative Study Of Large-scale Classical Numerics
authors: Joseph Vovrosh, Sergi Julià-Farré, Wladislaw Krinitsin, Michael Kaicher, Fergus Hayes, Emmanuel Gottlob, Augustine Kshetrimayum, Kemal Bidzhiev, Simon B. Jäger, Markus Schmitt, Joseph Tindall, Constantin Dalyac, Tiago Mendes-Santos, And Alexandre Dauphin
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph Vovrosh, Sergi Julià-Farré, Wladislaw Krinitsin, Michael Kaicher, Fergus Hayes, Emmanuel Gottlob, Augustine Kshetrimayum, Kemal Bidzhiev, Simon B. Jäger, Markus Schmitt, Joseph Tindall, Constantin Dalyac, Tiago Mendes-Santos, and Alexandre Dauphin

The quantum dynamics of many-qubit systems is an outstanding problem that has recently driven significant advances in both numerical methods and programmable quantum processing units (QPUs). In this work, we employ a comprehensive toolbox of state-of-the-art numerical approaches to classically simul…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023311] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks classical numerical methods for simulating the 2D transverse-field Ising model dynamics.
motivation: Quantum dynamics of many-qubit systems is computationally hard; this work compares various classical numerical approaches to assess their accuracy and scalability.
method: Applies a suite of state-of-the-art numerical methods (e.g., tensor networks, neural quantum states, exact diagonalization) to simulate the 2D transverse-field Ising model.
result: Provides a comparative analysis of the performance and limitations of each method for different parameter regimes.
conclusion: No single method is universally optimal; the choice depends on the specific regime and desired accuracy.

title: Disorder-induced Topological Phases In A Two-dimensional Chern Insulator With Strong Magnetic Disorder
authors: Devesh Vaish And Michael Potthoff
abstract:
Author(s): Devesh Vaish and Michael Potthoff

Strong directional disorder in local magnetic moments coupled to a Chern insulator gives rise to topological phases that cannot be realized in any clean system and are therefore genuinely disorder driven. We demonstrate this in a spinful Qi-Wu-Zhang model of a two-dimensional Chern insulator coupled…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023312] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies disorder-induced topological phases in a Chern insulator with strong magnetic disorder, a topic in condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To explore whether strong directional disorder in local magnetic moments can induce topological phases not realizable in clean systems.
method: The authors use a spinful Qi-Wu-Zhang model of a two-dimensional Chern insulator coupled to magnetic disorder and analyze topological invariants.
result: They demonstrate that strong directional disorder gives rise to genuinely disorder-driven topological phases.
