conclusion: Disorder can be a resource for realizing novel topological phases in Chern insulators.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, bridging the gap between theory and experiment.
motivation: Previous BosonSampling complexity proofs assumed a dilute regime, but experimental demonstrations operate in a saturated regime; this work extends the theoretical basis to cover realistic experimental conditions.
method: The authors prove that BosonSampling with a linear number of modes remains hard for classical computers under standard complexity assumptions, using techniques from computational complexity theory and quantum optics.
result: They show that approximate BosonSampling in the saturated regime is #P-hard, and that the linear number of modes is optimal for hardness.
conclusion: The results provide rigorous complexity-theoretic support for photonic quantum advantage experiments operating in the saturated regime.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates quantum computational advantage using an ultracold-atom processor to simulate driven many-body dynamics.
motivation: To experimentally show a utilizable quantum advantage in a programmable quantum simulator.
method: Uses a 61-site ultracold-atom processor to simulate the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
result: Achieves a quantum computational advantage by outperforming classical simulations for the specific task.
conclusion: The ultracold-atom platform can serve as a viable quantum processor for demonstrating practical quantum advantage.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the stability of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature using theoretical modeling.
motivation: To understand whether topological magnon gaps survive at finite temperatures, which is important for spintronic applications.
method: Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures, likely using many-body perturbation theory or spin-wave theory.
result: Topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point.
conclusion: The findings provide a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, and Victor Galitski

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models challenges the thermodynamic limit.
motivation: To understand how domain shape can alter macroscopic ground states in quantum spin and dimer models.
method: Theoretical analysis of quantum dimer models with geometry-induced phase separation.
result: Domain shape fundamentally changes the ground state, breaking the thermodynamic limit assumption.
conclusion: Traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit may not hold in certain quantum spin systems.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Uses Fourier neural operators to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and dynamics of time-periodic quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling periodically driven quantum systems is computationally expensive; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to accelerate simulations.
method: Fourier neural operators are trained on time-series data from quantum systems to learn the Floquet Hamiltonian and predict observable dynamics and operator growth.
result: The method accurately extrapolates dynamics beyond training data and captures temporal correlations in frequency space.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and efficient surrogate for simulating time-periodic quantum systems.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; the paper aims to provide a pedagogical overview of space-time duality as a unifying framework.
method: The review discusses discretizing time evolution on lattice systems, treating space and time on equal footing, and focuses on brickwork quantum circuits.
result: It presents a unified view of dynamical evolution in quantum many-body systems through the lens of quantum computation.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a powerful analogy with quantum computation for understanding many-body dynamics, but the paper is a review without novel results.

title: Ferromagnetism Versus Antiferromagnetism In Narrow-Band Systems: Competition Between Quantum Geometry And Band Dispersion
authors: Haoyu Hu, Oskar Vafek, Kristjan Haule, And B. Andrei Bernevig
abstract:
Author(s): Haoyu Hu, Oskar Vafek, Kristjan Haule, and B. Andrei Bernevig

Magnetism in narrow-band systems arises from the interplay between electronic correlations, quantum geometry, and band dispersion. In particular, both ferro and antiferro magnets are known to occur as ground states of (different) models featuring narrow bands. This poses the question of which is fav…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256505] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the competition between ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism in narrow-band systems, focusing on the role of quantum geometry and band dispersion.
motivation: Understanding the origin of magnetic order in narrow-band systems is important for correlated electron physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical models and possibly numerical methods to analyze the interplay of correlations, quantum geometry, and dispersion.
result: They identify conditions favoring ferromagnetic versus antiferromagnetic ground states.
conclusion: Quantum geometry plays a key role in determining magnetic order, but the work is purely condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics angle.

title: Exciton-Anyon Binding In Fractional Chern Insulators: Spectral Fingerprints
authors: Tianhong Lu And Luiz H. Santos
abstract:
Author(s): Tianhong Lu and Luiz H. Santos

Transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) uniquely combine topological electronic states realized without external magnetic fields with a strong optical response arising from long-lived excitons. Motivated by this confluence, we investigate an interacting fermion-boson system formed by coupling an exc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256605] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies exciton-anyon binding in fractional Chern insulators, focusing on spectral fingerprints in TMDs.
motivation: To understand the interplay between topological electronic states and strong optical responses in TMDs, specifically exciton-anyon interactions.
method: The authors model an interacting fermion-boson system coupling excitons to anyonic quasiparticles in fractional Chern insulators, likely using analytical or numerical techniques.
result: They identify spectral fingerprints of exciton-anyon binding, providing signatures for experimental detection.
conclusion: The work reveals new physics in fractional Chern insulators and suggests experimental probes for anyonic statistics via optical spectroscopy.

title: Profile And Dynamics Of Antiferromagnetic Domain Walls Under Spin-Orbit Torque
authors: G. Theodorou And S. Komineas
abstract:
Author(s): G. Theodorou and S. Komineas

Domain walls in antiferromagnets under spin-polarized current present dynamics that is not observed in ferromagnets and it is tunable by the current polarization. Propagating walls are obtained for an in-plane polarization and precessional dynamics is obtained for perpendicular polarization. We obta…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256710] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of antiferromagnetic domain walls driven by spin-orbit torque, focusing on propagating and precessional motion depending on current polarization.
motivation: Understanding domain wall dynamics in antiferromagnets is important for spintronic applications, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors use micromagnetic simulations or analytical models to analyze domain wall profiles and dynamics under spin-orbit torque with different current polarizations.
result: They find that in-plane polarization leads to propagating walls, while perpendicular polarization yields precessional dynamics, which is tunable by current polarization.
conclusion: The work provides insights into antiferromagnetic domain wall motion but remains within classical spintronics, with no relevance to the user's research interests.

title: Revisiting The Charge-Density-Wave Superlattice Of $1T\text{−}{\text{TiSe}}_{2}$
authors: Wei Wang, Patrick Liu, Lijun Wu, Jing Tao, Genda Gu, Binghai Yan, Alfred Zong, And Yimei Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Wei Wang, Patrick Liu, Lijun Wu, Jing Tao, Genda Gu, Binghai Yan, Alfred Zong, and Yimei Zhu

A number of intriguing phenomena, including exciton condensation, orbital ordering, and emergence of chirality, have been proposed to accompany charge-density-wave (CDW) formation in the layered transition metal dichalcogenide [MATH]. Explaining these effects relies on knowl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256101] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper revisits the charge-density-wave superlattice in 1T-TiSe2, focusing on structural and electronic properties without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To resolve controversies about the CDW superlattice structure in 1T-TiSe2, which is important for understanding exciton condensation and chirality.
method: Combines electron diffraction, scanning tunneling microscopy, and first-principles calculations to determine the atomic-scale CDW modulation.
result: Identifies a specific CDW superlattice pattern and clarifies the role of orbital ordering.
conclusion: The findings provide a definitive structural model for the CDW phase in 1T-TiSe2, but do not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Curvature-Induced Magnon Frequency Combs
authors: Hao Zhao, Qianjun Zheng, And Peng Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Zhao, Qianjun Zheng, and Peng Yan

A tiny bump in a magnetic film exposed to microwaves can engender spin waves with precisely spaced frequencies.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256708] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A bump in a magnetic film under microwaves generates spin waves with equally spaced frequencies, forming a magnon frequency comb.
motivation: To explore nonlinear spin-wave dynamics and generate frequency combs in magnetic systems.
method: Theoretical modeling and numerical simulations of spin-wave excitation in a curved magnetic film.
result: Curvature-induced magnon frequency combs are predicted, with precise frequency spacing.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a new mechanism for magnon frequency combs, potentially useful for magnonic devices.

title: Enhancing Hot-Carrier Lifetime Through Spin Splitting And Strain Interaction In Chiral Perovskite Materials
authors: Yuling Huang, Xiao-Feng Luo, Shaokuan Gong, Jie Xue, Haipeng Lu, Jin-Zhu Zhao, And Xihan Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yuling Huang, Xiao-Feng Luo, Shaokuan Gong, Jie Xue, Haipeng Lu, Jin-Zhu Zhao, and Xihan Chen

The dynamical control over electronic properties represents a key area of research in condensed-matter physics. Here, we demonstrate all-optical control of carrier-strain-mediated giant enhancement of spin splitting (100 meV) in a chiral 2D perovskite. Ultrafast circular dichroism measurements and a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256902] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates all-optical control of spin splitting and hot-carrier lifetime enhancement in chiral 2D perovskites via strain interaction.
motivation: To achieve dynamical control over electronic properties in condensed-matter systems, specifically enhancing hot-carrier lifetimes for potential optoelectronic applications.
method: Ultrafast circular dichroism measurements and theoretical modeling to study carrier-strain-mediated spin splitting in chiral 2D perovskite materials.
result: Giant spin splitting of 100 meV and enhanced hot-carrier lifetime are observed through all-optical control.
conclusion: The strain-spin interaction in chiral perovskites offers a pathway to control carrier dynamics, relevant for optoelectronics but not directly connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Trion Formation And Ordering In The Attractive Su(3) Fermi-Hubbard Model
authors: Jonathan Stepp, Eduardo Ibarra-García-Padilla, Richard T. Scalettar, And Kaden R. A. Hazzard
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Stepp, Eduardo Ibarra-García-Padilla, Richard T. Scalettar, and Kaden R. A. Hazzard

Recent advances in microwave shielding have increased the stability and control of large numbers of polar molecules, allowing for the first realization of a molecular Bose-Einstein condensate. Remarkably, it was also recently realized that shielded polar molecules exhibit an [MATH] symmetr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250402] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies trion formation and ordering in the attractive SU(3) Fermi-Hubbard model using determinant quantum Monte Carlo.
motivation: Understanding strongly correlated phases in multi-component fermionic systems, particularly with SU(3) symmetry, is of fundamental interest in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use determinant quantum Monte Carlo (DQMC) simulations to compute thermodynamic observables and correlation functions for the attractive SU(3) Fermi-Hubbard model.
result: They find evidence of trion (three-fermion bound state) formation and a transition to a trion-ordered phase at low temperatures.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the existence of trion ordering in a lattice model, which may be relevant to ultracold atomic gases and certain materials.

title: Nonperturbative $S$-Matrix Renormalization
authors: Laurent Freidel, José Padua-Argüelles, Susanne Schander, And Marc Schiffer
abstract:
Author(s): Laurent Freidel, José Padua-Argüelles, Susanne Schander, and Marc Schiffer

We propose a renormalization group flow equation for a functional that generates [MATH]-matrix elements and which captures similarities to the well-known Wetterich and Polchinski equations. While the latter ones, respectively, involve the effective action and Schwinger functional, which are genuine off…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251602] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a nonperturbative renormalization group flow equation for generating S-matrix elements, drawing analogies to Wetterich and Polchinski equations.
motivation: To develop a renormalization group approach directly for on-shell S-matrix elements, avoiding off-shell complications.
method: The authors derive a functional flow equation for an S-matrix generating functional, using techniques similar to the functional renormalization group.
result: They obtain a nonperturbative equation that captures the renormalization of scattering amplitudes.
conclusion: This approach provides a new tool for studying nonperturbative aspects of quantum field theories directly from S-matrix elements.

title: Fluid Flow And Spatiotemporal Chaos In Chemically Active Emulsions
authors: Charu Datt, Jonathan Bauermann, Nazmi Burak Budanur, And Frank Jülicher
abstract:
Author(s): Charu Datt, Jonathan Bauermann, Nazmi Burak Budanur, and Frank Jülicher

We study phase-separating fluid mixtures as they demix in the presence of chemical reactions that maintain them away from thermodynamic equilibrium. We show that in such chemically active emulsions the interplay of chemical reactions, phase separation, and hydrodynamics effects complex self-organiza…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 254001] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spatiotemporal chaos in chemically active emulsions, focusing on fluid dynamics and phase separation far from equilibrium.
motivation: To understand how chemical reactions and phase separation interact with hydrodynamics to produce complex self-organization in active emulsions.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model combining Cahn-Hilliard phase separation, chemical reaction kinetics, and Navier-Stokes hydrodynamics, and analyze it numerically.
result: They find that chemical activity can drive spatiotemporal chaos and complex flow patterns in phase-separating fluids.
conclusion: Chemically active emulsions exhibit rich nonlinear dynamics that may be relevant to biological and synthetic active matter systems.

title: Observation Of Linear Scaling Of Superconductivity With Crystal Orientation At $a\text{−}{\mathrm{LaAlO}}_{3}/{\mathrm{KTaO}}_{3}$ Interfaces
authors: Xueshan Cao, Meng Zhang, Yishuai Wang, Ming Qin, Yi Zhou, And Yanwu Xie
abstract:
Author(s): Xueshan Cao, Meng Zhang, Yishuai Wang, Ming Qin, Yi Zhou, and Yanwu Xie

The superconducting transition temperature [MATH] at [MATH]-based oxide interfaces exhibits a dramatic dependence on crystallographic orientation, yet a unifying mechanism remains elusive. Here, we report a linear scaling between [MATH] and a single geometric parameter—the angle $…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256002] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a linear scaling between superconducting transition temperature and crystal orientation at LaAlO3/KTaO3 interfaces.
motivation: The superconducting transition temperature at oxide interfaces shows a strong dependence on crystallographic orientation, but the underlying mechanism is not understood.
method: The authors measure the superconducting transition temperature for different crystal orientations and find a linear scaling with a geometric parameter.
result: A linear scaling between Tc and the angle of crystal orientation is observed.
conclusion: The linear scaling suggests a simple geometric origin for the orientation dependence, but the mechanism remains to be explained.

title: Geometric Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory
authors: Éric Cancès, Théo Duez, Jari van Gog, Asbjørn Bækgaard Lauritsen, Mathieu Lewin, And Julien Toulouse
abstract:
Author(s): Éric Cancès, Théo Duez, Jari van Gog, Asbjørn Bækgaard Lauritsen, Mathieu Lewin, and Julien Toulouse

A geometric reformulation of time-dependent density-functional theory better describes nonequilibrium systems.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256401] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: A geometric reformulation of time-dependent density functional theory for nonequilibrium systems.
motivation: Standard TDDFT has limitations in describing nonequilibrium dynamics; a geometric approach may provide a more accurate framework.
method: The authors develop a geometric reformulation of TDDFT, likely using differential geometry concepts to better capture time-dependent phenomena.
result: The geometric reformulation improves the description of nonequilibrium systems compared to conventional TDDFT.
conclusion: This work offers a new theoretical tool for studying nonequilibrium quantum systems, but it is not directly aligned with the user's research interests.

title: Emergent Spacetime Supersymmetry At 2d Fractionalized Quantum Criticality
authors: Zhengzhi Wu, Zhou-Quan Wan, Shao-Kai Jian, And Hong Yao
abstract:
Author(s): Zhengzhi Wu, Zhou-Quan Wan, Shao-Kai Jian, and Hong Yao

While experimental evidence for spacetime supersymmetry (SUSY) in particle physics remains elusive, condensed matter systems offer a promising arena for its emergence at quantum critical points (QCPs). Although there have been a variety of proposals for emergent SUSY at symmetry-breaking QCPs, the e…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256502] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes emergent spacetime supersymmetry at a 2D fractionalized quantum critical point in a condensed matter system.
motivation: To realize spacetime supersymmetry in a condensed matter setting, which has not been observed in particle physics, and to explore its emergence at quantum critical points beyond symmetry-breaking transitions.
method: The authors construct a lattice model of interacting bosons and fermions that exhibits a fractionalized quantum critical point, and use field-theoretic and numerical techniques to demonstrate emergent SUSY.
result: They show that at the critical point, the low-energy theory is described by a supersymmetric conformal field theory with N=2 supersymmetry in 2D.
conclusion: This work provides a concrete example of emergent SUSY in a fractionalized quantum critical system, opening avenues for studying supersymmetry in condensed matter experiments.

title: Dynamics Of Superconducting Pairs In The Two-Dimensional Hubbard Model
authors: G. Sordi, E. M. O’callaghan, C. Walsh, M. Charlebois, P. Sémon, And A.-M. S. Tremblay
abstract:

The frequency structure of the superconducting correlations in cuprates gives insights on the pairing mechanism. Here we present an exhaustive study of this problem in the two-dimensional Hubbard model with cellular dynamical mean-field theory. To this end, we systematically quantify the dependence …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256503] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of superconducting pairs in the two-dimensional Hubbard model using cellular dynamical mean-field theory.
motivation: Understanding the frequency structure of superconducting correlations in cuprates provides insights into the pairing mechanism.
method: The authors use cellular dynamical mean-field theory to systematically quantify the dependence of superconducting correlations on various parameters.
result: The paper presents an exhaustive study of the frequency structure of superconducting pairs in the Hubbard model.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of pairing mechanisms in high-temperature superconductors.

title: Edge Reconstruction In A Quantum Spin Hall Insulator
authors: Rahul Soni, Matthias Thamm, Gonzalo Alvarez, Bernd Rosenow, And Adrian Del Maestro
abstract:
Author(s): Rahul Soni, Matthias Thamm, Gonzalo Alvarez, Bernd Rosenow, and Adrian Del Maestro

We study interaction-driven edge reconstruction in a quantum spin Hall insulator described by the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang model with Kanamori-Hubbard interactions using the real-space density matrix renormalization group method in both the grand-canonical and canonical ensembles. For a two-dimensional…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256504] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies interaction-driven edge reconstruction in a quantum spin Hall insulator using DMRG, focusing on the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang model with Kanamori-Hubbard interactions.
motivation: Understanding edge reconstruction in quantum spin Hall insulators is important for characterizing topological phases, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use real-space density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) in both grand-canonical and canonical ensembles to simulate the two-dimensional system.
result: They observe interaction-driven edge reconstruction in the quantum spin Hall insulator.
conclusion: The work provides insights into edge physics of topological insulators but does not advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Ultrafast Magneto-Optical Fingerprints Of Altermagnetism In MnTe
authors: Xu Yang, Xingkai Cheng, Zhuo Deng, Yu-Han Gao, Qing-Lin Yang, Zheng Chang, Peng-Tao Yang, Hong-Mei Feng, Xiang-Qun Zhang, Wei He, Junwei Liu, And Zhao-Hua Cheng
abstract:
Author(s): Xu Yang, Xingkai Cheng, Zhuo Deng, Yu-Han Gao, Qing-Lin Yang, Zheng Chang, Peng-Tao Yang, Hong-Mei Feng, Xiang-Qun Zhang, Wei He, Junwei Liu, and Zhao-Hua Cheng

Recently identified altermagnets exhibit a distinctive dual-space nature: they possess spin-split electronic bands akin to ferromagnets in momentum space while maintaining the fully compensated magnetization of antiferromagnets in real space. This inherent duality, originating from the same crystal …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256702] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports ultrafast magneto-optical fingerprints of altermagnetism in MnTe, a condensed matter physics study of a novel magnetic phase.
motivation: Altermagnets are a recently identified class of magnetic materials with spin-split bands but zero net magnetization, and their ultrafast dynamics are unexplored.
method: The authors use time-resolved magneto-optical Kerr effect (TR-MOKE) spectroscopy to probe the spin dynamics in MnTe thin films.
result: They observe distinct ultrafast magneto-optical signatures that are attributed to the altermagnetic order, distinguishing it from conventional antiferromagnets.
conclusion: The findings establish ultrafast magneto-optics as a tool to identify and study altermagnetism, opening new avenues for spintronic applications.

title: Hearing The Light: Stray-Field Noise From The Emergent Photon In Quantum Spin Ice
authors: Gautam K. Naik, Jonathan N. Hallén, Nishan C. Jayarama, Roderich Moessner, And Chris R. Laumann
abstract:
Author(s): Gautam K. Naik, Jonathan N. Hallén, Nishan C. Jayarama, Roderich Moessner, and Chris R. Laumann

Decisive experimental confirmation of the U(1) quantum spin liquid phase in quantum spin ice remains an outstanding challenge. In this Letter, we propose stray-field magnetometry as a direct probe of the emergent photons—the gapless excitation of the emergent electrodynamics in quantum spin ice. The…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256705] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Proposes stray-field magnetometry to detect emergent photons in quantum spin ice, a U(1) quantum spin liquid.
motivation: Experimental confirmation of U(1) quantum spin liquids remains challenging; the paper aims to provide a direct probe of the emergent photon excitation.
method: Theoretical analysis of stray-field noise from emergent electrodynamics in quantum spin ice, calculating magnetometry signatures.
result: Stray-field magnetometry can detect the gapless photon excitation via characteristic noise spectrum.
conclusion: This technique offers a viable experimental route to confirm quantum spin ice and emergent photons.

title: Close Proximity To A Quantum Phase Transition In ${\mathrm{TmZn}}_{2}{\mathrm{GaO}}_{5}$
authors: Matthew Ennis, Rabindranath Bag, Tessa Cookmeyer, Matthew B. Stone, Alexander I. Kolesnikov, Tao Hong, Leon Balents, And Sara Haravifard
abstract:

tldr: This paper reports the synthesis and characterization of a new triangular lattice magnet TmZn2GaO5, which exhibits a quantum phase with strong Ising anisotropy and proximity to a quantum phase transition.
motivation: To discover and study new quantum materials that may host exotic magnetic phases, particularly in frustrated triangular lattice systems.
method: Neutron scattering and thermodynamic measurements on single crystals of TmZn2GaO5, combined with theoretical modeling.
result: The material shows a gapped excitation at the M point and strong Ising anisotropy, indicating a quantum paramagnetic state near a quantum critical point.
conclusion: TmZn2GaO5 is a promising platform for studying quantum phase transitions in frustrated magnets, but the work is primarily materials characterization without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Optimal Displacement Detection Of Arbitrarily Shaped Levitated Dielectric Objects Using Optical Radiation
authors: Shaun Laing, Shelby Klomp, George Winstone, Alexey Grinin, Andrew Dana, Zhiyuan Wang, Kevin Seca Widyatmodjo, James Bateman, And Andrew A. Geraci
abstract:
Author(s): Shaun Laing, Shelby Klomp, George Winstone, Alexey Grinin, Andrew Dana, Zhiyuan Wang, Kevin Seca Widyatmodjo, James Bateman, and Andrew A. Geraci

Optically levitated dielectric objects are promising for precision force, acceleration, torque, and rotation sensing due to their extreme environmental decoupling. While many levitated optomechanics experiments employ spherical objects, for some applications nonspherical geometries offer advantages.…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063529] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes displacement detection for arbitrarily shaped levitated dielectric objects using optical radiation, focusing on precision sensing applications.
motivation: Optically levitated objects are promising for precision sensing, but most work uses spherical objects; nonspherical geometries offer advantages but require optimized detection.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for optimal displacement detection of arbitrarily shaped levitated dielectric particles using optical radiation, considering scattering and interference effects.
result: They derive optimal detection schemes and show that nonspherical shapes can enhance sensitivity for certain degrees of freedom.
conclusion: The work provides a foundation for designing levitated optomechanical sensors with tailored geometries for improved force and torque sensing.

title: Phase-space Open-system Dynamics Of Second-order Nonlinear Interactions With Pulsed Quantum Light
authors: Emanuel Hubenschmid And Victor Rueskov Christiansen
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Hubenschmid and Victor Rueskov Christiansen

The theoretical description of broadband, multimode quantum pulses undergoing a second-order [MATH]-nonlinear interaction can be quite intricate due to the large dimensionality of the underlying phase space. However, in many cases only a few broadband (temporal) modes are relevant before and af…

tldr: The paper develops a phase-space method for simulating broadband multimode quantum pulses undergoing second-order nonlinear interactions.
motivation: Modeling broadband quantum pulses in nonlinear optics is computationally challenging due to high-dimensional phase space; the authors aim to reduce complexity by identifying relevant temporal modes.
method: They employ a phase-space approach based on the positive-P representation and derive equations of motion for the relevant broadband modes, truncating the expansion to a few modes.
result: The method accurately captures the dynamics of second-order nonlinear interactions for pulsed quantum light, demonstrating agreement with full simulations for specific examples.
conclusion: The reduced phase-space method enables efficient simulation of multimode quantum nonlinear optics, facilitating the study of quantum light generation and manipulation.

title: Geometric Theory Of Constrained Schrödinger Dynamics With Application To Time-dependent Density-functional Theory On A Finite Lattice
authors: Éric Cancès, Théo Duez, Jari van Gog, Asbjørn Bækgaard Lauritsen, Mathieu Lewin, And Julien Toulouse
abstract:
Author(s): Éric Cancès, Théo Duez, Jari van Gog, Asbjørn Bækgaard Lauritsen, Mathieu Lewin, and Julien Toulouse

Time-dependent density-functional theory (TDDFT) is a central tool for studying the dynamical electronic structure of molecules and solids, yet aspects of its mathematical foundations remain insufficiently understood. In this work, we revisit the foundations of TDDFT within a finite-dimensional sett…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062222] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a geometric theory of constrained Schrödinger dynamics and applies it to time-dependent density-functional theory on a finite lattice.
motivation: To provide rigorous mathematical foundations for time-dependent density-functional theory (TDDFT), which is widely used but lacks a complete mathematical understanding in finite-dimensional settings.
method: The authors formulate the dynamics as a constrained evolution on a manifold of Slater determinants, using tools from differential geometry and symplectic mechanics to derive equations of motion.
result: They obtain a geometric characterization of the TDDFT equations on a finite lattice, clarifying the role of the Runge-Gross theorem and the v-representability condition.
conclusion: The work establishes a solid mathematical framework for TDDFT on finite lattices, which may guide the development of more accurate approximations.

title: Systematic Errors From Inhomogeneous Alkali-spin Polarization In Nmr Gyroscopes And Comagnetometers
authors: Xiangdong Zhang, Jinbo Hu, Juhao Luo, Chaohong Lee, And Nan Zhao

Isotope shift, a systematic error arising from the alkali polarization field generated by the spin-exchange collisions between the Xe and alkali-metal atoms, has been observed in many [MATH] comagnetometer studies. This isotope shift constitutes a major source of syste…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062816] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes systematic errors from inhomogeneous alkali-spin polarization in NMR gyroscopes and comagnetometers.
motivation: Isotope shift due to alkali polarization field is a major source of systematic error in comagnetometer studies, limiting their accuracy.
method: The authors model the spin-exchange collisions between Xe and alkali-metal atoms and derive the effect of inhomogeneous polarization on the measured signal.
result: They quantify the isotope shift error and propose methods to mitigate it.
conclusion: Understanding and correcting this error is crucial for improving the performance of NMR gyroscopes and comagnetometers.

title: Ultrafast Three-dimensional Steering Of Electronic Ring Currents In Benzene: Coherent Control Of Angular Momentum
authors: Dongming Jia, Yuteng Zhou, Chunmei Liu, And Yonggang Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Dongming Jia, Yuteng Zhou, Chunmei Liu, and Yonggang Yang

Coherent control of electronic ring currents enables the steering of optomagnetic responses on femtosecond timescales. However, most existing schemes confine these currents to the molecular plane, effectively constraining the electronic angular momentum (EAM) vector to a fixed direction. Here, we de…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063115] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates coherent control of electronic ring currents in benzene to steer the electronic angular momentum vector in three dimensions on femtosecond timescales.
motivation: Existing schemes confine ring currents to the molecular plane, limiting control of the angular momentum direction. The authors aim to achieve full three-dimensional steering.
method: Using tailored laser pulses (e.g., circularly and linearly polarized pulses) to excite and manipulate electronic wavepackets in benzene, they simulate the resulting ring currents and angular momentum dynamics via time-dependent quantum mechanics.
result: They show that the electronic angular momentum vector can be oriented arbitrarily in 3D space, and the ring currents can be switched on ultrafast timescales.
conclusion: This work provides a method for ultrafast optomagnetic control at the molecular level, with potential applications in molecular spintronics and quantum information processing.

title: Structures And Proximity Effects Of Inhomogeneous Population-imbalanced Fermi Gases With Pairing Interactions
authors: Bishal Parajuli, Devin J. Gagnon, And Chih-Chun Chien

[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063324] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ground-state structures and proximity effects in inhomogeneous population-imbalanced Fermi gases with pairing interactions using Bogoliubov–de Gennes theory.
motivation: To understand how spatially varying pairing interactions or spin polarization lead to coexisting phases in quasi-one-dimensional atomic Fermi gases.
method: The authors implement the Bogoliubov–de Gennes (BdG) formalism to solve for the ground state of a quasi-1D Fermi gas with spatially varying interaction strength or spin polarization in a box potential.
result: They identify multiple coexisting phases (e.g., normal, superfluid, polarized) and analyze their structures and proximity effects as a function of the inhomogeneity.
conclusion: The work provides insights into phase separation and proximity effects in ultracold Fermi gases, relevant to condensed matter and atomic physics.

title: Atom-chip Interferometer
authors: B. Wirtschafter, C. I. Westbrook, And M. Dupont-Nivet
abstract:
Author(s): B. Wirtschafter, C. I. Westbrook, and M. Dupont-Nivet

tldr: This paper demonstrates a Ramsey-type interferometer using a thermal cloud of magnetically trapped rubidium-87 atoms on an atom chip.
motivation: Atom-chip interferometers offer compact, scalable platforms for precision measurements, but thermal clouds introduce dephasing; this work aims to realize such an interferometer and characterize its performance.
method: The authors use a thermal cloud of Rb-87 atoms trapped on a chip, apply state-selective spatial splitting of two internal states, and implement a Ramsey interferometry sequence.
result: The interferometer is realized and its fringe visibility and coherence time are measured, demonstrating the feasibility of thermal atom-chip interferometry.
conclusion: Thermal atom-chip interferometers can operate with reasonable performance, paving the way for compact sensing devices.

title: Gaussian Mode Coupling Of Spectrally Broadband Photons From Bulk Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion: A Spatial-spectral Mode Analysis Of Fiber Coupling
authors: Carlos Sevilla-Gutiérrez, Varun Raj Kaipalath, And Fabian Steinlechner
abstract:
Author(s): Carlos Sevilla-Gutiérrez, Varun Raj Kaipalath, and Fabian Steinlechner

Photon sources based on spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) are central to experimental quantum optics and quantum technologies. Their performance is commonly quantified by three metrics: pair-collection probability, heralding efficiency, and spectral purity. In bulk-crystal SPDC, these me…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063733] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the spatial-spectral mode coupling of broadband photons from bulk SPDC into single-mode fibers, focusing on optimizing pair-collection probability, heralding efficiency, and spectral purity.
motivation: Efficient fiber coupling of SPDC photons is crucial for quantum optics experiments and quantum technologies, but broadband photons suffer from spatial-spectral correlations that degrade performance.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model for Gaussian mode coupling of spectrally broadband photons, analyzing the spatial-spectral mode structure and its impact on fiber coupling efficiency.
result: They derive conditions for optimal coupling and show trade-offs between pair-collection probability, heralding efficiency, and spectral purity.
conclusion: The analysis provides guidelines for designing SPDC sources with improved fiber coupling, but the work is primarily an engineering optimization without fundamental quantum information or thermodynamic insights.

title: Unconventional Distance Scaling Of Casimir-Polder Force Between Atomic Arrays
authors: Qihang Ye, Haosheng Fu, Bing Miao, And Lei Ying
abstract:
Author(s): Qihang Ye, Haosheng Fu, Bing Miao, and Lei Ying

Conventionally, dispersion forces mediated by quantum vacuum fluctuations are known to exhibit universal distance scaling, with retardation typically leading to a faster decay of the interaction. Here, we show that this expectation fails for intrinsically discrete systems. Using the microscopic scat…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062813] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Casimir-Polder force between atomic arrays and finds unconventional distance scaling due to discreteness.
motivation: Conventional dispersion forces exhibit universal distance scaling, but the authors question whether this holds for intrinsically discrete systems like atomic arrays.
method: They use a microscopic scattering approach to compute the Casimir-Polder interaction between two periodic arrays of atoms.
result: They show that the force decays more slowly than the conventional power law, with the exponent depending on the array geometry and atomic spacing.
conclusion: Discreteness can fundamentally alter the distance scaling of dispersion forces, which has implications for nanoscale systems and quantum optics.

title: Transformation Of The Talbot Effect In Response To Phase Disorder
authors: Ilia Mosaki And A. V. Turlapov
abstract:
Author(s): Ilia Mosaki and A. V. Turlapov

Bose-Einstein condensates initially arranged in a long chain freely expand and interfere. If the initial phases of the condensates are identical, the initial density distribution is restored periodically during the expansion, giving rise to the Talbot effect. Even a slight disorder in the initial ph…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063322] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Talbot effect in Bose-Einstein condensates under phase disorder, focusing on density pattern evolution during free expansion.
motivation: To understand how initial phase disorder affects the revival of density patterns in expanding BEC chains, which is relevant to matter-wave interferometry.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the free expansion of a chain of BECs with random initial phases, using the Talbot effect framework and disorder averaging.
result: Phase disorder suppresses the Talbot revivals; the density distribution becomes irregular and the revival amplitude decays with disorder strength.
conclusion: Phase disorder fundamentally alters the Talbot effect, limiting its applicability in realistic BEC interferometers.

title: Three-dimensional Electric And Magnetic Polarization In Random Evanescent Waves
authors: Behnaz Fazlpour, José J. Gil, Ari T. Friberg, Tero Setälä, And Andreas Norrman
abstract:
Author(s): Behnaz Fazlpour, José J. Gil, Ari T. Friberg, Tero Setälä, and Andreas Norrman

We analyze the spectral three-dimensional (3D) polarimetric properties of the electric and magnetic fields in an evanescent wave created by a random stationary light beam undergoing total internal reflection. [Phys. Rev. A 113, 063525] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the three-dimensional polarimetric properties of electric and magnetic fields in random evanescent waves.
motivation: To understand the polarization structure of evanescent waves, which are important in near-field optics and surface physics.
method: The authors use spectral polarimetry and statistical optics to compute degrees of polarimetric purity, polarimetric dimensions, and nonregularity for both electric and magnetic fields.
result: They characterize the polarimetric properties of random evanescent waves, comparing electric and magnetic field behavior.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed polarimetric description of evanescent waves, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Bistable Fourth Sound Resonance In Superfluid $^{3}\mathrm{He}\text{−}\mathrm{B}$ Due To Gap Suppression
authors: Alexander J. Shook, Daksh Malhotra, Aymar Muhikira, And John P. Davis
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander J. Shook, Daksh Malhotra, Aymar Muhikira, and John P. Davis

Superfluidity in [MATH] exhibits many unique properties that are of interest to modern condensed matter research, including multiple superfluid phase transitions, topological defects, and exotic classes of excitations like Majorana and Weyl fermions. Many of the most interesting theoretic…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214519] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies bistable fourth sound resonance in superfluid 3He-B due to gap suppression, a condensed matter physics phenomenon.
motivation: To understand nonlinear acoustic effects in superfluid 3He-B arising from order parameter suppression.
method: Experimental measurement of fourth sound resonance in a superfluid 3He-B cavity, analyzing nonlinear response and bistability.
result: Observation of bistable resonance behavior attributed to gap suppression by the sound field.
conclusion: Gap suppression leads to nonlinear acoustic effects that must be accounted for in precision measurements of superfluid properties.

title: Many-body Wave Function And Edge Magnetization Of An Open $p+is$ Superconducting Chain
authors: Jiarui Jiao, Chao Xu, Congjun Wu, And Wang Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Jiao, Chao Xu, Congjun Wu, and Wang Yang

Although BCS wave functions for superconductors under periodic boundary conditions are well established, obtaining an explicit form of the many-body BCS wave function under open boundary condition is usually a nontrivial problem. In this work, we construct the exact BCS ground-state wave function of…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224525] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs the exact BCS ground-state wave function for an open p+is superconducting chain and studies its edge magnetization.
motivation: BCS wave functions under open boundary conditions are nontrivial but important for understanding edge properties of topological superconductors.
method: The authors analytically construct the many-body BCS wave function for a p+is superconducting chain with open boundaries using a Bogoliubov transformation and solving the resulting equations.
result: They obtain an explicit form of the ground-state wave function and compute the edge magnetization, revealing topological edge modes.
conclusion: The work provides a rare exact solution for a superconducting system with open boundaries, highlighting edge physics in topological superconductors.

title: Flat-band Driven Kondo Breakdown And Reentrant Effects In Heavy-fermion Moiré Superlattices
authors: Fabian Eickhoff, Jian-Xin Zhu, And Benedikt Fauseweh
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Eickhoff, Jian-Xin Zhu, and Benedikt Fauseweh

Moiré superlattices (MSLs) in van der Waals heterostructures have demonstrated their incredible power in driving emergent electronic phenomena, some of which are reminiscent of those usually only observed in bulk strongly correlated quantum materials. With the recent discovery of van der Waals [MATH]-e…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235153] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Kondo breakdown and reentrant effects in heavy-fermion moiré superlattices, focusing on strongly correlated electronic phenomena.
motivation: Moiré superlattices in van der Waals heterostructures can host emergent electronic phenomena similar to bulk strongly correlated materials, motivating the study of heavy-fermion behavior in these systems.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling, likely involving mean-field or dynamical mean-field theory, to analyze the Kondo lattice model in a moiré superlattice geometry.
result: They find flat-band-driven Kondo breakdown and reentrant heavy-fermion phases, with a phase diagram showing transitions between Kondo-screened and local-moment regimes.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that moiré superlattices provide a tunable platform for studying heavy-fermion physics, including Kondo breakdown and reentrant behavior.

title: Orbital Magnetization Reveals Multiband Topology
authors: Chun Wang Chau, Robert-Jan Slager, And Wojciech J. Jankowski
abstract:
Author(s): Chun Wang Chau, Robert-Jan Slager, and Wojciech J. Jankowski

We demonstrate that nontrivial multiband topological invariants of electronic wave functions can be revealed through orbital magnetization responses to external magnetic fields. We find that decomposing orbital magnetization into energetic and quantum-geometric contributions allows one to deduce non…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235154] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that orbital magnetization can reveal multiband topological invariants in electronic systems.
motivation: To find a physical observable that directly probes multiband topology beyond the usual single-band Chern number.
method: Decompose orbital magnetization into energetic and quantum-geometric contributions and relate them to topological invariants.
result: The decomposition allows extraction of multiband topological invariants from orbital magnetization responses.
conclusion: Orbital magnetization is a useful probe for multiband topology, linking quantum geometry to observable magnetism.

title: Large Anomalous Hall Conductivity And Topological Hall Effect In The Kagome Helimagnet ${\mathrm{MgMn}}_{6}{\mathrm{Ge}}_{6}$
authors: Jie Du, Zhonghua Ma, Hang Li, Xiaodong Zhou, Jie Chen, Tao Zhu, Yong-Chang Lau, And Wenhong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Jie Du, Zhonghua Ma, Hang Li, Xiaodong Zhou, Jie Chen, Tao Zhu, Yong-Chang Lau, and Wenhong Wang

Magnetic kagome materials have emerged as a new platform for exploring exotic topological transport phenomena. The anomalous Hall effect, a phenomenon prevalently observed in various magnetic kagome materials, is commonly explained using Berry-curvature concepts. Here we report that ${}…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245146] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports large anomalous Hall conductivity and topological Hall effect in the kagome helimagnet MgMn6Ge6, attributed to Berry curvature from non-coplanar spin textures.
motivation: To explore exotic topological transport phenomena in magnetic kagome materials, specifically the anomalous and topological Hall effects.
method: Synthesis of MgMn6Ge6 single crystals, measurement of Hall resistivity and magnetization, and analysis using Berry curvature concepts.
result: Observation of large anomalous Hall conductivity and topological Hall effect, indicating non-coplanar spin textures and Berry curvature contributions.
conclusion: MgMn6Ge6 is a promising platform for studying topological transport in kagome magnets.

title: Strain-driven Antiferroelastic Switching Of Altermagnetism
authors: Fanjunjie Han, Shuaihao Tang, Jian-Dong Sun, Xin-Gang Zhao, And Haiyang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Fanjunjie Han, Shuaihao Tang, Jian-Dong Sun, Xin-Gang Zhao, and Haiyang Xu

Altermagnetism, characterized by pronounced momentum-space spin splitting without net magnetization, provides an emerging platform for spintronics. Yet nonvolatile control of its spin states remains a key challenge for device application. Here, we demonstrate that antiferroelastic lattice distortion…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214457] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates nonvolatile control of altermagnetism via antiferroelastic lattice distortion, enabling switching of spin states without net magnetization.
motivation: Nonvolatile control of altermagnetic spin states is crucial for spintronic device applications, but remains a key challenge.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations to show that antiferroelastic lattice distortion can switch the altermagnetic order parameter.
result: They find that strain-driven antiferroelastic switching is possible, with a large energy barrier ensuring nonvolatility.
conclusion: This work provides a mechanism for electrically or mechanically controlling altermagnetism, advancing altermagnetic spintronics.

title: Predicting Interface And Spin States In Armchair Graphene Nanoribbon Junctions
authors: Sofia Sanz And Daniel Sánchez-Portal
abstract:
Author(s): Sofia Sanz and Daniel Sánchez-Portal

We present a theoretical analysis of interface states emerging at junctions between armchair graphene nanoribbons of varying widths. By exploring diverse width combinations and junction geometries, we demonstrate that predicting the precise number of interface states requires considerations beyond t…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235434] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Theoretical analysis of interface states in armchair graphene nanoribbon junctions.
motivation: Understanding interface states in graphene nanoribbon junctions is important for nanoelectronics, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Tight-binding or DFT calculations to predict interface states based on width combinations and junction geometries.
result: The number of interface states depends on more than simple width rules, requiring detailed electronic structure analysis.
conclusion: Predicting interface states in graphene nanoribbon junctions is nontrivial and requires beyond-simple models.

title: Loss/gain-induced Hall Effect Of Vortex Light
authors: Yucheng Lai, Yongliang Zhang, And Kai Chang
abstract:
Author(s): Yucheng Lai, Yongliang Zhang, and Kai Chang

The Hall effect provides a route for unidirectional manipulations of classical and quantum waves. In optics, the spin Hall effect (SHE) induced by the interaction between intrinsic angular momentum (AM) and material inhomogeneity enables AM-dependent control of light at the subwavelength scale. Desp…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245309] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports a loss/gain-induced Hall effect for vortex light in photonic systems, analogous to the spin Hall effect but for orbital angular momentum.
motivation: To explore how non-Hermitian effects (loss/gain) can induce a Hall-like effect for vortex light, enabling unidirectional control of light carrying orbital angular momentum.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a photonic system with loss/gain gradients and derive the Hall effect for vortex light using coupled-mode theory and numerical simulations.
result: They demonstrate that loss/gain gradients can induce a transverse shift of vortex light, analogous to the spin Hall effect, and that the effect depends on the topological charge of the vortex.
conclusion: The loss/gain-induced Hall effect provides a new mechanism for manipulating orbital angular momentum of light, with potential applications in photonic devices.

title: Collective Phonon Mixing And Eigenvector Transport Under Isotope Substitution
authors: Jeff Armstrong, Hamish Cavaye, Pankaj Sharma, And Matthew E. Potter
abstract:
Author(s): Jeff Armstrong, Hamish Cavaye, Pankaj Sharma, and Matthew E. Potter

Isotopic substitution modifies nuclear masses without altering the electronic potential-energy surface to first order and is therefore often interpreted as a simple rescaling of vibrational frequencies. In solids with dense phonon manifolds, however, mass substitution acts as a parametric Hermitian …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214325] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how isotope substitution affects phonon modes and eigenvector transport in solids, focusing on collective mixing and transport phenomena.
motivation: Understanding how mass disorder from isotopes modifies vibrational properties is important for interpreting experiments and designing materials with tailored thermal transport.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and numerical simulations to analyze parametric Hermitian perturbations in dense phonon manifolds under isotope substitution.
result: Isotope substitution leads to collective phonon mixing and eigenvector transport, altering vibrational mode localization and transport properties.
conclusion: Mass substitution in solids with dense phonon manifolds cannot be simply rescaled; it induces nontrivial mixing and transport effects that must be accounted for.

title: Stacking Theory For Bilayer Two-dimensional Magnets
authors: Jun-Xi Du, Sike Zeng, And Yu-Jun Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Xi Du, Sike Zeng, and Yu-Jun Zhao

Two-dimensional unconventional magnetism has recently attracted growing interest due to its intriguing physical properties and promising applications in spintronics. However, existing studies on stacking-induced unconventional magnetism mainly focus on specific materials and stacking configurations.…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214455] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of stacking-induced unconventional magnetism in bilayer two-dimensional magnets, focusing on general principles rather than specific materials.
motivation: To understand how stacking configurations in bilayer 2D magnets can induce unconventional magnetic phases, beyond case-by-case studies.
method: Develops a stacking theory based on symmetry analysis and model Hamiltonians to classify possible magnetic orders.
result: Identifies general conditions for stacking-induced ferromagnetism, antiferromagnetism, and more exotic states.
conclusion: Provides a unified framework for predicting magnetic properties of bilayer 2D magnets based on stacking.

title: Antiferromagnetic Solitons In NiO As Possible Entities For Logic Operations
authors: Z. Li, T. Chirac, J. Tranchida, J.-Y. Chauleau, And M. Viret
abstract:
Author(s): Z. Li, T. Chirac, J. Tranchida, J.-Y. Chauleau, and M. Viret

We show here using atomistic simulations that NiO stripes can be used as waveguides for antiferromagnetic spin waves or domain walls. We numerically demonstrate some of their salient features including their fast velocity over 40 km/s and their interesting propagation properties enabling them to cro…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214456] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies antiferromagnetic solitons in NiO for potential logic operations, focusing on spin wave and domain wall propagation.
motivation: To explore antiferromagnetic materials as a platform for high-speed logic devices using solitons.
method: Atomistic simulations of NiO stripes to model spin wave and domain wall dynamics.
result: Demonstrates fast soliton velocities over 40 km/s and propagation properties enabling crossing and interference.
conclusion: Antiferromagnetic solitons in NiO show promise for logic operations, but further experimental validation is needed.

title: Nontrivial Three-sublattice Magnetization In The Easy-axis Spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ Xxz Antiferromagnet On The Triangular Lattice
authors: Masahiro Kadosawa, Masaaki Nakamura, Yukinori Ohta, And Satoshi Nishimoto
abstract:
Author(s): Masahiro Kadosawa, Masaaki Nakamura, Yukinori Ohta, and Satoshi Nishimoto

We investigate the ground-state magnetic structure of the spin-[MATH] XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice in the easy-axis regime using the density-matrix renormalization group. By applying spiral boundary conditions, we exactly map finite [MATH] clusters onto one-dimensional chains while av…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224442] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the ground-state magnetic structure of an easy-axis spin-1/2 XXZ antiferromagnet on a triangular lattice using DMRG.
motivation: To understand nontrivial magnetic ordering in frustrated quantum magnets, specifically the three-sublattice magnetization in the easy-axis regime.
method: Density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) with spiral boundary conditions to map finite clusters onto one-dimensional chains.
result: Identifies a nontrivial three-sublattice magnetization pattern in the ground state.
conclusion: The easy-axis XXZ model on a triangular lattice exhibits a three-sublattice magnetic order, contributing to the understanding of frustrated quantum magnetism.

title: Spin-dependent Orbital Selectivity And Partial Kondo-like Screening In The Magnetically Ordered Hund's Metal ${\mathrm{Sr}}_{2}{\mathrm{CoO}}_{4}$
authors: Shivani Bhardwaj And Sudhir K. Pandey
abstract:
Author(s): Shivani Bhardwaj and Sudhir K. Pandey

Hund's metallicity in [MATH] transition metal oxides constitutes a rare class of compounds, since they have been long understood considering the dominance of Hubbard [MATH]. [MATH] belong to this rare class of metals; among them,…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235147] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-dependent orbital selectivity and Kondo-like screening in the Hund's metal Sr2CoO4 using DFT+DMFT.
motivation: To understand the electronic structure and correlation effects in Hund's metals, which are rare and poorly understood.
method: First-principles DFT+DMFT calculations with continuous-time quantum Monte Carlo impurity solver.
result: They find spin-dependent orbital selectivity and partial Kondo-like screening in the magnetically ordered state.
conclusion: The study reveals complex interplay between Hund's coupling, orbital selectivity, and magnetic ordering in Sr2CoO4.

title: Orbital Hybridization Induces Giant Cubic Rashba Effect At The $\text{Cu/}{\mathrm{WO}}_{3}$ Interface
authors: Md Aktar Hossain And Saikat Das
abstract:
Author(s): Md Aktar Hossain and Saikat Das

Harnessing Rashba spin-orbit interaction and related spintronic functionalities has traditionally relied on metallic surfaces or interfaces containing elemental heavy metals. Here, using first-principles calculations and [MATH] as a model heterostructure, we…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235149] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study of giant cubic Rashba effect at Cu/WO3 interface due to orbital hybridization.
motivation: To explore Rashba spin-orbit interaction at interfaces without heavy metals, enabling spintronic applications.
method: Density functional theory (DFT) calculations on Cu/WO3 heterostructure, analyzing band structure and spin texture.
result: Giant cubic Rashba effect observed, originating from orbital hybridization between Cu and WO3.
conclusion: Cu/WO3 interface is a promising platform for Rashba-based spintronics without heavy elements.

title: Taxonomy Of Integrable And Ground-state Solvable Models: Jastrow Wave Functions On Graphs And Parent Hamiltonians
authors: Nilanjan Sasmal And Adolfo Del Campo
abstract:
Author(s): Nilanjan Sasmal and Adolfo del Campo

We introduce a family of many-body systems of distinguishable continuous-variable particles in which interparticle interactions are set by the adjacency matrix of a graph. The ground-state wave function of such systems is of a generalized Jastrow form involving the product of pair-correlation functi…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235151] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a family of many-body systems with Jastrow ground states on graphs, providing exact solvability and integrability.
motivation: To systematically construct and classify exactly solvable many-body models with Jastrow wave functions on arbitrary graphs.
method: Defines interactions via graph adjacency matrices and derives parent Hamiltonians for which the Jastrow product state is the exact ground state.
result: Establishes a taxonomy of integrable and ground-state solvable models, linking graph theory to many-body physics.
conclusion: Provides a unified framework for constructing solvable models, with potential applications in condensed matter and quantum information.

title: Toroidal Fermi Surface Geometry And Phonon-limited Transport In Nodal-line Semimetals
authors: Aman Anand And Alessandro de Martino
abstract:
Author(s): Aman Anand and Alessandro De Martino

Nodal-line semimetals (NLSs) can display unconventional quasiparticle dynamics and charge transport properties due to their extended band degeneracy and the peculiar geometry of their Fermi surface. We consider electron-acoustic phonon scattering as the dominant relaxation mechanism and compute the …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235432] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phonon-limited transport in nodal-line semimetals, focusing on the role of toroidal Fermi surface geometry.
motivation: Nodal-line semimetals have unique Fermi surface geometry that may lead to unconventional transport properties; understanding phonon scattering is key.
method: The authors compute the electrical resistivity due to electron-acoustic phonon scattering using Boltzmann transport theory, incorporating the toroidal Fermi surface geometry.
result: They find that the resistivity exhibits a distinct temperature dependence and anisotropy due to the nodal-line structure.
conclusion: The toroidal Fermi surface geometry significantly influences phonon-limited transport, which could be tested experimentally.

title: Free-electron Decoherence: Theory And Applications
authors: Cruz I. Velasco, Valerio Di Giulio, And F. Javier García de Abajo
abstract:
Author(s): Cruz I. Velasco, Valerio Di Giulio, and F. Javier García de Abajo

Electron microscopy relies on the spatial coherence of electron beams to generate atomic-scale images using interference and diffraction, which can be degraded by inelastic-scattering processes that induce decoherence. Here, we present a theoretical study of decoherence arising from the electromagne…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235433] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies decoherence of free electrons due to electromagnetic interactions, with applications to electron microscopy.
motivation: Understanding decoherence in electron beams is crucial for high-resolution electron microscopy, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on the electromagnetic interaction between a free electron and its environment, calculating decoherence rates.
result: They derive expressions for decoherence induced by inelastic scattering and discuss implications for electron beam coherence.
conclusion: The work provides insights into decoherence mechanisms in electron microscopy but does not advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Theory Of ab Initio Downfolding With Arbitrary-range Electron-phonon Coupling
authors: Norm M. Tubman, Christopher J. N. Coveney, Chih-En Hsu, Andres Montoya-Castillo, Marina R. Filip, Jeffrey B. Neaton, Zhenglu Li, Vojtech Vlcek, And Antonios M. Alvertis
abstract:
Author(s): Norm M. Tubman, Christopher J. N. Coveney, Chih-En Hsu, Andres Montoya-Castillo, Marina R. Filip, Jeffrey B. Neaton, Zhenglu Li, Vojtech Vlcek, and Antonios M. Alvertis

Ab initio downfolding describes the electronic structure of materials within a low-energy subspace, often around the Fermi level. Typically starting from mean-field calculations, this framework allows for the calculation of one- and two-electron interactions, and the parametrization of a many-body H…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245144] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for ab initio downfolding with arbitrary-range electron-phonon coupling to describe low-energy electronic structure in materials.
motivation: Accurate modeling of electron-phonon interactions is crucial for understanding material properties, but existing downfolding methods are limited to short-range coupling.
method: The authors extend downfolding theory to include arbitrary-range electron-phonon coupling, starting from mean-field calculations and deriving effective interactions within a low-energy subspace.
result: They demonstrate that the method captures long-range electron-phonon effects and can be used to parametrize many-body Hamiltonians for correlated materials.
conclusion: The framework provides a systematic way to incorporate electron-phonon coupling into low-energy models, enabling more accurate predictions of electronic and transport properties.

title: Emergence Of Multiple Zero Modes Bound To Vortices In Extended Topological Josephson Junctions
authors: Adrian Reich, Kiryl Piasotski, Eytan Grosfeld, And Alexander Shnirman
abstract:
Author(s): Adrian Reich, Kiryl Piasotski, Eytan Grosfeld, and Alexander Shnirman

We study planar Josephson junctions formed on the surface of a three-dimensional topological insulator (Fu-Kane proposal). We examine the experimentally relevant parameter regimes in which the frequently used effective description in terms of two counter-propagating one-dimensional Majorana modes wi…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245426] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies zero-energy Majorana modes bound to vortices in topological Josephson junctions on a topological insulator surface.
motivation: To understand the emergence of multiple zero modes in extended topological Josephson junctions beyond the simplified one-dimensional model.
method: The authors analyze a planar Josephson junction on a topological insulator using a two-dimensional effective theory and solve for bound states in the vortex core.
result: They find that multiple zero-energy Majorana modes can appear bound to a single vortex, depending on junction parameters.
conclusion: The results show richer physics than previously thought, with implications for topological quantum computing but not directly addressing quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Spatiotemporal Migration Of Antiferromagnetic Domain Walls In ${\mathrm{Sr}}_{2}{\mathrm{IrO}}_{4}$
authors: Ian Robinson, David Yang, Ross Harder, Dina Sheyfer, Longlong Wu, Jack Griffiths, Emil Bozin, Mark P. M.
