While laser-driven demagnetization and magnetic x-ray scattering in Sr
[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220410] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the spatiotemporal migration of antiferromagnetic domain walls in Sr2IrO4 using pump-probe X-ray scattering.
motivation: Understanding domain wall dynamics in antiferromagnets is important for spintronics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use coherent X-ray scattering at a free-electron laser in a pump-probe setup to track domain wall motion.
result: They measure a wall-migration velocity for the first time in this material.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into antiferromagnetic domain wall dynamics but is purely condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics angle.

title: Van Hove Singularities In The Density Of States Of A Chaotic Dynamical System
authors: Bryn Davies
abstract:
Author(s): Bryn Davies

We show that the statistics of chaotic systems can be predicted by constructing an associated sequence of periodic differential operators and computing their densities of states. For such operators, the density of states is well understood and can be computed straightforwardly, often yielding explic…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064211] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper predicts statistics of chaotic dynamical systems using periodic differential operators and their density of states, focusing on Van Hove singularities.
motivation: To understand and predict the statistical properties of chaotic systems, which are typically difficult to analyze.
method: Constructs an associated sequence of periodic differential operators and computes their density of states, leveraging known results for such operators.
result: The density of states for these operators can be computed explicitly, often yielding analytic expressions that reveal Van Hove singularities.
conclusion: The approach provides a new way to predict chaotic system statistics by linking them to periodic operator spectra.

title: Controlling Synchronization Dynamics Via Physics-informed Neural Networks
authors: Kaiming Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiming Luo

Synchronization control in networked dynamical systems requires regulating not only whether coherence is achieved but also when and to what extent it emerges. We propose a physics-informed neural network framework for continuous-time synchronization regulation, in which system trajectories and contr…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064212] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Uses physics-informed neural networks to control synchronization dynamics in networked systems.
motivation: To regulate not only whether synchronization occurs but also when and to what extent it emerges.
method: Proposes a physics-informed neural network framework that incorporates system dynamics into the loss function for continuous-time synchronization control.
result: Demonstrates effective regulation of synchronization timing and degree in networked dynamical systems.
conclusion: Physics-informed neural networks offer a flexible approach for controlling synchronization dynamics.

title: Electronic Access To Glass Transition In Supercooled Ionic Liquids Using Ambipolar Transistor
authors: Tanima Kundu, Rahul Paramanik, Aishee Saha, Shibnath Mandal, Antarik Sarkar, Bipul Karmakar, And Subhadeep Datta
abstract:
Author(s): Tanima Kundu, Rahul Paramanik, Aishee Saha, Shibnath Mandal, Antarik Sarkar, Bipul Karmakar, and Subhadeep Datta

Relaxation dynamics of supercooled liquids approaching glassy arrest remain a central challenge in integrated electronic architectures, where conventional rheometry becomes incompatible. Here, we demonstrate that an ambipolar [MATH] field-effect transistor functions as an electrical p…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065425] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses an ambipolar transistor to probe the glass transition in supercooled ionic liquids via electronic transport.
motivation: Conventional rheometry is incompatible with integrated electronic architectures, so a new method to study glassy dynamics in supercooled liquids is needed.
method: An ambipolar field-effect transistor is employed to measure electrical transport properties of supercooled ionic liquids as they approach the glass transition.
result: The transistor provides electronic access to relaxation dynamics, revealing signatures of the glass transition.
conclusion: Electronic transport measurements can serve as a probe for glassy dynamics, offering a platform compatible with electronic devices.

title: Mode Coupling And Resonance-induced Relaxation In Carbon Nanotubes
authors: Hang Yu, Lin Deng, Weicheng Fu, Zhigang Zhu, Yisen Wang, And Liang Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Hang Yu, Lin Deng, Weicheng Fu, Zhigang Zhu, Yisen Wang, and Liang Huang

Understanding how vibrational modes relax in low-dimensional materials is central to thermal transport, mechanical coherence control, and the design of high-[MATH] nanomechanical resonators. Here we investigate the intrinsic relaxation dynamics of armchair carbon nanotubes (CNTs) under single-mode exci…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065507] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies vibrational mode relaxation in carbon nanotubes, focusing on thermal transport and mechanical coherence.
motivation: Understanding relaxation dynamics in low-dimensional materials is important for thermal management and nanomechanical resonator design.
method: The authors investigate intrinsic relaxation of armchair carbon nanotubes under single-mode excitation using theoretical modeling.
result: They find mode coupling and resonance-induced relaxation mechanisms that govern energy dissipation.
conclusion: The work provides insights into vibrational energy decay in carbon nanotubes, relevant for thermal transport and mechanical applications.

title: Robustness Of Networks Of Hypergraphs
authors: Xiyao Sun, Yuanyuan Pang, Zhengao Guo, Xiaoming Liang, And Jie Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Xiyao Sun, Yuanyuan Pang, Zhengao Guo, Xiaoming Liang, and Jie Zhou

Hypergraphs provide a natural representation of complex systems with higher-order interactions and are commonly interdependent with each other. In this work, based on a bipartite network representation of hypergraphs, we propose a framework of networks of hypergraphs (NOH) to describe the structures…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064312] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a framework for networks of hypergraphs to study robustness in complex systems with higher-order interactions.
motivation: Real-world systems often involve higher-order interactions and interdependencies, which hypergraphs can model; understanding their robustness is important.
method: The authors use a bipartite network representation of hypergraphs to construct a network of hypergraphs (NOH) framework and analyze percolation-based robustness.
result: They derive theoretical conditions for robustness and demonstrate that interdependent hypergraphs can exhibit cascading failures similar to interdependent networks.
conclusion: The NOH framework provides a useful tool for studying robustness in systems with higher-order interactions, but the work is primarily in network science and complex systems, not quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Steady-state Equilibrium And Nonequilibrium Noisy Network Dynamics
authors: Pik-Yin Lai
abstract:
Author(s): Pik-Yin Lai (黎璧賢)

The fluctuating dynamics of a network about its stable, noise-free steady state are theoretically investigated. Various causes of nonequilibrium dynamics are identified in terms of the properties and symmetry of the network connections and the noise covariance matrices. Several equivalent conditions…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064148] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies steady-state fluctuations in noisy networks, focusing on equilibrium and nonequilibrium dynamics from a classical stochastic perspective.
motivation: To understand how network connectivity and noise properties lead to nonequilibrium steady states.
method: Theoretical analysis using Langevin equations and covariance matrices for network dynamics.
result: Identifies conditions for equilibrium and nonequilibrium dynamics based on network symmetry and noise correlations.
conclusion: The framework provides a general characterization of noisy network fluctuations but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Collective Ballistic Motion Explains Fast Aggregation In Adhesive Active Matter
authors: Emanuel F. Teixeira, Pablo de Castro, Carine P. Beatrici, Heitor C. M. Fernandes, And Leonardo G. Brunnet
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel F. Teixeira, Pablo de Castro, Carine P. Beatrici, Heitor C. M. Fernandes, and Leonardo G. Brunnet

Inspired by motile cells in tissue formation, we find that active systems of self-aligning adhesive particles undergo ballistic aggregation through a flocking transition. This kinetic regime emerges when the cluster persistence length grows faster with cluster mass than the intercluster distance doe…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065422] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ballistic aggregation in active matter systems of self-aligning adhesive particles, focusing on collective motion and cluster growth.
motivation: Understanding fast aggregation in active matter, inspired by motile cells in tissue formation.
method: Simulations of self-aligning adhesive particles, analyzing cluster persistence length and intercluster distance.
result: A flocking transition leads to ballistic aggregation where cluster persistence length grows faster than intercluster distance.
conclusion: Collective ballistic motion explains rapid aggregation in adhesive active matter systems.

title: Hydrodynamic Theory Of Wetting By Active Particles
authors: Noah Grodzinski, Michael E. Cates, And Robert L. Jack
abstract:
Author(s): Noah Grodzinski, Michael E. Cates, and Robert L. Jack

The accumulation of self-propelled particles on repulsive barriers is a widely observed feature in active matter. Despite being implicated in a broad range of biological processes, from biofilm formation to cytoskeletal movement, wetting of surfaces by active particles remains poorly understood. In …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065423] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a hydrodynamic theory for the wetting of repulsive barriers by active particles, extending classical wetting concepts to active matter.
motivation: Wetting by active particles is poorly understood despite its relevance to biological processes like biofilm formation and cytoskeletal movement.
method: The authors derive a hydrodynamic theory based on continuum equations for active particle density and orientation, incorporating activity and repulsive interactions.
result: The theory predicts that active particles can accumulate on repulsive barriers, leading to wetting transitions that depend on activity strength and barrier properties.
conclusion: Active wetting differs qualitatively from passive wetting, with activity enabling novel wetting behaviors not seen in equilibrium systems.

title: Nonreciprocal Blume-Capel Model With Antisymmetric Single-ion Anisotropies
authors: Arjun R, Pratyush Prakash Patra, And A. V. Anil Kumar
abstract:
Author(s): Arjun R, Pratyush Prakash Patra, and A. V. Anil Kumar

We investigate the interplay between nonreciprocal interactions and chemical-potential imbalance in a two-species nonreciprocal Blume-Capel model. Combining a systematic mean-field bifurcation analysis with large-scale Monte Carlo simulations in two and three dimensions, we map the model's dynamical…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064140] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a nonreciprocal Blume-Capel model with antisymmetric single-ion anisotropies using mean-field analysis and Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: To understand the interplay between nonreciprocal interactions and chemical-potential imbalance in a two-species magnetic model.
method: Combines systematic mean-field bifurcation analysis with large-scale Monte Carlo simulations in two and three dimensions.
result: Maps the dynamical phase diagram and identifies novel phases arising from nonreciprocity.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal interactions lead to rich nonequilibrium behavior in the Blume-Capel model.

title: Collective Coordinate Descriptions Of A Kink In A Driven-damped ${ϕ}^{4}$ Model
authors: Jacek Gatlik, Tomasz Dobrowolski, Jean-Guy Caputo, And Panayotis G. Kevrekidis
abstract:
Author(s): Jacek Gatlik, Tomasz Dobrowolski, Jean-Guy Caputo, and Panayotis G. Kevrekidis

Extending a recent effective theory formulation for the dynamics of kinks in the sine-Gordon model [T. Dobrowolski et al.,
tldr: This paper develops effective collective coordinate models for kink dynamics in a driven-damped φ⁴ model, extending previous work on sine-Gordon kinks.
motivation: To provide a reduced description of kink motion in the φ⁴ model under driving and damping, capturing position, width, and internal mode dynamics.
method: Three reduced models based on collective coordinates (position, width, internal mode) are derived from the full field theory using a variational approach and compared with direct numerical simulations.
result: The reduced models accurately reproduce kink dynamics in certain parameter regimes, but discrepancies arise due to neglected degrees of freedom.
conclusion: Collective coordinate descriptions offer a useful but limited effective theory for kinks in driven-damped φ⁴ models, with accuracy depending on the driving and damping strengths.

title: Relationship Between Heider Links And Ising Spins
authors: Zdzislaw Burda, Maciej Wołoszyn, Krzysztof Malarz, And Krzysztof Kułakowski
abstract:
Author(s): Zdzislaw Burda, Maciej Wołoszyn, Krzysztof Malarz, and Krzysztof Kułakowski

We show that the Heider model with an external field is equivalent, in the limit of structural balance, to the Ising model with nearest-neighbor interactions without an external field. More precisely, we claim that the signs of the Heider relations that maintain structural equilibrium in the system …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062104] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes an equivalence between the Heider model of social balance and the Ising model in the limit of structural balance.
motivation: To connect sociological balance theory with statistical physics, specifically showing that Heider's social relations can be mapped to Ising spins.
method: Analytical derivation showing that the Heider model with an external field reduces to the Ising model without an external field under structural balance constraints.
result: The signs of Heider relations maintaining structural equilibrium correspond to Ising spin configurations with nearest-neighbor interactions.
conclusion: The equivalence provides a bridge between social network theory and condensed matter physics, but the work is purely theoretical and not directly applicable to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Discontinuous Wealth-gradient Transition Driving Cooperation
authors: Hyun Gyu Lee, Hyeong-Chai Jeong, And Deok-Sun Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Hyun Gyu Lee, Hyeong-Chai Jeong, and Deok-Sun Lee

The universal prevalence of cooperation is puzzling, as defection typically yields higher payoffs than cooperation, motivating searches for hidden pathways to cooperation. Here we study a game-theoretic model on a lattice structured population in which interaction payoffs are scaled by the minimum o…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064306] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cooperation in a game-theoretic model on a lattice, focusing on wealth-gradient transitions.
motivation: Understanding the emergence of cooperation despite the payoff advantage of defection is a classic puzzle in evolutionary game theory.
method: The authors analyze a spatial game where payoffs are scaled by the minimum of players' wealth, leading to a discontinuous transition driven by wealth gradients.
result: They find a discontinuous transition to cooperation as wealth inequality increases, with a critical gradient threshold.
conclusion: Wealth inequality can promote cooperation in structured populations, offering a new mechanism for the evolution of cooperation.

title: ChronoCast: A Time-series Paradigm For Molecular Dynamics Simulation Using Equivariant Graph Neural Networks
authors: Yuxing Wang, Zhongwei Zhang, Shuang Lu, Shuyue Shan, Vitaly A. Kuzkin, Anton M. Krivtsov, And Jie Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yuxing Wang, Zhongwei Zhang, Shuang Lu, Shuyue Shan, Vitaly A. Kuzkin, Anton M. Krivtsov, and Jie Chen

We propose a time-series paradigm named ChronoCast for molecular dynamics simulation using an advanced autoregressive Equivariant Graph Neural Network, which reformulates the conventionally time-consuming integration process into a forecasting task. This reformulation in turn offers a promising solu…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065305] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: ChronoCast uses an equivariant graph neural network to accelerate molecular dynamics simulations by reformulating integration as a time-series forecasting task.
motivation: Molecular dynamics simulations are computationally expensive due to the need for numerical integration over many time steps; the authors aim to speed this up using machine learning.
method: They propose an autoregressive equivariant graph neural network that predicts future atomic positions from past trajectories, effectively replacing the integrator.
result: The method achieves accurate long-term predictions while significantly reducing computational cost compared to traditional integration.
conclusion: ChronoCast demonstrates that time-series forecasting with equivariant GNNs can effectively accelerate molecular dynamics simulations.

title: Theory Uncertainties In Predictions Of Strong-field Qed
authors: T. G. Blackburn
abstract:
Author(s): T. G. Blackburn

Experiments using high-power lasers and relativistic electron beams will soon be capable of precision testing of the theory of strong-field quantum electrodynamics. The comparison between experiment and theory always occurs via numerical simulations, but the lack of quantitative uncertainty bounds f…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023346] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper discusses theoretical uncertainties in numerical simulations of strong-field quantum electrodynamics (QED) for high-power laser experiments.
motivation: Precision tests of strong-field QED require accurate simulations, but current methods lack quantitative uncertainty bounds, hindering comparison with experiments.
method: The author reviews sources of uncertainty in Monte Carlo simulations of strong-field QED, including finite-size effects, discretization, and approximations in the photon emission and pair production rates.
result: The paper identifies key uncertainty contributions and proposes a framework for estimating systematic errors in simulated observables.
conclusion: Quantifying theory uncertainties is essential for reliable validation of strong-field QED, and the proposed methods can improve future experimental comparisons.

title: Differentiable Learning And Control Of Free-energy-driven Pattern Dynamics
authors: Alexander E. Cohen, Samuel Degnan-Morgenstern, Simon Daubner, Jörn Dunkel, And Martin Z. Bazant
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander E. Cohen, Samuel Degnan-Morgenstern, Simon Daubner, Jörn Dunkel, and Martin Z. Bazant

Pattern-forming dynamics govern the behavior of many quantum, electrochemical, and soft-matter systems, yet learning and controlling the corresponding partial differential equation (PDE) models on realistic geometries remains challenging. In this work, we develop a unified, differentiable framework …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023344] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A differentiable framework for learning and controlling pattern-forming PDEs in soft matter and electrochemical systems.
motivation: Pattern-forming dynamics are important in many systems but learning and controlling PDE models on realistic geometries is challenging.
method: Develops a unified differentiable framework using neural networks and adjoint methods to learn and control free-energy-driven pattern dynamics.
result: Demonstrates effective learning and control of pattern formation in simulated examples.
conclusion: The framework enables data-driven discovery and control of pattern dynamics, with potential applications in soft matter and electrochemistry.

title: Tiling By Near Coincidence
authors: Meshy Ochana And Ron Lifshitz
abstract:
Author(s): Meshy Ochana and Ron Lifshitz

Moiré patterns of twisted and scaled bilayers have recently emerged as a fertile source of quasiperiodic order in two-dimensional materials. Inspired by these systems, we introduce the near-coincidence method for generating quasiperiodic tilings of the plane. The method is intuitive—admitting pairs …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023330] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a near-coincidence method for generating quasiperiodic tilings inspired by moiré patterns in twisted bilayers.
motivation: Moiré patterns in twisted bilayers have shown quasiperiodic order; the authors aim to provide a general method to generate such tilings.
method: The near-coincidence method constructs tilings by overlaying two periodic lattices with a small mismatch in scale or rotation, then selecting vertices that nearly coincide.
result: The method produces a variety of quasiperiodic tilings, including those with 12-fold symmetry, and can be tuned by adjusting the lattice parameters.
conclusion: The near-coincidence method offers an intuitive and flexible way to generate quasiperiodic tilings, potentially useful for modeling moiré materials.

title: Phase-space Topology And Spectral Flow In Screened Magnetized Plasmas
authors: Xianhao Rao, Adil Yolbarsop, Hong Li, And Wandong Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Xianhao Rao, Adil Yolbarsop, Hong Li, and Wandong Liu

Topological wave phenomena in continuous media are fundamentally challenged by unbounded spectra and the absence of a compact Brillouin zone, which obstruct conventional bulk-interface formulations. We develop a unified phase-space framework for screened magnetized plasma based on a pseudo-Hermitian…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023334] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a phase-space framework for topological wave phenomena in screened magnetized plasmas, focusing on spectral flow and bulk-interface correspondence in continuous media.
motivation: Topological wave phenomena in continuous media are challenged by unbounded spectra and lack of a compact Brillouin zone, which obstruct conventional bulk-interface formulations.
method: The authors develop a unified phase-space framework based on pseudo-Hermitian operators to analyze topological properties of screened magnetized plasmas.
result: They demonstrate spectral flow and establish a bulk-interface correspondence in this continuous medium.
conclusion: The phase-space framework provides a way to study topological phenomena in continuous media with unbounded spectra.

title: One-particle Density Matrix Framework For Mode-shell Correspondence: Characterizing Topology In Amorphous Higher-order Topological Insulators
authors: Miguel F. Martínez, Lucien Jezequel, Jens H. Bardarson, Thomas Klein Kvorning, And Julia D. Hannukainen
abstract:
Author(s): Miguel F. Martínez, Lucien Jezequel, Jens H. Bardarson, Thomas Klein Kvorning, and Julia D. Hannukainen

We present a framework for characterizing higher-order topological phases directly from the one-particle density matrix, without any reference to an underlying Hamiltonian. Our approach extends the mode-shell correspondence, originally formulated for single-particle Hamiltonians, to Gaussian states …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023320] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A framework for characterizing higher-order topological phases in amorphous materials using the one-particle density matrix.
motivation: To extend topological characterization to amorphous systems where traditional band-structure methods fail.
method: Extends the mode-shell correspondence to Gaussian states via the one-particle density matrix, without reference to a Hamiltonian.
result: Demonstrates that higher-order topological invariants can be computed from the density matrix, applicable to amorphous topological insulators.
conclusion: Provides a robust method for identifying topological phases in disordered systems, broadening the scope of topological classification.

title: Excited Eigenstates From A Two-species Random Walk
authors: Paul-Henry Glinel, Normand Beaudoin, And Alexandre Melanson
abstract:
Author(s): Paul-Henry Glinel, Normand Beaudoin, and Alexandre Melanson

Macroscopically, the population density function of random walk models can satisfy self-contained dynamics and exhibit unexpected order. Here, we show how a two-species random walk model that includes diffusion, probabilistic absorption of walkers mediated by a potential function, cross-species anni…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023324] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A two-species random walk model with diffusion, absorption, and cross-species annihilation is studied, showing emergent order in population density.
motivation: To understand how macroscopic order can arise from simple stochastic microscopic rules in multi-species systems.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of a two-species random walk with potential-mediated absorption and annihilation.
result: The population density function satisfies self-contained dynamics and exhibits unexpected order.
conclusion: The model demonstrates that complex emergent behavior can occur in random walk systems with multiple interacting species.

title: Theory Of High-harmonic Generation With Quantum Light
authors: Haoyu Liu, Hanxu Zhang, Xu Wang, And Jianmin Yuan
abstract:
Author(s): Haoyu Liu, Hanxu Zhang, Xu Wang, and Jianmin Yuan

High-harmonic generation (HHG) driven by intense quantum light has recently emerged as a new frontier in strong-field physics. Yet, the mechanism underlying HHG with nonclassical fields such as bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) light—characterized by a vanishing mean electric field—remains elusive. In th…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023326] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theory of high-harmonic generation driven by quantum light, specifically bright squeezed vacuum, revealing a new mechanism distinct from classical HHG.
motivation: To understand the mechanism of high-harmonic generation when driven by nonclassical light with vanishing mean electric field, which is not explained by classical strong-field physics.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework combining quantum optics and strong-field physics, likely using a combination of analytical and numerical methods to model HHG with bright squeezed vacuum.
result: They identify a new mechanism for HHG that relies on quantum fluctuations of the driving field, leading to distinct spectral and temporal features compared to classical HHG.
conclusion: Quantum light can drive HHG through a fundamentally different mechanism, opening new possibilities for controlling and probing strong-field processes with nonclassical light.

title: Before The Cycle Is Over: Subcycle Time Refraction At Optical Frequencies
authors: Ohad Segal, Noa Konforty, Oded Schiller, Maxwell J. Tolchin, Tony Yasniger, Soham Saha, Ryan W. Spangler, Jon-Paul Maria, Yonatan Plotnik, And Mordechai Segev
abstract:
Author(s): Ohad Segal, Noa Konforty, Oded Schiller, Maxwell J. Tolchin, Tony Yasniger, Soham Saha, Ryan W. Spangler, Jon-Paul Maria, Yonatan Plotnik, and Mordechai Segev

This work demonstrates subcycle order-unity variations in the refractive index at optical frequencies and measures the time-refraction of a probe wave propagating in the modulated medium.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022054] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates subcycle time refraction at optical frequencies by modulating refractive index on ultrafast timescales.
motivation: To achieve and measure order-unity refractive index changes within an optical cycle, enabling new regimes of light-matter interaction.
method: Experimental setup using ultrafast optical modulation to induce subcycle refractive index variations and probe wave time-refraction.
result: Observation of subcycle time refraction with order-unity index changes at optical frequencies.
conclusion: Subcycle refractive index modulation is feasible and can be measured, opening possibilities for ultrafast optical control.

title: Formation Of Bosonic $^{23}\mathrm{Na}^{41}\mathrm{K}$ Feshbach Molecules
authors: Sungjun Lee, Younghoon Lim, Jongyeol Kim, Jaeryeong Chang, And Jee Woo Park
abstract:
Author(s): Sungjun Lee, Younghoon Lim, Jongyeol Kim, Jaeryeong Chang, and Jee Woo Park

Ultracold Feshbach molecules are a crucial intermediate step for the creation of quantum degenerate gases of strongly dipolar molecules. After coherent transfer to the rovibrational ground state, these dimers can realize stable dipolar gases with strong, tunable long-range interactions. Here, we rep…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023307] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the formation of ultracold 23Na41K Feshbach molecules, a step toward creating quantum degenerate dipolar gases.
motivation: Ultracold Feshbach molecules are essential for producing strongly dipolar quantum gases with tunable long-range interactions, enabling studies of novel quantum phases.
method: The authors use magnetoassociation across a Feshbach resonance in a mixture of 23Na and 41K atoms, followed by coherent transfer to the rovibrational ground state.
result: They successfully create Feshbach molecules and characterize their properties, demonstrating a key step toward quantum degenerate dipolar gases.
conclusion: This work advances the experimental capability to produce ultracold dipolar molecules, which can be used for quantum simulation and many-body physics.

title: Observation Of Surface Ferromagnons In The Axion-insulating Phase Of The Antiferromagnetic Topological Insulator ${\mathrm{EuSn}}_{2}{\mathrm{As}}_{2}$
authors: Mamoun Hemmida, Santanu Pakhira, David C. Johnston, And Hans-Albrecht Krug von Nidda
abstract:
Author(s): Mamoun Hemmida, Santanu Pakhira, David C. Johnston, and Hans-Albrecht Krug von Nidda

We report the study of spin dynamics of [MATH] in the antiferromagnetic axion topological insulator [MATH] by means of antiferromagnetic resonance at 9.34 GHz. Below the Néel temperature ([MATH]), two types of resonance modes, the conventiona…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023309] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports antiferromagnetic resonance measurements in the topological insulator EuSn2As2, observing surface ferromagnons in the axion-insulating phase.
motivation: To study spin dynamics and surface magnetic excitations in a topological insulator with antiferromagnetic order, which is relevant for understanding axion electrodynamics in condensed matter.
method: Electron spin resonance (ESR) at 9.34 GHz was used to measure antiferromagnetic resonance modes below the Néel temperature.
result: Two resonance modes were observed: conventional antiferromagnetic resonance and a surface ferromagnon mode, indicating surface magnetic order.
conclusion: The observation of surface ferromagnons supports the existence of an axion-insulating phase in EuSn2As2, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Confinement And Finite-range Effects In A Quasi-two-dimensional Gas Of Fermionic Dimers
authors: Giovanni Midei, Jordi Boronat, And Grigory E. Astrakharchik
abstract:
Author(s): Giovanni Midei, Jordi Boronat, and Grigory E. Astrakharchik

A study of a gas of fermionic dimers in a quasi-two-dimensional geometry induced by strong harmonic confinement in one direction is presented. Fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo calculations are used to quantify the effects of confinement and finite interaction range on the equation of state and density profiles, with the results benchmarked against analytical theories.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022051] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A Monte Carlo study of fermionic dimers in a quasi-2D geometry, focusing on confinement and finite-range effects on the equation of state.
motivation: To understand how strong confinement and finite interaction range affect the properties of a gas of fermionic dimers, relevant to ultracold atomic systems.
method: Fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo simulations are used to compute the equation of state and density profiles, benchmarked against analytical theories.
result: Quantifies the effects of confinement and finite range, providing benchmarks for analytical models.
conclusion: The study provides insights into quasi-2D fermionic dimer gases but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Rare Cage Escapes Drive Relaxation In Deeply Supercooled Liquids
authors: Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, And Walter Kob
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, and Walter Kob

Simulations conducted significantly below the mode coupling temperature allow dynamic properties of glass forming systems to be uncovered.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021061] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Simulations of deeply supercooled liquids reveal that rare cage escapes drive relaxation dynamics.
motivation: Understanding relaxation in supercooled liquids is key to the glass transition problem.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations below the mode coupling temperature to analyze particle motion.
result: Relaxation is governed by rare events where particles escape from cages formed by neighbors.
conclusion: Rare cage escapes are the primary mechanism for structural relaxation in deeply supercooled liquids.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains, showing they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and are detectable via neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand the quantum dynamics of chiral solitons in spin chains, which are topological excitations with potential relevance to condensed matter physics.
method: A nonperturbative quantization approach is applied to chiral solitons in a spin chain model, analyzing their low-energy behavior and scattering properties.
result: Chiral solitons condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase, with signatures in inelastic neutron scattering.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for observing chiral solitons in experiments, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To develop a non-perturbative method for studying strongly coupled conformal field theories using the fuzzy sphere as a regularization scheme.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative geometry, to discretize the sphere and simulate fermionic CFTs via numerical methods.
result: They demonstrate that the fuzzy sphere can accurately capture the critical properties of free and interacting fermionic CFTs, and observe emergent supersymmetry in certain interacting models.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere provides a powerful tool for studying 3D fermionic CFTs and may enable exploration of non-perturbative phenomena such as emergent supersymmetry.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures, demonstrating three distinct magnetic phases in EuAg4Sb2.
motivation: To understand and control complex spin textures in moiré superlattices for potential information manipulation.
method: Neutron scattering and thermodynamic measurements combined with theoretical modeling to map spin textures.
result: Three tunable magnetic phases are identified, establishing a design framework for spin-based vortex lattices.
conclusion: The work provides a platform for engineering spin textures in moiré materials, relevant for spintronics but not directly for quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions.
motivation: To explore whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational hardness of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network using theoretical complexity arguments and algorithmic experiments.
result: Efficient algorithms are unable to find collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision-resistant.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for designing cryptographic protocols based on machine learning models.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: Understanding causal relationships in complex networks is crucial for predicting system behavior, but existing methods often lack a physical basis.
method: The authors develop a framework that incorporates physical principles to infer causal links from time-series data of network dynamics.
result: The framework accurately predicts physical links across various networked dynamical systems, outperforming standard causal inference methods.
conclusion: Physics-informed causal inference provides a robust approach for uncovering network structure and dynamics.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts anyonic exciton superfluidity in quantum Hall bilayers at topological criticality.
motivation: To explore exotic collective quantum states in fractional quantum Hall systems beyond the conventional paradigm.
method: Theoretical analysis using field theory and numerical methods to study bilayer quantum Hall systems near a topological phase transition.
result: Anyonic excitons form a superfluid phase with unique properties due to fractional statistics.
conclusion: Topological criticality provides a robust mechanism for engineering anyonic superfluids in quantum Hall bilayers.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
Author(s): Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, and Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
motivation: To understand the nature of the ground state and phase transition in the kagome ice compound HoAgGe, which exhibits spin ice behavior and potential hidden order.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements combined with neutron scattering and other techniques to probe the magnetic phase transition and symmetry breaking.
result: The transition belongs to the three-dimensional XY universality class, and the ground state shows hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
conclusion: The study provides experimental evidence for a 3D XY transition in a kagome ice system and reveals subtle symmetry breaking in the ground state.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the discovery of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature using ARPES.
motivation: Flat bands can host strongly correlated electron states, but they are often fragile or require low temperatures; this work aims to find a stable room-temperature platform.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) was used to measure the electronic band structure of layered transition-metal oxyhalides.
result: Intrinsic flat bands were observed that remain stable at room temperature, with orbital selectivity.
conclusion: These materials provide a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states at ambient conditions.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses magneto-optical spectroscopy to probe quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, demonstrating electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To investigate the quantum anomalous Hall phase in twisted bilayer WSe2 and understand the interplay between topology and magnetism in moiré materials.
method: Magneto-optical spectroscopy, specifically attractive polaron spectroscopy, is used to probe the electronic structure and magnetic ordering of twisted bilayer WSe2 under applied electric fields.
result: The experiments reveal a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and show that an electric field can switch between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: Twisted bilayer WSe2 is a promising platform for studying topological phases with tunable magnetism, relevant for future quantum devices.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, a topic in soft condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand the unusual critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids, which exhibit suppressed density fluctuations yet high susceptibility at the critical point.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly simulations to investigate the critical properties of hyperuniform fluids composed of spinning particles.
result: They find that hyperuniform fluids show suppressed critical opalescence but enhanced susceptibility, leading to a unique critical point.
conclusion: Hyperuniform fluids exhibit a distinct type of criticality that challenges standard theories of liquid-gas phase transitions.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, and Ivan J. Vera-Marun

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates ballistic spin transport and spin valve behavior in graphene using transverse magnetic focusing, a condensed matter physics experiment with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To realize a gate-tunable ballistic spin valve in graphene, leveraging electron optics for coherent spin control.
method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene devices, measuring spin-dependent transport.
result: Observation of ballistic spin transport and spin valve effect, with gate-tunable spin coherence.
conclusion: Graphene can serve as a platform for coherent spin control via electron optics, relevant for spintronics but not for the specified research directions.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum algorithm for computing persistence in topological data analysis, claiming exponential speedup.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a powerful tool for extracting features from data, but classical algorithms are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer speedups.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and sampling techniques to compute persistence diagrams.
result: They prove a provable exponential speedup over classical algorithms for certain instances of the problem.
conclusion: The work suggests that quantum computers could enable practical topological data analysis for large datasets, though practical implementation remains challenging.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A high-level perspective piece proposing a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, focusing on scientific milestones rather than technical results.
motivation: To outline a roadmap bridging the gap between current quantum computing capabilities and real-world applications.
method: Conceptual framework based on expert opinion and analysis of the field's progress.
result: A five-stage framework with milestones for quantum utility.
conclusion: The framework provides a structured path but lacks novel technical contributions.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, serving as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, and its approximation is a candidate for quantum advantage.
method: The authors design an end-to-end quantum algorithm that includes state preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They demonstrate the algorithm on small knots and show that the quantum computation yields results consistent with classical evaluations, validating the pipeline.
conclusion: The work establishes a practical benchmark for quantum computers and provides insights into the potential for quantum advantage in topological computations.

title: Photon Catalysis For General Multimode Multi-Photon Quantum State Preparation
authors: Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, And Massimo Frigerio
abstract:
Author(s): Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, and Massimo Frigerio

Using a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition, every photonic state can be prepared with realistic experimental tools and a predictable number of steps.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020323] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: A method for preparing arbitrary photonic states using symmetric tensor decomposition and photon catalysis.
motivation: To provide a systematic and experimentally feasible approach for generating complex multimode multi-photon quantum states.
method: The authors use symmetric tensor decomposition to represent target states and design a photon catalysis procedure to realize them with a predictable number of steps.
result: They show that any photonic state can be prepared using realistic experimental tools, with the number of steps determined by the tensor rank.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a universal and efficient way to prepare photonic states, advancing quantum state engineering.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, focusing on HHL and post-HHL developments.
motivation: Linear system solving is a central task in computation, and quantum algorithms promise exponential speedups for certain problems.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, block-encoding, quantum signal processing, and variable-time amplitude amplification.
result: It provides a taxonomy of QLSP algorithms, discusses their complexities, and surveys applications in machine learning, differential equations, and data fitting.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource requirements and noise.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge in 2D magnetism, which has seen rapid progress since 2016.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical results on 2D magnets, including topology, dynamics, and light-matter interactions.
result: The field encompasses ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topological phases, nonequilibrium dynamics, and spintronics.
conclusion: 2D van der Waals magnets offer a rich platform for fundamental physics and potential applications.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from frustrated lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing findings from multiple studies.
result: Kagome metals exhibit amplified correlation effects leading to states like orbital antiferromagnetism, flux phases, and electronic nematicity.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for exploring strongly correlated and topological electronic phases.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation, with broad applications to physical systems.
motivation: Spin glasses are a classic model for disordered systems, and understanding their dynamics is relevant to many fields, but the paper does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The review synthesizes experimental results, theoretical developments, and large-scale simulations of spin-glass dynamics.
result: The paper tracks progress in the field and highlights the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation, including future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich area for interdisciplinary study, but the paper is not aligned with the specified research interests.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on material candidates and topological properties.
motivation: To understand frustrated quantum magnets and their potential for realizing quantum spin liquids.
method: Review of theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental candidate materials.
result: Summarizes progress in identifying materials with Kitaev interactions and their topological features.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain a vibrant field with many open questions, offering insights into quantum magnetism.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to neural network data, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding coordinated activity in large neural networks is a key goal in neuroscience.
method: The authors review recent progress in using maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to analyze recordings from thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible behaviors and provide predictive power comparable to other areas of physics.
conclusion: Statistical physics offers a quantitative bridge between neural data and theoretical principles.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and their applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key photophysical process, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings is important for applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models used to describe internal conversion, including nonadiabatic dynamics and quantum chemistry approaches.
result: The review summarizes the current state of theoretical methods and identifies challenges and opportunities for incorporating these models into applied studies.
conclusion: Theoretical methods for internal conversion are mature but need further development to be effectively integrated into practical applications like photonics and energy harvesting.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review of quantum aspects of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their formation and quantum features.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are topological spin textures with potential applications in spintronics; understanding their quantum properties is important for future technologies.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on quantum interactions underlying skyrmion formation and quantum features of skyrmions themselves.
result: Discusses quantum-mechanical aspects such as quantum tunneling, superposition, and entanglement of skyrmions, as well as quantum effects in their interactions.
conclusion: Quantum properties of skyrmions open new avenues for fundamental physics and applications, but the field is still in early stages.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, including their potential connection to dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand possible new physics beyond the Standard Model, particularly spin-dependent forces mediated by exotic bosons that could explain dark matter and dark energy.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent interactions and surveys experimental techniques used to search for them, such as precision measurements with atomic, molecular, and optical systems.
result: The review summarizes current constraints on various exotic spin-dependent interactions and highlights the most sensitive experimental bounds.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain an active area of research with potential implications for fundamental symmetries and the nature of dark matter and dark energy.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on implementing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for quantum simulation.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries, enabling simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Reviews experimental and theoretical approaches for realizing synthetic quantum matter in fractal, curved, and higher-dimensional geometries using atomic, photonic, and electronic platforms.
result: Summarizes progress in engineering exotic geometries and discusses potential for simulating topological and gravitational models.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries is a rapidly advancing field with connections to condensed matter and high-energy physics, but the paper is a broad review without deep technical contributions to the user's specific directions.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of using massive quantum systems to probe gravity, including tests of quantum gravity effects and entanglement mediation.
motivation: To understand the interplay between quantum mechanics and gravity, which is poorly understood, and to explore experimental tests using massive quantum systems.
method: Review of theoretical proposals and experimental efforts, including matter-wave interferometry, optomechanics, and tests of gravity-induced entanglement.
result: Summarizes current theoretical models and experimental progress, highlighting that no definitive evidence of quantum gravity has been found yet.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to test quantum gravity, but further theoretical and experimental work is needed.

title: Real-Space Dynamic Electron Correlation In Beryllium
authors: Rudra B. Bista, Yuya Shinohara, Wojciech Dmowski, Chae Woo Ryu, Jung Ho Kim, Mary Upton, Hlynur Gretarsson, Martin Sundermann, And Takeshi Egami
abstract:
Author(s): Rudra B. Bista, Yuya Shinohara, Wojciech Dmowski, Chae Woo Ryu, Jung Ho Kim, Mary Upton, Hlynur Gretarsson, Martin Sundermann, and Takeshi Egami

The size of the exchange-correlation hole in beryllium is about 2 Å, but it extends up to about 5 Å at the plasmon excitation energy, demonstrating that electron correlations are affected significantly by electron dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256402] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies real-space dynamic electron correlation in beryllium using inelastic X-ray scattering, revealing that the exchange-correlation hole extends up to 5 Å at plasmon excitation energy.
motivation: Understanding electron correlation is fundamental to condensed matter physics, but this work focuses on electronic structure rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use inelastic X-ray scattering to measure the dynamic structure factor and reconstruct the exchange-correlation hole in real space.
result: The exchange-correlation hole size is about 2 Å at low energy but extends to about 5 Å at the plasmon excitation energy, showing significant dynamic effects.
conclusion: Electron correlations are significantly affected by electron dynamics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Antiferroaxial Altermagnetism
authors: Yichen Liu And Cheng-Cheng Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yichen Liu and Cheng-Cheng Liu

The antiferroaxial state is emerging as an important ferroic order in condensed matter systems. Here, we establish antiferroaxial altermagnetism as a broadly prevalent, generic, and microscopically grounded multiferroic mechanism, in which antiferroaxial counterrotating distortions both induce alter…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256709] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces antiferroaxial altermagnetism as a multiferroic mechanism combining antiferroaxial distortions and altermagnetism.
motivation: To establish a new multiferroic mechanism that couples antiferroaxial order with altermagnetism, potentially enabling novel magnetoelectric effects.
method: The authors use symmetry analysis and first-principles calculations to demonstrate the prevalence of antiferroaxial altermagnetism in various materials.
result: They show that antiferroaxial counterrotating distortions induce altermagnetic spin splitting, leading to a multiferroic state.
conclusion: Antiferroaxial altermagnetism is a generic and microscopically grounded multiferroic mechanism with potential for spintronic applications.

title: Novel Chiroptical Spectroscopy Technique
authors: Jorge Olmos-Trigo, Cristina Sanz-Fernández, And Ivan Fernandez-Corbaton
abstract:
Author(s): Jorge Olmos-Trigo, Cristina Sanz-Fernández, and Ivan Fernandez-Corbaton

Chiral objects typically exhibit a different extinction for the two circular polarizations of light. Researchers often detect the chirality of objects by measuring this extinction difference employing circular dichroism spectroscopy. In this Letter, we present a new spectroscopy technique for detect…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253802] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: A new chiroptical spectroscopy technique for detecting chirality via extinction difference of circular polarizations.
motivation: Chirality detection is important in chemistry and biology; existing circular dichroism spectroscopy has limitations.
method: The authors propose a novel spectroscopy technique that measures the extinction difference for circular polarizations.
result: The technique is demonstrated theoretically or experimentally (details not fully given).
conclusion: The new method offers an alternative approach to chiroptical spectroscopy.

title: Block-Type Antiferromagnetism In Single Chain Quasi-One-Dimensional ${\mathrm{K}}_{3}{\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}{\mathrm{Se}}_{4}$
authors: Fei Gao, Nikhil Dhale, Ling-Fang Lin, Keith M. Taddei, Yang Zhang, Clarina Dela Cruz, Elbio Dagotto, And Bing Lv
abstract:
Author(s): Fei Gao, Nikhil Dhale, Ling-Fang Lin, Keith M. Taddei, Yang Zhang, Clarina Dela Cruz, Elbio Dagotto, and Bing Lv

One-dimensional (1D) structures provide a unique platform to study the correlated quantum interactions and phase transitions such as unconventional magnetism and superconducting states. Here, we report that iron chalcogenide [MATH] exhibits an unusual bl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256706] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports an unusual block-type antiferromagnetic order in a quasi-one-dimensional iron chalcogenide, studied via neutron scattering and theoretical modeling.
motivation: To understand the magnetic ground state of K3Fe2Se4, which exhibits a block antiferromagnetic structure that is rare in 1D systems.
method: Single-crystal neutron diffraction and first-principles calculations were used to determine the magnetic structure and exchange interactions.
result: The material shows a block antiferromagnetic order with ferromagnetically coupled Fe dimers arranged antiferromagnetically along the chain.
conclusion: The block-type antiferromagnetism arises from competing exchange interactions and may be relevant to understanding magnetism in iron-based superconductors.

title: Critical Phenomenon Inside Asymptotically Flat Black Holes With Spontaneous Scalarization
authors: Li Li, Ze Sun, And Fu-Guo Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Li Li, Ze Sun, and Fu-Guo Yang

We study the nonlinear interior dynamics of spontaneously scalarized black holes in Einstein-Maxwell-scalar theory with zero cosmological constant, revealing novel critical phenomena. We demonstrate that, for a wide range of scalar-electromagnetic couplings, scalarized black holes possess no smooth …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251402] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
