result: Insights into melting and supercooling mechanisms at atomic scale.
conclusion: The study clarifies microscopic phase transition mechanisms, aiding design of thermal storage materials.

title: Modulation Of High-energy Electrons With A Nanopore Matter Lens
authors: Guangyi Huang, Wenhao He, Xian Li, And Changlin Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Guangyi Huang, Wenhao He, Xian Li, and Changlin Zheng

We demonstrate the modulation of high-energy electrons using a nanosized pore in solid as a strong electrostatic lens. The inner Coulomb potential of matter decreases rapidly from the edge of the pore toward the center, creating a strong electric field on the order of 10 GV/m. This electric field st…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023345] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates modulation of high-energy electrons using a nanopore in solid as a strong electrostatic lens.
motivation: To explore a new method for focusing and modulating high-energy electron beams using nanoscale structures.
method: The authors use a nanosized pore in a solid material, where the inner Coulomb potential creates a strong electric field (10 GV/m) that acts as a lens for high-energy electrons.
result: They show that the nanopore can effectively modulate the trajectory of high-energy electrons, achieving focusing effects.
conclusion: Nanopore matter lenses offer a novel approach for electron beam manipulation, with potential applications in electron microscopy and lithography.

title: Stochastic Acceleration Of Electrons In Fluctuating Fields Induced By Stimulated Raman Scattering In Subrelativistic Laser-plasma Interactions
authors: Yuji Takagi, Natsumi Iwata, Emmanuel D’humieres, Takayoshi Sano, And Yasuhiko Sentoku
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Takagi, Natsumi Iwata, Emmanuel d’Humieres, Takayoshi Sano, and Yasuhiko Sentoku

Stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) plays a crucial role in the energy conversion process from lasers to plasmas in the subrelativistic regime, where laser intensities range around [MATH]. SRS induces excitations of Langmuir waves (LWs) and density …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023342] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies stochastic acceleration of electrons via stimulated Raman scattering in subrelativistic laser-plasma interactions.
motivation: Understanding energy transfer from lasers to plasmas is important for inertial confinement fusion and plasma physics.
method: Particle-in-cell simulations and theoretical analysis of electron acceleration in fluctuating fields induced by SRS.
result: Electrons can be stochastically accelerated to high energies by the fluctuating electric fields from SRS-driven Langmuir waves.
conclusion: Stochastic acceleration is a key mechanism for hot electron generation in subrelativistic laser-plasma interactions.

title: High-stability Optical Clock Based On A Continuously Ground-state Cooled ${\mathrm{Al}}^{+}$ Ion Without Compromising Its Accuracy
authors: Fabian Dawel, Lennart Pelzer, Kai Dietze, Johannes Kramer, Marek Hild, Steven A. King, Nicolas C. H. Spethmann, Joshua Klose, Kilian Stahl, Sören Dörscher, Erik Benkler, Christian Lisdat, Sergey G. Porsev, Marianna S. Safronova, And Piet O. Schmidt
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Dawel, Lennart Pelzer, Kai Dietze, Johannes Kramer, Marek Hild, Steven A. King, Nicolas C. H. Spethmann, Joshua Klose, Kilian Stahl, Sören Dörscher, Erik Benkler, Christian Lisdat, Sergey G. Porsev, Marianna S. Safronova, and Piet O. Schmidt

Single-ion optical clocks have shown systematic frequency uncertainties below [MATH], but typically require more than one week of averaging to achieve a corresponding statistical uncertainty. This time can be reduced with longer probe times, but comes at the cost of a higher time-dilation shif…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023327] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a high-stability optical clock based on a single Al+ ion with continuous ground-state cooling, achieving reduced averaging time without compromising accuracy.
motivation: Single-ion optical clocks require long averaging times to reach statistical uncertainty; the goal is to reduce this time while maintaining systematic accuracy.
method: The authors implement continuous ground-state cooling of the Al+ ion and use a clock laser with improved stability, enabling longer probe times and faster averaging.
result: The clock achieves a statistical uncertainty of 1.0e-18 in 1000 seconds, a tenfold improvement over previous Al+ clocks, without degrading systematic uncertainty.
conclusion: Continuous ground-state cooling and improved laser stability enable high-stability optical clocks with reduced averaging time, advancing timekeeping precision.

title: Elastic And Structural Anisotropy In Silica Thin Films For Gravitational-Wave Detectors
authors: Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, And Silvia Corezzi
abstract:
Author(s): Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, and Silvia Corezzi

Researchers find that silica films in mirror coatings of gravitational-wave detectors have hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment. This discovery informs coating design and deposition and postprocessing strategies aimed at reducing thermal noise.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021036] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies elastic and structural anisotropy in silica thin films used in gravitational-wave detector mirror coatings, focusing on thermal noise reduction.
motivation: Thermal noise in mirror coatings limits the sensitivity of gravitational-wave detectors; understanding and mitigating anisotropy in silica films could improve performance.
method: The authors characterize the elastic and structural properties of silica thin films using experimental techniques to reveal hidden anisotropy and test the effects of heat treatment.
result: Silica films exhibit hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment, impacting their mechanical properties.
conclusion: The findings inform coating design and postprocessing strategies to reduce thermal noise in gravitational-wave detectors.

title: Effect Of Glass Stability On The Low Frequency Vibrations Of Vapor Deposited Glasses
authors: I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, And G. Baldi
abstract:
Author(s): I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, and G. Baldi

An improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique helps clarify the connections between complex vibrations and the properties of glasses.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021021] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies low-frequency vibrations in vapor-deposited glasses using improved inelastic x-ray scattering, focusing on glass stability effects.
motivation: Understanding the connection between complex vibrations and glass properties is important for materials science, but the paper does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors use an improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique to measure low-frequency vibrational modes in vapor-deposited glasses with varying stability.
result: They find correlations between glass stability and the low-frequency vibrational spectrum, providing insights into the boson peak and related phenomena.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of glass physics but has no direct relevance to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on the role of surface defects and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-voltage devices; understanding its mechanism is crucial for improving reliability.
method: The authors synthesize experimental observations and computer simulations to build a coherent mechanistic picture of the breakdown process.
result: A unified model emerges where tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact to trigger breakdown.
conclusion: These insights can guide the design of more robust accelerator structures and other high-power technologies.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: A review of radiation forces and torques in optics and acoustics, focusing on classical wave phenomena and particle manipulation.
motivation: To provide a unified perspective on how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in wave fields induce forces and torques on particles, with applications in trapping, sorting, and pulling.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and experimental demonstrations of optical and acoustic radiation forces and torques, emphasizing common principles.
result: It highlights the connection between wave momentum and spin densities and the resulting mechanical effects on particles, including novel pulling forces.
conclusion: The review consolidates knowledge across optics and acoustics, offering insights for future applications in particle manipulation and microfluidics.

title: Pressure Effects On Metals, Alloys, And Compounds Of Transplutonium Elements
authors: Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, And Thomas E. Albrecht
abstract:
Author(s): Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, and Thomas E. Albrecht

Materials containing transplutonium elements (the actinides Am–Cm that come after Pu in the periodic table) are important for nuclear power, nuclear waste management, and long-term storage. They also have fascinating properties, with 5
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A review of the physics and chemistry of transplutonium elements under high pressure, focusing on their electronic properties and behavior in metals, alloys, and compounds.
motivation: Transplutonium elements are important for nuclear power and waste management, and their 5f electrons exhibit unique localized/itinerant behavior under pressure.
method: The paper reviews experimental and theoretical studies of transplutonium materials under high pressure, including traditional metals, alloys, and coordination complexes.
result: The review summarizes the current understanding of how pressure affects the electronic structure and properties of these materials.
conclusion: The work expands knowledge of transplutonium materials but is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational waves and X-ray pulse profiles.
motivation: To understand the behavior of matter at extreme densities found in neutron stars, which is crucial for nuclear physics and astrophysics.
method: Summarizes recent observational results from gravitational-wave detections of binary neutron star mergers and X-ray pulse profile measurements, comparing them to theoretical predictions of the nuclear equation of state.
result: Provides constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, and compares them to extrapolations of nuclear equation of state models.
conclusion: Neutron star observations offer unique insights into dense matter, but further data are needed to discriminate between competing theoretical models.

title: Nobel Lecture: Boltzmann Machines
authors: Geoffrey Hinton
abstract:
Author(s): Geoffrey Hinton

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030502] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: This is the Nobel lecture by Geoffrey Hinton on Boltzmann machines, a foundational concept in machine learning, not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The lecture presents the development and significance of Boltzmann machines in the context of artificial neural networks and machine learning.
method: The paper describes the architecture and learning algorithm of Boltzmann machines, including hidden units and stochastic dynamics.
result: Boltzmann machines can learn complex probability distributions and serve as building blocks for deep learning models.
conclusion: Boltzmann machines have been influential in machine learning, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the paper reviews three real-space techniques to address this challenge.
method: The authors review scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined use for a complete picture of defects.
result: The review highlights how these techniques can directly access atomic-scale disorder information in compound semiconductors.
conclusion: Combining multiple real-space probes provides a more comprehensive understanding of defects in semiconductors.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: A review of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonances.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions at stellar energies is crucial for astrophysics but difficult to measure directly.
method: Summarizes theoretical approaches for low-energy nuclear reactions, including tunneling, resonances, and interference effects.
result: Provides an overview of the state-of-the-art in stellar nuclear reaction theory and experimental techniques.
conclusion: Quantum mechanical effects dominate stellar reactions, and new methods are needed to study them on Earth.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of all available data.
motivation: Accurate and consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology, requiring periodic updates as new measurements become available.
method: A least-squares adjustment is performed on a global dataset of measurements and theoretical calculations, incorporating correlations and uncertainties to produce self-consistent constant values.
result: The 2022 set of recommended values for fundamental constants and conversion factors is provided, along with their uncertainties.
conclusion: The CODATA recommended values serve as the internationally accepted standard for fundamental constants, supporting precision measurements and theoretical work across physics and chemistry.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in active matter systems, focusing on how active units align their orientation with their velocity, leading to novel collective behaviors.
motivation: To understand and unify the phenomenon of self-alignment in active matter, which has implications for biology, smart materials, and robotics.
method: The paper reviews existing models and experiments on self-alignment, presenting a unified mathematical and conceptual framework.
result: Self-alignment enables a spectrum of behaviors from single-particle orbits to synchronized motion in dense assemblies.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a fundamental property that reshapes motion in active systems, with potential for groundbreaking applications.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This review discusses optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser-induced ultrasound to image deep tissues with optical contrast.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers noninvasive deep-tissue imaging with high resolution.
method: The paper reviews the basic physics of optoacoustic signal generation, detection, and recent developments in multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: Optoacoustic microscopy can achieve high-resolution imaging at depths of millimeters to centimeters, providing optical contrast in biological tissues.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological and clinical research, with ongoing developments in multimodal imaging.

title: Wrinkles, Creases, And Cusps In Growing Soft Matter
authors: Martine Ben Amar
abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

The buckling of a material surface subject to compression or growth is a ubiquitous phenomenon, arising in materials science contexts such as the swelling of gels as well as in biological contexts such as morphogenesis and embryogenesis. A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory. This review presents a modern treatment of the Biot instability, integrating many standard techniques of nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, such as bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015004] Published Mon Feb 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of buckling instabilities in growing soft matter using nonlinear elasticity theory.
motivation: Understanding creases and cusps in soft materials is important for morphogenesis and materials science.
method: The review integrates bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and nonlinear elasticity to analyze the Biot instability.
result: Provides a modern treatment of buckling patterns in growing soft matter.
conclusion: Nonlinear elasticity is essential to fully describe the observed instabilities.

title: Wannier-function Software Ecosystem For Materials Simulations
authors: Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, And Giovanni Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, and Giovanni Pizzi

The description of the electronic structure in terms of extended Bloch states has made it possible to understand and calculate many properties in condensed-matter physics. However, understanding and insight often require a local description, and Wannier functions provide an exact and insightful map of extended reciprocal-space Bloch states into localized real-space orbitals. Applications range far and wide, from ultra-accurate integrations to topological invariants, and their widespread uptake by the electronic-structure community has resulted in a growing and interoperable ecosystem of methods and associated software tools. This review provides a description of this ecosystem that has now become a major instrument for the electronic-structure community in its pursuit of understanding, discovering, and designing materials.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045008] Published Mon Dec 23, 2024.
tldr: A review of the Wannier-function software ecosystem for materials simulations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the methods and tools for constructing and using Wannier functions in electronic structure calculations.
method: The paper surveys the ecosystem of software packages (e.g., Wannier90) and their applications, describing the underlying theory and interoperability.
result: The review catalogs the capabilities of the software ecosystem, including applications to topological invariants, Berry phases, and accurate integrations.
conclusion: Wannier functions are a powerful tool for condensed-matter physics, and the software ecosystem enables a wide range of materials simulations.

title: Transient Large-Scale Anisotropy In TeV Cosmic Rays Due To An Interplanetary Coronal Mass Ejection
authors: Zhen Cao et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen Cao et al. (LHAASO Collaboration)

A solar storm hitting Earth appears to have reduced the amount of incoming high-energy cosmic rays, suggesting a new way of measuring solar activity.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251002] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a transient large-scale anisotropy in TeV cosmic rays caused by an interplanetary coronal mass ejection, as observed by the LHAASO collaboration.
motivation: To study the effect of solar activity on high-energy cosmic rays and explore a new method for measuring solar storms.
method: Analysis of cosmic ray data from the LHAASO observatory during a solar storm event.
result: A reduction in incoming high-energy cosmic rays was observed, correlated with the interplanetary coronal mass ejection.
conclusion: Solar storms can modulate cosmic ray flux at TeV energies, offering a new probe of solar activity.

title: Pattern Formation During Melting Of Lamellar Eutectics
authors: Rahul Nellissery Rajan, Rajesh Kumari Rajendran, Guillaume Boussinot, Kamal Sbargoud, Sabine Bottin-Rousseau, And Silvère Akamatsu
abstract:
Author(s): Rahul Nellissery Rajan, Rajesh Kumari Rajendran, Guillaume Boussinot, Kamal Sbargoud, Sabine Bottin-Rousseau, and Silvère Akamatsu

A rich diversity of patterns emerge during melting of a two-phase eutectic solid.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256301] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies pattern formation during melting of lamellar eutectics, a topic in materials science and solidification physics.
motivation: Understanding pattern formation in eutectic melting is important for controlling microstructure in materials processing.
method: Experimental observation and theoretical analysis of melting dynamics in two-phase eutectic solids.
result: A rich diversity of patterns emerge during melting, revealing complex dynamics.
conclusion: The study provides insights into pattern formation mechanisms in eutectic systems.

title: Synthetic Spatiotemporal Plasmonic Vortices On Chip
authors: Qian Chen, Shuoshuo Zhang, Guoyu Xian, Haoqiang Hu, Xiaohua Wu, Xiaofei Wu, Jer-Shing Huang, Chen-Bin Huang, Jin-Hui Zhong, Yuquan Zhang, Xiaocong Yuan, Changjun Min, And Yanan Dai
abstract:
Author(s): Qian Chen, Shuoshuo Zhang, Guoyu Xian, Haoqiang Hu, Xiaohua Wu, Xiaofei Wu, Jer-Shing Huang, Chen-Bin Huang, Jin-Hui Zhong, Yuquan Zhang, Xiaocong Yuan, Changjun Min, and Yanan Dai

Spatiotemporal vortices are polychromatic modes that intertwine orbital angular momentum in space and time. Here, we introduce a new class of such vortices, “spatiotemporal plasmonic vortices,” carrying nontrivial topological spin textures. They are generated by chronotopic interference of temporall…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256903] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces synthetic spatiotemporal plasmonic vortices on a chip, which are polychromatic modes carrying topological spin textures generated by chronotopic interference of temporally and spatially structured light.
motivation: To create a new class of spatiotemporal vortices in plasmonic systems, enabling nontrivial topological spin textures on a chip.
method: The authors use chronotopic interference of temporally and spatially structured light to generate spatiotemporal plasmonic vortices.
result: They demonstrate the generation of spatiotemporal plasmonic vortices with nontrivial topological spin textures.
conclusion: This work expands the concept of spatiotemporal vortices to plasmonic platforms, potentially enabling new applications in nanophotonics and spin-orbit coupling.

title: Search For Dark Matter Induced Airglow In Planetary Atmospheres
authors: Carlos Blanco, Rebecca K. Leane, Marianne Moore, And Joshua Tong
abstract:
Author(s): Carlos Blanco, Rebecca K. Leane, Marianne Moore, and Joshua Tong

We point out that dark matter (DM) can illuminate planetary skies via ultraviolet airglow. Dark matter annihilation products can excite molecular hydrogen, which then deexcites to produce ultraviolet emission in the Lyman and Werner bands. We search for this new effect by analyzing nightside ultravi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251001] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper searches for dark matter annihilation signals in planetary atmospheres via ultraviolet airglow.
motivation: Dark matter annihilation could produce UV emission in planetary atmospheres, providing a new detection method.
method: The authors analyze nightside ultraviolet observations of planetary atmospheres to search for excess emission from dark matter annihilation products exciting molecular hydrogen.
result: No significant dark matter signal is found, and constraints are placed on dark matter annihilation cross-sections.
conclusion: Planetary atmospheres can be used as dark matter detectors, but current data show no evidence of dark matter induced airglow.

title: Short Strings In Three-Dimensional Anti–de Sitter Space: From Weak To Strong Coupling
authors: Simon Ekhammar, Nikolay Gromov, Bogdan Stefański, Jr., And Charles Thull
abstract:
Author(s): Simon Ekhammar, Nikolay Gromov, Bogdan Stefański, Jr., and Charles Thull

We numerically solve the conjectured quantum spectral curve for strings on [MATH] with Ramond-Ramond charge from weak to strong coupling. At strong coupling, the spectrum organizes into flat-space string mass levels with universal square-root s…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251603] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves the quantum spectral curve for strings in AdS3 with Ramond-Ramond charge, studying the spectrum from weak to strong coupling.
motivation: To understand the spectrum of short strings in three-dimensional anti-de Sitter space, which is a key problem in string theory and holography.
method: Numerical solution of the conjectured quantum spectral curve, an integrability-based method.
result: At strong coupling, the spectrum organizes into flat-space string mass levels with universal square-root scaling.
conclusion: The work provides a non-perturbative check of the quantum spectral curve and reveals the structure of the string spectrum in AdS3.

title: Curvature Instability Of An Active Gel Growing On A Wavy Membrane
authors: Kristiana Mihali, Dennis Wörthmüller, And Pierre Sens
abstract:
Author(s): Kristiana Mihali, Dennis Wörthmüller, and Pierre Sens

Cell shape changes are largely controlled by the actin cytoskeleton, a dynamic filament network beneath the plasma membrane. Several cell types can form extended freestanding protrusions not supported by an extracellular substrate or matrix, and regulated by proteins sensitive to the cell membrane c…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 258401] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the curvature instability of an active gel growing on a wavy membrane, focusing on cell shape changes and actin cytoskeleton dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how cells form freestanding protrusions without extracellular support is important for cell biology, but the topic is far from quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors model an active gel (actin network) growing on a deformable membrane with wavy curvature, analyzing the instability using linear stability analysis and continuum mechanics.
result: They find that the active gel growth can be unstable to curvature perturbations, leading to pattern formation on the membrane.
conclusion: The work provides insights into mechanical instabilities in active biological systems, but has no connection to quantum computing, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Black Hole Mergers Beyond General Relativity: A Self-Force Approach
authors: Ayush Roy, Lorenzo Küchler, Adam Pound, And Rodrigo Panosso Macedo
abstract:
Author(s): Ayush Roy, Lorenzo Küchler, Adam Pound, and Rodrigo Panosso Macedo

A modular framework within the self-force formalism that applies to a large class of effective field theories of gravity in order to perform tests of general relativity with binary black hole mergers is critical for tests of general relativity that make use of the upcoming space-based gravitational wave detectors such as LISA.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251404] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a self-force formalism for testing general relativity with black hole mergers, focusing on gravitational wave astrophysics.
motivation: To enable tests of general relativity using upcoming gravitational wave detectors like LISA by modeling black hole mergers beyond general relativity.
method: A modular framework within the self-force formalism is applied to effective field theories of gravity.
result: The framework allows for systematic calculations of gravitational waveforms in modified gravity theories.
conclusion: The approach provides a pathway to constrain deviations from general relativity with future gravitational wave observations.

title: Relating Rates Of Global Change, Evolutionary Adaptation, And Extinction
authors: Daniel H. Rothman And Sergei Petrovskii
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel H. Rothman and Sergei Petrovskii

It is widely assumed that extinction occurs when environmental change outpaces a species’ capacity to adapt. However, this hypothesis lacks support at the scale of global change, in part because the distribution of adaptation rates is unknown. Here, we test this idea by formulating a general model t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 254201] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper models the relationship between global environmental change rates, species adaptation rates, and extinction risk using a general mathematical framework.
motivation: To test the hypothesis that extinction occurs when environmental change outpaces adaptation, and to understand the distribution of adaptation rates at a global scale.
method: Formulates a general model linking rates of global change, evolutionary adaptation, and extinction, likely using differential equations or stochastic processes.
result: The model provides a quantitative relationship between change rates and extinction probability, potentially identifying critical thresholds.
conclusion: The findings support the idea that extinction risk increases when environmental change exceeds adaptive capacity, with implications for biodiversity conservation.

title: How The Oblique Drift Instability Alters Solar Wind Heating And Constrains The Distribution Of Solar Wind Observations
authors: Mihailo M. Martinović, Kristopher G. Klein, Leon Ofman, Yogesh, Gregory G. Howes, Jaye L. Verniero, Peter H. Yoon, Daniel Verscharen, And Benjamin L. Alterman
abstract:
Author(s): Mihailo M. Martinović, Kristopher G. Klein, Leon Ofman, Yogesh, Gregory G. Howes, Jaye L. Verniero, Peter H. Yoon, Daniel Verscharen, and Benjamin L. Alterman

Ion-driven plasma instability thresholds, derived from linear theory, constrain the distribution of solar observations in parameter space, defining boundaries of stable plasma parameters. Excursions beyond these thresholds result in the emission of energy, transferred from particles to coherent elec…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 255201] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the oblique drift instability in solar wind plasma, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To understand how ion-driven plasma instabilities constrain solar wind observations and affect heating.
method: Linear theory and analysis of solar wind data to identify instability thresholds.
result: The oblique drift instability alters solar wind heating and constrains the distribution of observed plasma parameters.
conclusion: The instability plays a key role in solar wind dynamics, but the work is purely classical plasma physics.

title: Flexible Gravitational-Wave Parameter Estimation With Transformers
authors: Annalena Kofler, Maximilian Dax, Stephen R. Green, Jonas Wildberger, Nihar Gupte, Jakob H. Macke, Jonathan Gair, Alessandra Buonanno, And Bernhard Schölkopf
abstract:
Author(s): Annalena Kofler, Maximilian Dax, Stephen R. Green, Jonas Wildberger, Nihar Gupte, Jakob H. Macke, Jonathan Gair, Alessandra Buonanno, and Bernhard Schölkopf

Gravitational-wave data analysis relies on accurate and efficient methods to extract physical information from noisy detector signals, yet the increasing rate and complexity of observations represent a growing challenge. Deep learning provides a powerful alternative to traditional inference, but exi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251401] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies transformer neural networks to gravitational-wave parameter estimation, achieving fast and accurate inference from noisy detector signals.
motivation: Gravitational-wave data analysis requires efficient methods to handle increasing observation rates and complexity; traditional inference is computationally expensive.
method: The authors develop a transformer-based deep learning model that directly maps detector strain data to posterior distributions over source parameters, trained on simulated signals.
result: The transformer achieves competitive accuracy with established methods while being orders of magnitude faster, and demonstrates flexibility across different noise conditions and waveform models.
conclusion: Transformers offer a scalable and accurate approach for real-time gravitational-wave parameter estimation, with potential for broader application in time-series inference tasks.

title: Quantum Damping Of Cosmological Shear: A New Prediction From Loop Quantum Cosmologies
authors: Wen-Cong Gan, Leila L. Graef, Rudnei O. Ramos, Gustavo S. Vicente, And Anzhong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Cong Gan, Leila L. Graef, Rudnei O. Ramos, Gustavo S. Vicente, and Anzhong Wang

We study the dynamics of the Bianchi I universe in modified loop quantum cosmology (mLQC-I) and uncover a robust mechanism for isotropization: the shear is dynamically suppressed after the bounce and decays rapidly in the quantum postbounce regime, independently of the equation of state of standard …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251501] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of Bianchi I universe in loop quantum cosmology, predicting a quantum damping of cosmological shear.
motivation: To understand the isotropization mechanism in the early universe within the framework of loop quantum cosmology.
method: The authors analyze the modified loop quantum cosmology (mLQC-I) model for Bianchi I spacetime and derive the evolution of shear.
result: They find that shear is dynamically suppressed after the bounce and decays rapidly in the quantum postbounce regime, independent of the equation of state.
conclusion: Loop quantum cosmology provides a robust isotropization mechanism, which is a new prediction of the theory.

title: Test Of $cp$ Symmetry In The Neutral Decays Of $\mathrm{Λ}$ Via $J/ψ→\mathrm{Λ}\overline{\mathrm{Λ}}$
authors: M. Ablikim et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): M. Ablikim et al. (BESIII Collaboration)

Using [MATH] events collected with the BESIII detector, a full angular analysis is carried out on the process [MATH]. The decay parameters [MATH] for [MATH] an…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251802] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper tests CP symmetry in neutral decays of Λ hyperons using J/ψ→ΛΛ¯ events from BESIII.
motivation: CP violation is a key phenomenon in particle physics, and testing it in hyperon decays provides a sensitive probe of the Standard Model.
method: A full angular analysis of the decay J/ψ→ΛΛ¯ is performed using 10 billion J/ψ events collected by the BESIII detector.
result: The decay parameters for Λ and Λ¯ are measured, and CP symmetry is tested by comparing them.
conclusion: The results are consistent with CP conservation within uncertainties.

title: Differential Momentum Measurement Of Strong-field Double Ionization Of Mg Atoms
authors: Libin Zheng, Linna Zhang, Huipeng Kang, And Xiaojun Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Libin Zheng, Linna Zhang, Huipeng Kang, and Xiaojun Liu

The authors have developed a time-of-flight spectrometer combining laser ablation with the supersonic molecular beam technique, which enables differential momentum measurement of nonsequential double ionization of Mg in strong laser fields. The experimental result provides direct evidence for the intermediate pathway of double ionization.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061101] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental differential momentum measurements of strong-field double ionization of Mg atoms using a time-of-flight spectrometer.
motivation: To investigate the intermediate pathway of nonsequential double ionization in strong laser fields.
method: A time-of-flight spectrometer combining laser ablation with supersonic molecular beam technique was developed to measure differential momentum of ions.
result: The experimental results provide direct evidence for the intermediate pathway of double ionization.
conclusion: The technique enables detailed momentum-resolved studies of strong-field double ionization.

title: Interband Transition-pathway Control Of High-order Harmonics In MgO Driven By Combined Pulses
authors: Yue Qiao, Yupeng Zhang, Ping Chen, Yong Liu, Jigen Chen, Shicheng Jiang, And Yujun Yang
abstract:

Based on the multiband strong-field approximation model, we perform a pathway-resolved analysis of high-order harmonic generation in bulk MgO crystals under monochromatic infrared laser and combined pulses. The results show that under the driving of monochromatic infrared pulse, due to the large ene…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063527] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies high-order harmonic generation in MgO crystals using combined laser pulses, focusing on interband transition pathways.
motivation: To understand and control high-order harmonic generation in solids for potential applications in attosecond science and strong-field physics.
method: Uses a multiband strong-field approximation model to perform pathway-resolved analysis of harmonic generation under monochromatic and combined pulses.
result: Identifies that combined pulses can selectively enhance or suppress specific interband transition pathways, leading to control over harmonic spectra.
conclusion: Pathway control via combined pulses offers a method to manipulate high-order harmonics in solids, relevant for ultrafast optics.

title: Spin-orbit-coupling Effect In Resonant Multiphoton Ionization Dynamics
authors: Chang-Tong Liang, Xianhong Zeng, Shilin Hu, Xuanyang Lai, And Jing Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Chang-Tong Liang, Xianhong Zeng, Shilin Hu, Xuanyang Lai, and Jing Chen

Spin-resolved strong-field dynamics have recently emerged as a frontier in ultrafast and nonlinear optics, with growing evidence that spin effects can critically influence strong-field phenomena. Motivated by experimental observations of potassium atoms in atomic ionization in strong laser fields, w…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063112] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-orbit coupling effects in resonant multiphoton ionization dynamics of potassium atoms in strong laser fields.
motivation: Recent experiments show spin effects can critically influence strong-field phenomena, motivating a theoretical investigation of spin-orbit coupling in multiphoton ionization.
method: The authors perform theoretical calculations and simulations of spin-resolved strong-field dynamics for potassium atoms, incorporating spin-orbit coupling.
result: They find that spin-orbit coupling significantly affects the ionization dynamics and spin polarization of photoelectrons.
conclusion: Spin-orbit coupling is an important factor in strong-field ionization and must be considered for accurate modeling.

title: Stability Of Lithium-xenon Compounds At High Pressures
authors: Xiaomeng Wang, Pei Zhou, Junjie Wang, Chi Ding, Qing Lu, Yu Han, Yang Ni, And Zhijie Cao
abstract:

Using crystal structure prediction and first-principles calculations, we show that the Li-Xe system exhibits diverse structural, electronic, and dynamical behaviors under pressure. Lithium-rich phases display electride character, with interstitial electrons dominating the states at the Fermi level, …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214113] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies high-pressure lithium-xenon compounds, focusing on crystal structure prediction and electronic properties.
motivation: To explore novel compounds and electride behavior under extreme conditions.
method: Crystal structure prediction and first-principles DFT calculations.
result: Identified stable Li-Xe phases with electride character at high pressures.
conclusion: Li-Xe system shows diverse pressure-induced structural and electronic transitions.

title: Parabolic Focusing Of Water Waves Via A Straight Reflector Based On The Space Transformation Method
authors: Zhigang Zhang, Chenxu Zhang, Chi Zhang, Takahito Iida, And Xiangqian Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhigang Zhang, ChenXu Zhang, Chi Zhang, Takahito Iida, and Xiangqian Zhu

Water-wave focusing is a significant technology for enhancing wave energy density, which can effectively improve the efficiency of the wave energy converter. To achieve parabolic focusing of water waves using a straight boundary, the space transformation method (STM) was employed to map a parabolic …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065110] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses space transformation method to design a straight reflector that achieves parabolic focusing of water waves for wave energy conversion.
motivation: To enhance wave energy density and improve efficiency of wave energy converters by focusing water waves using a simple straight boundary.
method: The space transformation method (STM) maps a parabolic reflector to a straight boundary, enabling parabolic focusing with a straight reflector.
result: The designed straight reflector can focus water waves parabolically, as demonstrated theoretically or numerically.
conclusion: The space transformation method provides a way to achieve parabolic focusing with a straight reflector, potentially improving wave energy converter performance.

title: Theory And Simulation Of Turbulence Driven By Momentum Transfer From Material Emitting High-energy Particles
authors: S. E. Kuratov, A. Yu. Mikulin, S. I. Glazyrin, And D. S. Shidlovski

The development of hydrodynamic instabilities may be significantly affected by the presence of suprathermal high-energy particles (HEPs). These effects are particularly pronounced in high-energy-density plasmas. We develop a single-equation diffusion-type turbulence model that describes the turbulen…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065111] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a turbulence model for high-energy-density plasmas driven by momentum transfer from high-energy particles.
motivation: To understand how suprathermal high-energy particles affect hydrodynamic instabilities in high-energy-density plasmas.
method: A single-equation diffusion-type turbulence model is developed and simulated.
result: The model describes turbulent kinetic energy evolution under the influence of high-energy particles.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for turbulence in plasmas with high-energy particles, relevant to astrophysical and fusion contexts.

title: Selective Wave Transmission In Strongly Nonlinear Disordered Granular Chains
authors: João Guilherme Pinto de Freitas, Luis Paulo Silveira Machado, And Surajit Sen
abstract:

Chains of 1000 granules in mutual contact, without precompression, and with random radii that follow a normal distribution are studied numerically. The standard deviation [MATH] controls the disorder level. The chains are subject to (i) a striker impact and (ii) an actuator that imposes band-limited wh…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065426] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Numerical study of wave transmission in disordered granular chains under impact and band-limited white noise.
motivation: To understand how disorder affects wave propagation in strongly nonlinear granular systems without precompression.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations of 1000-granule chains with random radii following a normal distribution, excited by striker impact or actuator with band-limited white noise.
result: Selective wave transmission is observed depending on disorder level and excitation type.
conclusion: Disorder can be used to control wave transmission in granular chains, with potential applications in shock absorption or energy harvesting.

title: Analytic Theory Of Shear Localization In Amorphous Solids Confined By Couette Geometry
authors: Yang Fu, Yuliang Jin, And Itamar Procaccia

Couette geometry refers to two concentric rings in two dimensions (or cylinders) in three dimensions with a medium in between. Typically, the inner and outer rings (or cylinders) rotate at different rates and the response of the medium is studied. Here we study a medium which is a two-dimensional am…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065509] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an analytic theory for shear localization in amorphous solids confined by Couette geometry.
motivation: Understanding shear localization in amorphous solids is important for material science and engineering applications.
method: The authors derive analytic expressions for the velocity profile and stress distribution using continuum mechanics and plasticity theory.
result: They obtain closed-form solutions that predict the width and location of shear bands as functions of system parameters.
conclusion: The analytic theory successfully captures the key features of shear localization observed in simulations and experiments.

title: Nonlinear Bubble Resonance: Geometric Mechanisms And Onset Scaling
authors: Shilin Yu, Wenbao Zheng, Chao Zeng, And Wen Deng
abstract:
Author(s): Shilin Yu, Wenbao Zheng, Chao Zeng, and Wen Deng

The oscillatory dynamics of trapped nonwetting fluids in pore constrictions influence multiphase flow and transient fluid mobility in geologic media. Although the small-amplitude linear response is relatively well understood, the mechanism responsible for nonlinear behavior at finite-amplitudes rema…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065109] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonlinear bubble resonance in pore constrictions, focusing on geometric mechanisms and onset scaling.
motivation: Understanding nonlinear oscillatory dynamics of trapped nonwetting fluids is important for multiphase flow in geologic media, but the mechanism for finite-amplitude nonlinear behavior is not well understood.
method: The authors analyze the oscillatory dynamics of trapped nonwetting fluids in pore constrictions, likely using theoretical modeling or numerical simulations to study geometric effects and scaling.
result: The paper identifies geometric mechanisms responsible for nonlinear resonance and characterizes the onset scaling of nonlinear behavior.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into nonlinear fluid dynamics in porous media, but the work is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: From Spark To Conflagration: A Multiscale Thermodynamic-percolation Framework For Wildland-fire Spread
authors: Xiaoping Shi, Mir Faizal, Arshid Shabir, And Behnam Pourhassan
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaoping Shi, Mir Faizal, Arshid Shabir, and Behnam Pourhassan

Wildland fire operates across multiple spatial and temporal scales, linking local combustion chemistry and turbulent heat transport to continental patterns of burned area. A quantitative bridge between microscale ignition physics and macroscale propagation has remained elusive because operational si…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064143] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a multiscale thermodynamic-percolation framework for wildland-fire spread, bridging microscale ignition to macroscale propagation.
motivation: A quantitative bridge between microscale ignition physics and macroscale fire propagation has been missing in operational fire models.
method: The authors combine thermodynamic principles with percolation theory across multiple spatial and temporal scales.
result: The framework successfully links local combustion and heat transport to large-scale burned area patterns.
conclusion: The multiscale approach provides a new tool for understanding and predicting wildland-fire spread.

title: Evolution Of Localized Pulses In The Defocusing Modified Korteweg–de Vries Equation Theory
authors: L. F. Calazans de Brito, A. Gammal, And A. M. Kamchatnov
abstract:
Author(s): L. F. Calazans de Brito, A. Gammal, and A. M. Kamchatnov

In this work, we develop, in the Gurevich-Pitaevskii framework, an analytic theory for the evolution of localized pulses in the defocusing modified Korteweg–de Vries equation theory for situations when a dispersive shock does not eventually transform into a sequence of well-separated solitons. We fo…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064208] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an analytic theory for the evolution of localized pulses in the defocusing modified Korteweg–de Vries equation, focusing on dispersive shock waves and soliton dynamics.
motivation: To understand the evolution of localized pulses in nonlinear wave systems where dispersive shocks do not break into well-separated solitons.
method: Uses the Gurevich-Pitaevskii framework to derive analytic solutions for pulse evolution in the defocusing mKdV equation.
result: Provides an analytic description of pulse evolution and dispersive shock formation in the mKdV equation.
conclusion: The work extends the understanding of nonlinear wave dynamics in integrable systems, with potential applications in fluid dynamics and optics.

title: Unsteady Phase Waves In The One-dimensional Swarmalator Model With Inertia
authors: Kevin O'keeffe
abstract:
Author(s): Kevin O'Keeffe

We study a one-dimensional swarmalator model with inertia. Previous studies have focused almost exclusively on the overdamped limit. We find inertia introduces an unsteady collective state in which the rainbow order parameters undergo multiharmonic oscillations. This “thrashing” phase wave bifurcate…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064210] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a one-dimensional swarmalator model with inertia, discovering a new unsteady collective state called 'thrashing' phase waves.
motivation: Previous studies of swarmalator models focused on the overdamped limit; this work aims to understand the effect of inertia on collective dynamics.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional swarmalator model with inertia using analytical and numerical methods, examining the bifurcation of rainbow order parameters.
result: Inertia introduces multiharmonic oscillations in the rainbow order parameters, leading to a 'thrashing' phase wave state.
conclusion: Inertia can fundamentally alter the collective behavior of swarmalators, producing unsteady states not present in the overdamped regime.

title: Effect Of Temporary Lockdowns On Disease Extinction Risk In Assortative Networks
authors: Elad Korngut And Michael Assaf
abstract:
Author(s): Elad Korngut and Michael Assaf

Changing environmental conditions can significantly affect the dynamics of disease spread. These changes may arise naturally or result from human interventions; in the latter case, lockdown measures that lead to abrupt but temporary reductions in transmission rates are used to combat disease spread.…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064309] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of temporary lockdowns on disease extinction in assortative networks using stochastic modeling.
motivation: Understanding how human interventions like lockdowns affect disease spread is crucial for public health policy.
method: The authors develop a stochastic model on assortative networks and analyze the probability of disease extinction under temporary lockdowns.
result: Temporary lockdowns can significantly increase the extinction probability, with the effect depending on network assortativity and lockdown timing.
conclusion: Lockdowns are effective in reducing disease extinction risk, but their impact is modulated by network structure.

title: Dynamic Stabilization Of The Isolated Internal Defect In The Presence Of A Temporally Modulated Laser Prepulse
authors: Y. Z. Han, K. G. Zhao, Z. Y. Li, Y. X. Liu, C. Xue, J. W. Li, Z. Chen, J. Q. Dong, J. F. Wu, L. F. Wang, And W. Y. Zhang
abstract:

Hydrodynamic instabilities seeded by isolated internal defects remain a critical performance-limiting factor in inertial confinement fusion experiments. Here we extend the concept of dynamic stabilization via temporally modulated laser pulses from the main drive [K. G. Zhao et al.,
tldr: This paper studies dynamic stabilization of hydrodynamic instabilities seeded by internal defects in inertial confinement fusion using temporally modulated laser prepulses.
motivation: Hydrodynamic instabilities from isolated internal defects limit performance in inertial confinement fusion experiments; the authors aim to extend dynamic stabilization via modulated laser pulses to mitigate these instabilities.
method: The authors extend the concept of dynamic stabilization using temporally modulated laser pulses from the main drive to the prepulse regime, analyzing the effect on isolated internal defects.
result: The study demonstrates that temporally modulated laser prepulses can dynamically stabilize isolated internal defects, reducing instability growth.
conclusion: Dynamic stabilization via modulated laser prepulses offers a potential approach to improve inertial confinement fusion performance by mitigating defect-seeded instabilities.

title: Self-propelled Droplet Dynamics On Superhydrophobic Surfaces Under Low-pressure Conditions
authors: Xiaonan Li, Jiayi Zhou, Haiyan Luo, Xueli Zheng, And Guo Chen

The self-removal of sessile droplets under low-pressure conditions is critical for extreme-environment surface engineering. [Phys. Rev. E 113, 065506] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of self-propelled droplets on superhydrophobic surfaces under low pressure, focusing on fluid mechanics and surface engineering.
motivation: Understanding droplet self-removal under low pressure is important for extreme-environment surface engineering applications.
method: High-speed photography and quantitative analysis were used to observe ethylene glycol-water solution droplets on irregular micro-nanostructured superhydrophobic surfaces.
result: The study reveals unique droplet dynamics under low-pressure conditions, including self-propulsion and removal mechanisms.
conclusion: The findings provide insights for designing surfaces that can self-clean or remove droplets in low-pressure environments.

title: Plume Stretching In The Trapped Region Of A Reoriented Potential Mixer
authors: Roseanna M. Neupauer, James D. Meiss, And Tomás G. Dabove
abstract:

The reoriented potential mixer (RPM) can enhance mixing and reaction during in situ remediation of contaminated groundwater, in which a chemical or biological amendment is introduced into a contaminant plume to react with and degrade the contaminant. [Phys. Rev. E 113, 065108] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fluid mixing in a reoriented potential mixer for groundwater remediation, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Enhance in situ remediation of contaminated groundwater by improving mixing of chemical or biological amendments with contaminants.
method: Analyzes plume stretching in the trapped region of a reoriented potential mixer using dipole flow and reorientation steps.
result: Characterizes stretching dynamics and mixing efficiency in the trapped region.
conclusion: The reoriented potential mixer can improve mixing, but the paper is purely classical fluid dynamics.

title: Redirecting Countermoving Swarms Through Collision
authors: Jason Hindes, Chinthan B. Prasad, Loy Mcguire, And Ira B. Schwartz
abstract:
Author(s): Jason Hindes, Chinthan B. Prasad, Loy McGuire, and Ira B. Schwartz

Multiswarm systems, where two or more swarms of mobile agents occupy the same region of space with different parameters and goals, occur in a variety of biological, engineering, and defense applications. Composites of multiple swarms can produce hybrid spatiotemporal patterns, which compared to sing…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023351] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of multiple swarms of mobile agents that collide and redirect each other, focusing on pattern formation and control.
motivation: Understanding and controlling the behavior of multiple interacting swarms is important for biological, engineering, and defense applications.
method: The authors develop a model for countermoving swarms and analyze their collision dynamics using numerical simulations and theoretical analysis.
result: They identify conditions under which swarms can be redirected through collisions, leading to hybrid spatiotemporal patterns.
conclusion: Collision-based redirection is a viable mechanism for controlling multiswarm systems without centralized coordination.

title: Parametric Resonance, Chaos, And Spatial Structure In The Lotka-Volterra Model

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023352] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies parametric resonance and chaos in the Lotka-Volterra predator-prey model with periodic carrying capacity.
motivation: Understanding how seasonal variations affect predator-prey dynamics and spatial pattern formation.
method: Analyzes ordinary differential equations and partial differential equations with periodic forcing, using numerical simulations and bifurcation analysis.
result: Identifies parametric resonance and chaotic behavior, and shows how spatial structure emerges from the temporal forcing.

title: Dispersed-phase Forcing Reorganizes Lagrangian Intermittency In Turbulence
authors: Zecai Zhou, Hendrik Hessenkemper, Andrew D. Bragg, And Tian Ma

motivation: Understanding how dispersed particles affect extreme velocity fluctuations in turbulence is important for multiphase flow modeling.
method: High-resolution 3D Lagrangian particle tracking experiments were conducted in turbulent flows with and without dispersed phase forcing.
result: Dispersed-phase forcing reorganizes Lagrangian intermittency, altering the scaling of velocity increment statistics.
